title: Cortical population codes for embedding sensory inputs into the prior context
source: Science Advances
abstract: According to theories of the brain as a predictive network, perceptual decisions result from integrating incoming sensory inputs with prior experience. A neuronal population implementing this form of computation must not only retain information about past events but also combine this information with current sensory evidence. To examine how this integration occurs, we recorded extracellular activity from both primary sensory cortex and a target frontal region in rats performing stimulus categorization. Psychophysical analysis showed that judgments were history dependent. Sensory cortex represented the current stimulus largely independently of prior stimuli and failed to account for the history dependence seen in behavior. In contrast, frontal cortex embedded current input within a representation of prior sensory information, with the two variables aligned along partially overlapping coding dimensions. This mechanism predicted choice bias in the behavioral data and involved a disproportionate contribution from putative fast-spiking units. These findings suggest distinct contributions of sensory and frontal cortical regions to predictive processing and point to frontal cortex as a potential site where sensory history may be integrated with incoming evidence to influence perceptual decisions.

title: Ni‐Embedded Carbon Fibers Enable Synergistic Confinement and Catalytic Conversion of Iodine Species for Zn–I 2 Batteries
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Due to their affordability, safety and high capacity, aqueous Zn–I 2 batteries show great potential for large‐scale energy storage. Nevertheless, the dissolution of I 3 − intermediates leads to the iodine shuttle effect, which results in irreversible capacity loss and poor cyclability, thus hindering practical deployment. Here, we propose a synergistic strategy combining hierarchical pore confinement with catalytic iodine conversion to suppress the shuttle effect. A self‐standing cathode is synthesized, consisting of Ni nanoparticle‐embedded carbon nanoboxes enclosed within carbon macroporous fibers (Ni@CNBs‐CMFs). The abundant hierarchical porous structure provides physical confinement for iodine species, while Ni nanoparticles serve as active centers to accelerate iodine conversion via d–p orbital interactions. Benefiting from the synergistic enhancement in iodine accommodation and reaction kinetics, the self‐standing Ni@CNBs‐CMFs iodine cathode delivers a cycle life of 16 000 cycles with a capacity of 144.5 mAh g −1 and maintains a Coulombic efficiency of 90.0% after a 168‐h resting period. Moreover, the cathode also achieves a capacity of 382.8 mAh g −1 at a current of 2 A g −1 via the I − /I 0 /I + redox pathway.

title: Cross-domain encoding models reveal shared and domain-specific neural representations across language and mathematics
source: Science Advances
abstract: Whether language and mathematics rely on shared or distinct neural representations remains unresolved in cognitive neuroscience. Here, we combined latent features from a large language model with functional magnetic resonance imaging encoding models to test cross-domain generalization in 32 participants performing sentence comprehension and calculation tasks. Cross-domain prediction identified cortical regions showing partially shared representations, most consistently in the left area 55b, while control analyses suggested that these effects could not be fully explained by low-level visual or task-general factors. Domain-specificity contrasts revealed stronger language-related prediction in the left superior temporal sulcus and angular gyrus and math-related prediction in the left precentral sulcus and bilateral intraparietal sulci. Model-weight analyses revealed distinct weight profiles associated with shared and domain-specific prediction patterns. Cross-domain regions also exhibited task-dependent functional coupling with language- and math-related networks. Together, these findings suggest that language and mathematics involve partially shared neural representations alongside domain-specific cortical organization, helping reconcile previous contrasting views on their neural basis.

title: Spatially multiplexed microneedle biosensors for low-abundance protein biomarker monitoring in dermal interstitial fluid
source: Science Advances
abstract: Microneedle (MN) biosensors offer a minimally invasive approach for molecular analysis of interstitial fluid (ISF), but multiplexed detection of low-abundance protein biomarkers remains limited by poor spatial functionalization and analytical sensitivity. Here, we introduce a high-resolution transfer-printing strategy that functionalizes individual MNs with distinct biorecognition elements on a single patch, enabling simultaneous capture and on-needle analysis of multiple protein biomarkers. Combined with plasmonic-enhanced ultrabright fluorescent nanolabels, the platform enables sensitive multiplexed quantification of low-abundance immune and kidney function biomarkers in mouse models and human subjects. ISF biomarker concentrations showed strong correlations with corresponding plasma levels, supporting the physiological relevance of MN-based measurements. The MN patch enabled painless, blood-free sampling with rapid skin recovery and no irritation. This scalable platform provides a versatile approach for minimally invasive biomarker profiling and may facilitate frequent disease monitoring and timely clinical decision-making.

title: Non-invasive, high-precision, and independently controllable neuromodulation via optimized multiple temporal interference stimulation
source: Science Advances
abstract: Non-invasive neuromodulation is an important approach in clinical and translational neuroscience, yet existing techniques remain limited in precisely and flexibly targeting spatially distributed brain regions. Temporal interference stimulation (TIS) enabled non-invasive selective targeting; however, conventional implementations lack sufficient spatial focality, steerability, and scalability for network-level modulation. Here, we introduce optimized multiple temporal interference stimulation (omTIS), a computationally optimized framework that achieves high spatial focality, flexible steerability, and scalable control for distributed neuromodulation. Using a multi-electrode architecture, finite element analysis (FEA)–based optimization, and carefully selected multiple carrier frequencies, omTIS generates focal interference envelopes that can be positioned across multiple brain targets, enabling simultaneous and independently controllable multi-focal stimulation with minimal mutual interference. Across simulations, tissue-mimicking phantom experiments, and in vivo mouse studies, omTIS outperformed conventional TIS in spatial selectivity, steering flexibility, and cross-talk-free multi-focal modulation. These results establish omTIS as a scalable platform for precise, non-invasive control of distributed brain networks.

title: An integrative single-cell long noncoding RNA atlas reveals regulatory programs in the pan-cancer tumor microenvironment
source: Science Advances
abstract: Long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) have been shown as critical components in cancer genomics, yet their functionality and regulation remain elusive. Here, we present an integrative lncRNA atlas covering more than 370,000 cells from 18 cancer types. In addition to multiple lineage- and cellular state transition–associated lncRNAs, we identify a set of lncRNAs that are embedded within cell type–specific regulons, suggesting associations between lncRNA expression and cell type–enriched transcriptional programs. By integrating CRISPR-based functional genomic screens and clinical data, we further prioritize not only CRISPR-supported candidate lncRNAs linked to tumor cell fitness and immune cell state features but also specific lncRNA signatures correlated with patient survival and immunotherapy response.

title: Auditory cortical coding of spectrotemporal modulations is sufficient to support perceptual categorization of speech and music
source: Science Advances
abstract: Auditory processing is typically described as hierarchical, culminating in neural representation of abstract categories. However, it remains unclear whether category-selective responses in auditory cortex require representational mechanisms beyond the coding of acoustic features or whether the acoustic representations already available in the auditory cortex are sufficient to account for categorization. Here, we test whether cortical coding of spectrotemporal modulation (STM) features is sufficient to support speech-music categorization by combining human intracranial recordings with continuous behavioral judgments of a naturalistic soundtrack in which speech and music occur both separately and simultaneously. We show that temporal and spectral modulation patterns largely characterize speech and music, respectively, and that cortical auditory regions robustly track these features over time, with distinct oscillatory frequency bands preferentially encoding temporal and spectral modulations. Critically, cortical representations of STMs predicted perceptual categorical judgments gathered in an independent sample. Last, speech- and music-related STM representations showed stronger tracking of category-specific acoustical features in left versus right cortical auditory regions, respectively. These findings indicate that the efficient neural coding of acoustical features provides a sufficient basis for the categorical distinction between speech and music and that the temporal and spectral components of this representation are implemented through distinct oscillatory mechanisms.

title: Ribosome-associated vesicles promote activity-dependent local translation in neurons
source: Science Advances
abstract: Local protein synthesis in axons and dendrites underpins synaptic plasticity. However, the composition of the protein synthesis machinery in distal neuronal processes and the mechanisms for its deployment to local translation sites remain unclear. Here, we employed multi-scale imaging that combines cryo-electron tomography, volume electron microscopy, and live-cell imaging to identify endoplasmic reticulum-derived KDEL-positive vesicles, a subset of which are decorated with ribosomes (Ribosome-Associated Vesicles, RAVs) in neurites. We demonstrate that neuronal stimulation triggers compartment-specific responses: dendrites accumulate stationary KDEL-positive vesicles at sites of enhanced translation, while axons accelerate vesicle transport. cLTP stimulation additionally increases the proportion of KDEL-positive vesicles that carry ribosomes, expanding the local RAV pool. Real-time imaging of translation at single mRNA resolution reveals that RAV-associated translation sites exhibit ∼30% greater nascent-peptide signal amplitude compared to periods without RAV association, indicating that RAVs boost local translation output. These findings establish RAVs as specialized platforms that integrate activity-dependent signals with local protein synthesis, providing a mechanistic framework for understanding how neurons achieve precise spatiotemporal control of translation.

title: Interfacial Amorphous Lithium Polysulfide Reservoir Design Enables High‐Power and Energy‐Dense All‐Solid‐State Li─S Battery
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT All‐solid‐state Li─S batteries (ASSLSBs) promise ultrahigh energy density and safety but suffer from sluggish charge transfer kinetics at the triple‐phase (sulfur, carbon, and solid electrolyte) interface. Herein, we construct an amorphous lithium reservoir (ALR) made of short‐chained lithium polysulfides on sulfur particles to boost the interfacial sulfur redox kinetics and stability, thereby enabling high‐power and energy‐dense performance in ASSLSBs. Spectroscopic analyses (Raman, XPS, NMR, XAFS) reveal the ALR features a disordered Li─S bonding behavior, which store and anchor Li + ions surrounding the sulfur particles, creating rapid Li + conduction pathways and ensuring continuous Li + supply for accelerated S/Li 2 S conversion. Consequently, the ASSLSBs exhibit superior rate capability, achieving a high reversible capacity of 1115 mAh g −1 at 1C and 732.8 mAh g −1 at 2C, respectively, as well as excellent cycling stability with an ultralow capacity decay rate of 0.049% per cycle after 1000 cycles at 1C. Moreover, the ALR design also demonstrate a high practical capacity of 12.8 mAh cm −2 under high sulfur loading of 10 mg cm −2 , suggesting its promise to resolve the longstanding kinetics issue and paves a practical path for future high‐energy‐density ASSLSBs.

title: Phylogeny explains differences in the crystal structures and chemistry of vertebrate tooth enamel and enameloid
source: Science Advances
abstract:
A phylogenetically diverse suite of modern tooth enamel/enameloid bioapatite from fishes, mammals, and reptiles from 22 species were chemically and structurally analyzed to establish whether crystal structure and chemistry are phylogenetically correlated. Rietveld refinement analysis of x-ray diffraction data suggests variable crystallographic parameters across vertebrates. Coupled chemical data show correlations between the
                    a
                    -axis of bioapatite and the proportions of sodium substitution for calcium, the introduction of vacancies, and carbonate substituting for phosphate (B-type substitution) or channel anions (A-type substitution). Principal component analysis of all variables suggests that
                    a
                    -axis lengths are highly influenced by the introduction of carbonate in both crystallographic sites. Phylogenetic variations in chemistry and structure of enamel/enameloid crystals show how biomineralization processes have changed through evolutionary time with implications for variation in biomineralization processes across vertebrate lineages. The predominant controls on tooth enamel/enameloid crystal structure are phylogeny rather than primary diet or habitat. Crystal structure variations also influence material properties across organisms, which may control how teeth are fossilized.

title: Dynein-dependent positioning of multiple organelles regulates adaptive gene expression during oxidative stress
source: Science Advances
abstract: Cells respond to environmental insults through well-characterized changes to their transcriptome and proteome. The contribution that reorganization of intracellular architecture makes to the adaptive stress response is much less understood. Here, we reveal a conserved spatial response to oxidative stress in which the microtubule motor dynein enhances perinuclear clustering of multiple membrane-bound organelles. These events are triggered by reactive oxygen species and protein kinase C and occur without increased association of dynein with its activator dynactin, pointing to a noncanonical mechanism for stimulating retrograde transport. Using a chemically inducible system for dispersing individual organelles, we show that perinuclear localization of multiple compartments potentiates oxidative stress–induced gene expression, with distinct genes depending on inputs from either combinations of organelles or individual compartments. Together, these findings implicate positioning of multiple membrane-bound compartments in gene expression regulation and identify coordinated organelle trafficking by dynein as an additional regulatory layer in the cellular stress response.

title: Nonpolar Micro‐Environment‐Induced Solvation Field Engineering Enables 600 Wh Kg −1 High‐Voltage Lithium Metal Pouch Cells
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Conventional‐carbonate electrolytes cannot simultaneously stabilize lithium metal interfaces and sustain fast ion transport. Existing designs mitigate interfacial degradation but compromise ion transport, low‐temperature fluidity, or salt dissociation. Herein, we propose a solvation field engineering strategy via a nonpolar micro‐environment‐induced electrolyte (NME) that overcomes this trade‐off at conventional salt concentration. Propyl propionate serves as an amphiphilic inducer: its carbonyl oxygen coordinates Li + , while its propyl chain extends outward to create a Li + ‐centered nonpolar micro‐environment that engineers the local solvation field by attenuating dielectric shielding and strengthening Li + –PF 6 − interactions, thereby driving a contact‐ion‐pair‐dominated solvation structure. Fluoroethylene carbonate and 2,2,2‐trifluoroethyl methyl carbonate ensure sufficient salt dissociation and high‐voltage oxidative stability. The resulting electrolyte combines rapid ion transport with a robust LiF/LiPO 2 F 2 interphase, suppressing electrolyte decomposition and enabling uniform Li plating/stripping. Consequently, a 4.2 Ah Li||LiNi 0.88 Co 0.07 Mn 0.05 O 2 pouch cell (∼425 Wh kg −1 ) retains 87.7% capacity after 200 cycles, and a 23.5 Ah Li||LiNi 0.95 Co 0.02 Mn 0.03 O 2 pouch cell achieves 604 Wh kg −1 . The strategy is further applicable to graphite‐based batteries, enabling a 3.6 Ah Graphite||LiNi 0.5 Co 0.2 Mn 0.3 O 2 pouch cell to deliver 81.5% retention after 100 cycles at −20°C. NME offers a novel principle to regulate solvation and interfacial stability for high‐energy batteries.

title: Strain‐Inversion Strategy Enables MOCVD Growth of 53 µm Ultra‐Thick, Stress‐Free, Buffer‐Free III‐Nitride Heteroepitaxial Films
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT As the semiconductor industry increasingly pivots toward “More than Moore” and “More Moore” paradigms, heterogeneous integration has emerged as a pivotal strategy for achieving system‐level performance breakthroughs. However, residual stress inherent to the integration of dissimilar materials represents a critical bottleneck, directly threatening the integrity and reliability of these advanced systems. Heteroepitaxy, as a representative example, is inherently constrained by stress accumulation, which limits epilayer thickness, increases threading dislocation density (TDD), and degrades device reliability. Here, we present a strain‐inversion strategy that effectively transfers misfit‐induced stress from the epilayer into the substrate stack. Through co‐designed theoretical modeling and experimental validation, we introduce 4H‐SiC/SiO 2 /polycrystalline‐ceramic‐AlN integrated substrates, and demonstrate metalorganic chemical vapor deposition (MOCVD) growth of 53‐µm‐thick, stress‐free heteroepitaxial GaN films. The films exhibit outstanding structural quality, with full‐width‐at‐half‐maximum (FWHM) values of x‐ray rocking curve of 83 and 119 arcsec for the (002) and (102) planes, respectively, and a TDD of 5 × 10 7 cm −2 . These results not only set a new thickness record for MOCVD‐grown heteroepitaxial GaN but also achieve crystal quality comparable to state‐of‐the‐art benchmarks. Our approach establishes strain‐inverted epitaxy as a highly promising platform for high‐performance nitride devices and paves the way for producing low‐cost and strain‐free GaN and AlN substrates.

title: The interferon-gamma response pathway is a targetable driver of FSHD muscular dystrophy progression
source: Science Advances
abstract: Facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy (FSHD) is a leading neuromuscular disorder caused by the aberrant expression of the transcription factor double homeobox 4 (DUX4) in skeletal muscle. While DUX4 is normally restricted to early embryonic development, its reactivation in FSHD triggers chronic inflammation and progressive muscle degeneration. However, the precise molecular links between DUX4 and persistent immune activation remain poorly understood. Here, we show that DUX4 induces a viral mimicry-like pathway that is fundamentally uncoupled from canonical type I interferon (IFN) activation. Instead, DUX4 establishes a non-canonical innate immune state dominated by IFN-γ signaling, providing a mechanistic explanation for the non-resolving inflammation characteristic of the disease. We demonstrate that while IFN-γ treatment alone is sufficient to recapitulate key DUX4 pathogenic effects, its inhibition rescues muscle inflammation and halts disease progression in FSHD models. These findings define a “skewed viral mimicry” process driven by a disease-specific transcription factor and identify IFN-γ as a primary therapeutic target for tissue-informed immunomodulation in muscular dystrophy.

title: Chromatin loci move coherently due to spatially correlated fluctuations
source: Science Advances
abstract:
From enhancer-promoter communication to DNA repair, essential genome functions require chromosomal loci to encounter each other. While live-cell imaging enables direct measurement of pairwise locus dynamics, a quantitative framework for interpreting them is lacking. Here, using imaging data from
                    Drosophila
                    embryos and mouse stem cells, we show that nearby loci diffuse relative to each other far more slowly than expected from polymer chain–mediated effects. We propose that this slowdown is caused by spatially correlated fluctuations (SCFs) which couple loci via the nucleoplasm. We theoretically predict how these fluctuations scale with space, time, and genomic separation and confirm these predictions using live-cell imaging. Using polymer simulations, we demonstrate that while spatially correlated equilibrium noise fails to reproduce the observed SCF scalings, coupling the polymer to actively driven flows recapitulates the experimental statistics. Consistently, we experimentally show that SCFs couple locus motion across chromosomes and that their magnitude depends on adenosine 5′-triphosphate (ATP)–dependent activity and cohesin-mediated loop extrusion. By reducing encounter frequencies while prolonging encounter durations, SCFs generate a trade-off with direct implications for gene regulation. Our results provide a quantitative framework for chromatin dynamics, revealing how nuclear activity governs chromatin encounters in living cells.

title: Machine-learning-driven identification of cooperative descriptors for polysulfide conversion on spinel oxides
source: Science Advances
abstract:
Spinel oxides have emerged as promising catalysts for polysulfide conversion, yet a comprehensive design strategy that elucidates the underlying structure–property relationship across diverse spinel oxides remains elusive. The complex multistep conversion processes make single descriptors insufficient to capture the full catalytic behavior, whereas identifying cooperative descriptors introduces additional complexity that challenges manual analysis. Here, we employ a machine-learning–assisted approach to uncover universal cooperative descriptors and accelerate the discovery of high-performance spinel catalysts. We reveal that the intrinsic polysulfide conversion efficiency of spinel oxides is cooperatively governed by two structural features. Further screening of promising catalysts is conducted using the extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) algorithm, achieving rapid and accurate prediction of these features on spinel oxides. The model identifies Fe
                    2
                    CoO
                    4
                    and Fe
                    2
                    NiO
                    4
                    as superior catalysts, which are experimentally validated to exhibit excellent performance. This work provides deep mechanistic insights and a powerful data-driven framework for the rational design of spinel catalysts, with potential extension to other applications.

title: Tunable spectral correlations of highly multimode visible light via broadband quantum frequency conversion
source: Science Advances
abstract: Multimode squeezed states of light are a resource for achieving quantum advantage in computing and sensing, where spatial or temporal modes have been the experimental norm. In our experiments, we generated highly frequency-multimode infrared quantum light and showed how adiabatic frequency conversion can be used to convert the quantum state to visible wavelengths while concurrently manipulating the joint spectrum by realizing a configurable many-port frequency-domain beamsplitter unitary transformation. We report near-unity efficiency quantum frequency conversion over a bandwidth >45 terahertz, which allowed us to measure the state with an electron-multiplying CCD (EMCCD) camera-based spectrometer, at noncryogenic temperatures. The parametric amplification and conversion of >400 frequency modes yielded an overall mean of ∼700 visible photons per shot and photon statistics consistent with squeezing. Our work shows how many-mode quantum states of light can be generated, manipulated, and measured with efficient use of hardware resources, motivating the use of frequency encoding in quantum optics.

title: Hydrogen radical-participating spatiotemporal sequential therapy via hypoxia aggravation for hypoxia-amplified immunotherapy
source: Science Advances
abstract: The hypoxic characteristics of the tumor microenvironment and endogenous antioxidant defenses compromise the efficacy of oxygen-consuming oxidative therapy, positioning oxygen-free reductive stress as a new paradigm in tumor treatment. Nevertheless, the immunosuppressive characteristics of hypoxia and reductive stress pose significant challenges for advancing reductive stress-induced immunotherapy. Here, we constructed a hydrogen radical (H•) generator synergistically activated by near-infrared light and thiols, and first elucidated that photocatalytic H•-mediated reductive stress can elicit a robust antitumor immune response via the H•-featured mechanism. Nanoplatform HA@UFTL was engineered using lactate oxidase as an ideal H• partner, with the synergistic contribution enabling cross-amplified antitumor immunotherapy. The H•-participating spatiotemporal sequential strategy highlights a triple spatiotemporal sequential cascade, including dual sequential hypoxia exacerbation, sequential oxidative-reductive stress, and sequential organelle damage. By aggravating rather than alleviating hypoxia, HA@UFTL overcomes immunosuppression induced by hypoxia and reductive stress with H• as a universal building block, providing new insights for hypoxia-based immunotherapy.

title: Electronic Polarization in Covalent Organic Frameworks With Alternating Hetero‐Linkages for High‐Performance H 2 O 2 Photosynthesis
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) hold considerable promise for photocatalytic H 2 O 2 production, yet achieving efficient carrier separation and transport to achieve excellent performance remains a significantly challenge. Herein, we constructed a library of polarized COFs featuring alternating hetero‐linkage C═N and C─N linkages, which establish continuous local charge gradients at molecular level. Remarkably, driven by the localized electronic polarization microenvironment, the optimal material (TPPZ‐BC) showed a photocatalytic H 2 O 2 production rate as high as 11.06 mmol g −1 h −1 , outperforming most reported COF‐based photocatalysts. Mechanistic studies revealed that the spatial alternation of electron‐withdrawing C═N and electron‐donating C─N linkages induced a strong intramolecular charge polarization. This effect significantly modulates the surface electrostatic potential distribution, increasing the proportion of highly positive regions and thereby enhancing the adsorption and activation of oxygen molecules. Moreover, this structural design breaks molecular symmetry and promotes the synergistic alignment of local dipoles, generating a robust intrinsic electric field. This work provides a new strategy for the development of crystalline porous photocatalysts toward highly efficient photosynthesis.

title: Bionic skin with hair follicle regeneration capability from acoustic fluids-mediated 3D printing
source: Science Advances
abstract: Tissue engineering holds substantial potential for constructing normal skin with appendages such as hair follicles, directly restoring skin’s complete physiological functions. The current challenge lies in recreating biomimetic hair follicle organs with high-level cell density and architecture. Here, we developed an acoustofluidic-assisted 3D bioprinting platform to fabricate bionic skins with efficient hair follicle regeneration capability. Pre-formed hair follicle germs, derived from co-cultured epidermal and dermal mesenchymal stem cells, were encapsulated within a hydrogel bioink. Controlled acoustic fields generated flow vortices that directed cell migration and promoted organized cellular assembly from initially disordered states. Guided cell aggregates were then patterned through bioprinting to construct a grid-structured bionic skin. This architecture provided stable 3D support while maintaining high porosity, enabling efficient gas exchange. The printed bionic skin exhibited well-organized spatial cell distribution, high cellular viability, and promising differentiation potential. Further in vivo experiments demonstrated the efficiency of the bionic skin in accelerating mature hair regeneration, showing promise for clinical alopecia treatment.

title: Synergistic Salt‐Bridge and Hydrophobic Interaction‐Driven Supramolecular Adhesives Enable Ultrastrong Dry/Underwater Bonding and Broad Harsh‐Condition Adaptability: Polyelectrolyte‐Templated Multi‐Promoting Effects
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Developing advanced amphibious adhesives that perform well in both dry and underwater environments is critical yet challenging for unlocking diverse underwater applications. Here, we propose a general polyelectrolyte‐templated multi‐regulation strategy to establish a new cooperative salt‐bridge/hydrophobic interaction‐driven supramolecular adhesive that overcomes long‐standing water‐adhesive conflicts and attains rapid yet ultrastrong dry/underwater adhesion with broad harsh‐environment adaptability. By engineering branched‐polycationic electrolytes with dense interaction sites as versatile templates, this strategy exerts multi‐promoting effects of polyelectrolytes on dense salt‐bridge formation, precursor wetting and ultrafast solvent‐free curing, which, in cooperation with flexible hydrophobic moieties, optimizes cohesion/interfacial adhesion, balances flexibility‐rigidity and inhibits water‐erosion and interface hydration within cured network. Thus, the optimized b‐PAE achieves ultrahigh dry and underwater bonding strengths up to 20.9 and 13.2 MPa on safety glass within 10 s—a performance integration rarely reported in previous adhesives. It further demonstrates robust adhesion in harsh underwater conditions (seawater, acidic, alkaline solutions), excellent cryogenic tolerance (−196°C) and versatile utility including oil tank leakage repair and rapid pipeline sealing. Mechanistic studies reveal that the synergy of salt‐bridge and hydrophobic interactions governs amphibious adhesion. This universal approach, applicable to various hydrophobic moieties, paves the way for developing diverse amphibious adhesives to advance underwater technologies.

title: Postimpact evolution of the South Pole–Aitken basin revealed by Chang’e-4 and Chang’e-6
source: Science Advances
abstract: South Pole–Aitken (SPA) basin has recorded complex geological histories of the Moon. It is a critical region for solving lunar fundamental questions but remained unexplored until the Chang’e-4 and Chang’e-6 missions of China. Their in situ measurements and the Chang’e-6 samples provided the first ground truth for the SPA evolution. On the basis of these constraints, we found that the SPA impact occurred ∼4.34 billion years ago, generating a thick melt sheet that differentiated to form moderately magnesium (Mg)–rich norites. They are exposed at the SPA central peaks and currently investigated by the Chang’e-4 mission in Von Kármán crater, transported by the Finsen impact to the site. Highly Mg-rich materials were found within SPA, likely products of Mg-suite magmatism, including those exposed at the Apollo western peak ring. They were initially excavated by the Apollo impact at ∼4.2 billion years ago and delivered to the Chang’e-6 site by the Chaffee S impact. A series of other events occurred in the SPA basin subsequently (e.g., the Orientale impact ∼3.87 billion years ago); all of them shaped the architecture of the Moon’s largest impact basin.

title: Transition-Metal-Mediated Discharge Intermediates Set Anionic-Redox Potentials and Voltage Hysteresis in Li-Rich Cathodes
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Voltage hysteresis arising from anionic redox reactions remains a central bottleneck for lithium-rich cathodes. While ligand-to-metal charge transfer (LMCT) has been invoked to describe the charging pathway, its proposed reverse counterpart, metal-to-ligand charge transfer (MLCT), remains experimentally unresolved during discharge. Here, using cation-disordered rock-salt Li2Ni0.33Ta0.66O3 (LNTO) as a model system, we combine electrochemical relaxation analysis with synchrotron-based spectroscopy to identify, for the first time, a metastable reduction intermediate characterized by Ni(2-δ)+/(O–O)n− during discharge, thereby providing direct experimental validation for the MLCT framework. The discovery of this metastable intermediate demonstrates that discharge proceeds through a two-step electrochemical–chemical pathway, wherein the spontaneous relaxation evolution of the metastable intermediate drives free-energy dissipation and voltage hysteresis. Guided by this picture, Ru substitution was introduced to modulate the cation–anion electronic structure, enabling Ru 4d–O 2p hybridization to generate persistent low-energy hole states that lower the energy of the metastable discharge intermediate and shift O–O dimer reduction to higher potentials. We further show that the discharge intermediate serves as the energetic link through which transition-metal electronic structure governs the effective anionic-redox potential. This work provides a discharge-side thermodynamic framework for understanding and mitigating voltage hysteresis in Li-rich anionic-redox cathodes.

title: In vivo screening reveals new regulators of natural killer cell development and functional response to acute cytomegalovirus infection
source: Science Advances
abstract: Natural killer (NK) cells are critical innate immune effectors in antiviral and antitumor responses. However, the factors governing NK cell development and function remain incompletely understood. To address this, we adopted an in vivo screening approach, generating a panel of mice deficient in genes differentially expressed across NK cell maturation stages or following viral infection. We performed a combinational screen comprising baseline immunophenotyping and mouse cytomegalovirus (MCMV) challenge. We identified regulators of NK cell development, including transcriptional regulators and proteins with putative trafficking functions. MCMV challenge studies additionally identified proteins that affected antiviral immunity independently of NK cell phenotypes, including a previously undescribed regulator of NK cell degranulation, synaptotagmin-like protein 3. Identified genes exhibited a trend toward reduced tolerance to loss of function in large-scale human sequencing studies and evidence for reduced NK cell numbers in a cohort of patients with immunodeficiency. Together, these findings provide a resource of NK-expressed genes important for NK cell maturation and function, with relevance to human health.

title: USP8 inhibition suppresses prostate tumorigenesis via promoting RICTOR degradation to inhibit mTORC2 signaling
source: Science Advances
abstract:
RICTOR plays an essential role in regulating mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 2 (mTORC2) kinase activity, but it remains largely elusive how RICTOR is aberrantly activated in human prostate cancer (PrCa). Here, we identify RICTOR as a substrate of Cullin 3–based ubiquitin ligase adaptor SPOP, an important tumor suppressor in PrCa. SPOP deficiency or cancer-derived
                    SPOP
                    mutations disrupt SPOP-mediated degradation of RICTOR, thereby promoting PrCa progression. Furthermore, we identify USP8 as its upstream deubiquitinase, and inhibition of USP8 specifically suppresses RICTOR/mTORC2 activity without affecting mTORC1. As such, the USP8 inhibitor induces RICTOR degradation concomitant with marked tumor suppression in vivo. Hence, these findings reveal an SPOP-USP8-RICTOR regulatory circuit that underlies PrCa tumorigenesis and provides a rationale for targeting RICTOR via USP8 inhibition as a therapeutic strategy for patients with PrCa.

title: Nanoparticle-enabled gene delivery for pediatric brain tumors
source: Science Advances
abstract: Pediatric brain tumors are the leading cause of disease-related death in children, yet effective treatment remains a major clinical challenge. These aggressive tumors have limited therapeutic options capable of crossing the blood-brain barrier (BBB) and frequently recur due to genetic or epigenetic alterations and treatment resistance. Gene therapy offers a promising strategy to address these limitations by modifying gene expression, correcting mutations, or introducing functional genes. Nanoparticle (NP) delivery systems facilitate this approach by protecting genetic cargo and enabling BBB penetration and tumor-specific uptake. This review summarizes current genetic engineering strategies and NP-based delivery systems for pediatric brain tumors, including their design principles and delivery mechanisms, highlights key therapeutic approaches under preclinical and clinical investigations, and discusses the major challenges and future directions in NP-mediated gene therapy for pediatric neuro-oncology. By critically evaluating these developments, we aim to underscore the transformative potential of NP-mediated gene therapies in reshaping treatment paradigms and improving outcomes and quality of life for children.

title: Globally antiaromatic anthracene–porphyrin nanobelts
source: Nature Chemistry
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Conjugated molecular belts attract increasing attention because of the unusual electronic and magnetic behaviour arising from their radially oriented
                    p
                    orbitals. A π-conjugated molecular belt is expected to behave like a quantum ring, showing global aromatic or antiaromatic ring currents, but in most hydrocarbon benzenoid belts, localized Clar sextets preclude the emergence of global ring currents. Here we report the synthesis of anthracene-bridged porphyrin nanobelts that sustain global antiaromatic ring currents in the neutral state. Macrocyclization was achieved by nickel(0)-mediated Yamamoto coupling. Scholl oxidation with DDQ/TfOH, promoted by electron-donating methoxy substituents, yielded the strained triple-stranded nanobelts. These hybrid nanobelts show global antiaromaticity, with Hückel circuits of 72, 96 or 120 π electrons, as revealed by
                    1
                    H NMR spectroscopy and corroborated by computational analysis. This work establishes a platform for synthesizing other heterocyclic nanobelts, in cases where the corresponding hydrocarbon nanobelt is not yet synthetically accessible.

title: Symmetry-Breaking Charge Localization Controls Radiationless Decay in a Multibranched Charge-Transfer State
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Symmetry breaking in multibranched charge-transfer (CT) excited states is generally viewed as a mechanism for excited-state localization, yet how such localization controls the subsequent fate of the excitation remains poorly understood. Here, we show that environmental stabilization of a symmetry-broken CT state can fundamentally reshape radiationless decay in a bent donor–acceptor–donor chromophore. Increasing solvent stabilization drives rapid reorganization toward a lower-energy CT configuration, collapsing the singlet lifetime from 1.98 ns in toluene to 9.2 ps in acetonitrile while increasing the effective nonradiative rate (knr) from 2.14 × 108 to >1.11 × 1011 s–1. Femtosecond transient absorption establishes that formation of the stabilized CT configuration precedes terminal population loss, while triplet accumulation observed in nonpolar media disappears as singlet depletion becomes ultrafast. Controlled toluene–acetonitrile mixtures further reveal that the nonradiative rate does not obey a single invariant energy-gap dependence: distinct energy-gap-law regimes emerge as the CT state is progressively stabilized, followed by a strongly reorganized regime in which knr continues to accelerate despite little additional change in the energy gap. Independently, the changing relationship between emission spectral variance and Stokes shift shows that the nuclear reorganization of the relaxed CT ensemble also changes with stabilization. Together, these results support a solvent-dependent symmetry-breaking landscape in which progressive charge localization reshapes both the excited-state energy and the nuclear coordinates governing access to the ground state. Symmetry breaking therefore acts not simply as an electronic localization process, but as an environmental kinetic switch, converting a long-lived, emissive and triplet-forming CT state into a rapidly quenched excited state.

title: Accessing Alkyl Linkers for Macrocyclic Peptide Synthesis via Nickel-Mediated Doubly DeAminative Macrocyclization
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The rise of macrocyclic peptides as a therapeutic modality has exposed gaps in the synthetic chemistry toolbox available for drug discovery teams to rapidly explore diverse linkers for structural optimization. In contrast to the thioether linkers common in peptide leads identified from mRNA display, all-carbon linkers are desirable for imparting solubility and stability, but existing approaches suffer from limited amino acid diversity, incompatibility with solid-phase peptide synthesis (SPPS), stereochemical loss, multistep requirements, or restricted linker placement. We report a Doubly DeAminative Macrocyclization (D2AM) to install alkyl linkers via C(sp3)–C(sp3) bond formation. This method uses pyridinium monomers derived from commercial amino acids that are stable to SPPS for the seamless synthesis of complex macrocyclic and polycyclic peptides with conservation of stereochemistry. This deaminative method is anticipated to accelerate optimization of peptide macrocycle structure in drug discovery.

title: Concerted Ligand-to-Metal Charge Transfer Absorption and Localized Photoluminescence in an Fe(III) Photosensitizer
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract There is tremendous interest in the electronic structure of [FeIII(phtmeimb)2]+, the first iron complex to show room temperature photoluminescence (PL) with an excited-state lifetime sufficient for dynamic quenching in fluid solution. Two types of excited states are generated by light absorption, termed the Franck–Condon (FC) state and the thermally equilibrated excited state (THEXI) that is photoluminescent. Herein we report solvatochromic and electroabsorption studies to probe the electronic structure of these two states. The doublet ligand-to-metal-charge-transfer absorption was found to be mostly solvent independent while a notable solvatochromism in the PL spectra indicated the presence of an excited-state dipole in polar solvents (μ⃗ = 16 ± 10 D), best formulated as [FeII(phtmeimb•+)(phtmeimb)]+*. However, standard and higher-order electroabsorption spectra revealed concerted and equal charge transfer from the two tridentate ligands to the metal, giving rise to a significant polarizability change (Δα) without the generation of a dipole moment (Δμ⃗ = 0) best formulated as [FeII(phtmeimb+1/2)2]+*. The strong interligand coupling necessary for such concerted charge transfer is proposed to be mediated by a t2g orbital of the Fe(III) center. Taken together, these findings provide new insights into this famed photoluminescent open-shell iron complex relevant to the design of improved iron photosensitizers.

title: Electrothermal Mapping: A Methodology for Decoupling Redox, Protonation, and Denaturation Dynamics of Cytochrome c
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Differential scanning calorimetry, fluorometry, circular dichroism, and electrospray ionization mass spectrometry are routinely used to study thermal and chemical denaturation of proteins. However, these powerful methods monitor protein unfolding in bulk aqueous solutions but overlook interfacial environments, such as lipid membranes and confined crevices, where electrostatic and hydrophobic forces reshape protein conformational landscapes and dictate their function. Herein, we introduce an electrothermal methodology that uniquely probes protein conformational changes in a potential-modulated biomimetic environment. Electrochemistry at the Interface between Two Immiscible Electrolyte Solutions (ITIES) captures nonredox fingerprints of cytochrome c under heat stress, offering a unique perspective on protein behavior without relying on electron transfer reactions and revealing interfacial activity not evident in bulk solutions by conventional methods. Electrothermal mapping presents the protein thermal stability as a current–potential–temperature landscape, enabling direct comparison of the protein’s native and non-native conformational states driven by electrostatic and hydrophobic interactions. Ultimately, our work establishes a new paradigm for predicting protein behavior under heat stress at membrane-like interfaces, with far-reaching implications for biotechnology and medicine, including drug development, enzyme engineering, and protein expression, where protein stability and crevice accessibility are critical.

title: Spatiotemporally Decoupled Cascade Photocatalysis on Dual S-Scheme Heterostructure with Interfacial Polarization Fields and Proton Shuttle Channels
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Transient surface reaction dynamics govern artificial-photosynthesis-enabled multistep tandem biomass oxidation but are hindered by spatially intermingled reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation and temporally entangled elementary-step sequences. A spatial-engineering strategy for fabricating ZnS/Sv-chalcogenide/MoSe2 (Sv = sulfur vacancies, chalcogenide = ZnIn2S4, Zn0.5Cd0.5S, CdIn2S4) dual S-scheme heterostructure, with chalcogenide as the shared mediator between the ZnS/chalcogenide and chalcogenide/MoSe2 S-junctions, is developed by anchoring MoSe2 nanoparticles onto chalcogenide nanosheets epitaxially grown from ZnS hollow dodecahedral cages. These ternary-component nanoreactors integrate dual interfacial features, the interfacial localized polarization field and the interfacial proton shuttle channel, to orchestrate dynamic intelligent catalysis. Specifically, the interfacial localized polarization field drives spatially decoupled ROS generation (•OH, •O2–, •OOH) via the asymmetric charge distributions, enabling zone-specific ROS to undertake differentiated oxidation tasks. Interfacial proton shuttle channel drives temporally decoupled elementary-step sequences via the interfacial dynamic hydrogen-bonding networks, thereby liberating pH-dependent proton transfer through directed radical protonation (•O2– → •OOH). This synergy provides a proof of concept for neutral 5-hydroxymethylfurfural-to-2,5-furandicarboxylic acid (HMF-to-FDCA) conversion and demonstrates a fundamental research-to-practical-application capability. This work proposes a generalizable catalyst design paradigm integrating interfacial localized polarization fields and interfacial proton shuttle channels, offering innovative insights for guiding spatiotemporally decoupled multistep cascade catalysis.

title: Taming Metal–Electrolyte Interface via Two-Dimensional Organic Metal Chalcogenide Colloids for Anode-Free Sodium Metal Batteries
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Anode-free metal batteries are promising candidates for next-generation energy storage technologies, yet their application is severely limited by dendrite growth and rapid capacity decay induced by an unstable metal–electrolyte interface. Herein, we propose a “colloid electrolyte” strategy employing coordination polymer nanosheets as electrolyte additives for constructing anode-free sodium metal batteries (AFSMBs). Unlike conventional molecular additives or inert particle suspensions, these colloidal nanosheets provide spatially organized and continuously available interfacial reaction domains, thereby spatially regulating electrolyte component distribution and interfacial reactions. These nanosheets, composed of AgS layers uniformly decorated with fluorinated groups, undergo in situ decomposition at the metal–electrolyte interface. This process generates gradient distributions of Ag nanoparticles and NaF/Na2S species, which guide the spontaneous formation of a functionally graded solid electrolyte interphase (SEI). This hierarchical SEI enables dendrite-free Na deposition and imparts sustained interfacial protection during cycling. Consequently, high-cathode-loading AFSMBs achieve an ultralong lifespan (>1600 cycles), representing a 10-fold improvement over counterpart cells without the colloidal additive. Notably, 0.5-Ah-level anode-free pouch cells exhibit stable cycling for 500 cycles at 2 C. This work establishes coordination polymer colloids as a new class of electrolyte additives for advanced alkali metal batteries.

title: Aryl Palladium Acetates as Highly Active Species in Intermolecular Heck Reactions of Hindered Olefins
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Despite decades of development since the early 1970s, the intermolecular Heck reaction of hindered tri- and tetrasubstituted olefins with aryl halides has remained a challenge. Traditional approaches relied on rate-acceleration by directing groups or high reactivity of cationic arylpalladium species generated from triflates and diazonium salts. Herein, we report the first general and efficient Heck coupling between trisubstituted alkenes (and selected tetrasubstituted olefins) with aryl iodides and bromides. Our protocol employs simple PdCl2 or Pd(OAc)2 as precatalyst and needs no directing groups. It features an exceptionally broad substrate scope, accommodating diverse (hetero)aryl halides and both acyclic and cyclic olefins, and the reaction proceeds efficiently on a gram scale with remarkably low palladium loadings. The practical value of this method is highlighted by its application in concise synthesis of several pharmaceutically relevant motifs. Mechanistically, HRMS and DFT calculations revealed that phosphine-free complexes of arylpalladium acetates─either monomer [(Ar)Pd(OAc)] or its paddlewheel dimer with bridging acetates─serve as the key active species. These species exhibit minimal steric hindrance, a high partial positive charge, and high electrophilicity at the palladium center, synergistically facilitating the binding and rapid insertion of hindered alkenes.

title: Phototunable Solid–Liquid Interfacial Energy via Ion–Electron Coupling
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The solid–liquid interfacial energy governs wetting, adhesion, and friction, yet is commonly regarded as a static property defined by surface chemistry and liquid composition. Here we show that light can reversibly modulate the interfacial energy at chemically invariant semiconductor–electrolyte interfaces by tuning the electrostatic coupling between electronic carriers in the solid and ions in the liquid. Using dark dynamic tensiometry, we directly quantify photoinduced changes in advancing and receding contact angles, revealing pronounced and reversible wettability modulation that is absent on insulating or metallic substrates. Systematic control experiments indicate that, in simple salt electrolytes, the response arises primarily from electrostatic coupling between photomodulated carriers and mobile ions in the electric double layer, rather than from detectable photochemical surface modification or changes in bulk liquid properties. In situ atomic force microscopy and ionovoltaic measurements provide microscopic and quantitative evidence that light attenuates or enhances electrostatic double-layer forces and ion–electron coupling, and reveal a sign reversal in the photoresponse between PFOTS-modified and bare Si interfaces. The opposing responses of PFOTS-modified and bare interfaces persist on p-type Si, showing that the effect is not confined to n-type substrates. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this phototunable coupling extends to reversible control of kinetic friction, enabling active modulation of droplet sliding dynamics. These results also identify imaging light as a potential source of bias in contact-angle measurements at photoactive semiconductor–electrolyte interfaces. These findings establish ion–electron coupling as a tunable thermodynamic lever linking semiconductor physics to macroscopic interfacial energy, opening opportunities for optically controlled wetting, friction, and interfacial transport.

title: The emerging geopolitics of sustainable aviation fuel: Policy architectures, book-and-claim and european strategic dependencies
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Energy Policy
abstract: Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) is becoming a strategic component of aviation decarbonization, but its expansion depends on technological, economic, institutional, and resource conditions. This study compares the combinations of policy instruments, structural production characteristics, and market-governance arrangements observed in the European Union, the United States, the United Kingdom, Japan, Singapore, and Brazil, and considers the potential strategic vulnerabilities these configurations suggest, particularly for the European Union. The comparative qualitative policy analysis draws on peer-reviewed literature, legislation, regulatory documents, and institutional sources, organized through a single four-part framework: policy-instrument mix; structural production conditions; market and governance conditions; and potential strategic vulnerabilities. The cases display different configurations. The European Union and the United Kingdom emphasize mandatory demand; the United States relies more heavily on producer incentives; Japan and Singapore emphasize coordination and supply security; and Brazil combines established biofuel capabilities with a developing SAF framework. These observations do not identify causal effects or rank the configurations. Instead, they indicate possible exposure to feedstock, production, finance, policy-continuity, import, and certification constraints. Book-and-Claim is examined as a governance arrangement that separates environmental attributes from physical fuel flows; its practical contribution depends on credible certification, verification, registry governance, and interoperability. For the European Union, the comparison suggests that regulatory leadership may coexist with external supply and institutional dependencies. The concept of resilient interdependence is therefore proposed as a policy lens rather than a measured outcome.

title: Radical Molecular-Junction Covalent Organic Framework for Asymmetric Iodide Conversion: 100,000 Cycles in Zn-Iodine Batteries
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Aqueous Zinc–iodine batteries are promising for large-scale energy storage owing to their eco-friendliness and safety. However, conventional two-electron cathode hosts suffer from poor cycling life due to polyiodide shuttling and sluggish one-step I–/I2 redox kinetics, which limits their practical usage. Herein, we designed a molecular-junction covalent organic framework (COF) denoted as TNCOF, integrating the tetrathiafulvalene (TTF) donor and the naphthalene diimide (NDI) acceptor. Typically, TTF forms a robust radical-cationic TTF•+ structure by anchoring to iodine electrostatically. TTF•+ and electron-withdrawing NDI within the T•+NCOF molecular junction provide a driving force through an intense local electrostatic potential for the asymmetric iodine conversion (AIC) pathway (I–/I3–/I2 vs. I2/I–), markedly boosting reaction kinetics and suppressing polyiodide shuttling. The optimized T•+NCOF cathode delivers a specific capacity of 228.7 mAh g–1 at 1 A g–1 and achieves an ultralong cycling stability exceeding 100,000 cycles, which is one of the highest records in this field. In situ measurements, Peak Force Tunneling atomic force microscopy (AFM) results, and calculations confirm the robust adsorption capability of T•+NCOF and demonstrate the accelerated I3– conversion kinetics. This work establishes that a radical-cationic molecular-junction COF enables robust I3– anchoring and a unique AIC pathway, offering a novel strategy to overcome inherent stability challenges in Zinc-halogen batteries.

title: In Situ STEM Imaging of Colloidal Crystals Based on Programmable Atom Equivalents
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract It is challenging to image the assembly of colloidal crystals composed of programmable atom equivalents (PAEs) using electron microscopy (EM). PAEs typically consist of nanoparticle cores densely functionalized with radially oriented DNA shells, which assemble in the liquid phase via DNA bonds. EM requires high-vacuum conditions, and electron beams can damage soft materials like nucleic acids. Here, we present a liquid-phase scanning transmission electron microscopy (LPSTEM) method for imaging PAEs composed of ∼5 nm gold nanoparticle cores in solution, enabling the direct investigation of their DNA-directed assembly processes. This system is particularly well-suited for in situ studies of soft-matter dynamics because the gold nanoparticle cores provide strong electron contrast. Using a nanofluidic liquid cell, the nucleation and growth of PAE assemblies, governed via the principles of colloidal crystal engineering with DNA, were directly observed. Imaging conditions were established to resolve colloidal assemblies in liquid while also characterizing electron-beam-induced damage under both conventional STEM and STEM-in-SEM conditions. Quantitative image analysis reveals changes in local coordination during crystal growth and subsequent beam-induced dissociation. Complementary ex situ simulations corroborate that radiolytic species generated in the buffer are major contributors to beam-induced damage. Together, these results establish a versatile and accessible platform for probing the in situ dynamics of PAE assembly in liquids, with broad applicability to the study of other soft nanomaterials and composites relevant to sensing, actuation, energy storage, catalysis, and medicine.

title: Supramolecular Regulation of the Enzymatic Dephosphorylation of Twin Phosphotyrosine Peptides
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract We report the design, preparation, and study of a supramolecular pseudopeptidic cage that selectively binds twin phosphotyrosine (pTyr–pTyr) peptides and modulates their enzymatic dephosphorylation in water. The receptor combines an expanded aromatic cavity specifically designed to encapsulate a twin Tyr-Tyr motif with peripheral Lys-derived ammonium groups that engage phosphate residues through electrostatic interactions. In addition to studying the cage’s binding properties through different experimental and computational techniques, we investigated the ability of the receptor to modulate the kinetics of the irreversible phosphate hydrolysis catalyzed by alkaline phosphatase (ALP). When different substrates are connected through irreversible catalytic reactions, forming a nascent network, the presence of a supramolecular protecting host, able to selectively bind these substrates, modifies the system outcome in a way that cannot be predicted from the mere comparison of individual binding constants. This leads to unexpected, emerging behaviors, altering the relative intermediate concentrations through time and therefore regulating the network response. We demonstrate the biochemical potential of this cage by protecting the twin pTyr–pTyr motif within the activation loop of JAK2 kinase from dephosphorylation by λ-protein phosphatase. Altogether, our results establish supramolecular substrate protection as an effective strategy to regulate multistep enzymatic reaction networks.

title: Isolable crystalline oxoboranes

abstract: Oxoboranes, compounds featuring a central dicoordinate boron atom engaged in a B–O triple bond, have long been regarded as highly reactive and are typically observed only as transient species. Although attempts to synthesize them date back to the 1960s, their isolation in the condensed phase has proved challenging. Now, two independent studies describe the isolation of neutral and cationic oxoboranes derived from related diboracumulenes.

title: Physical field coupling in hydrogen production: A critical review from single-field to multi-field synergistic mechanisms
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: Hydrogen production technologies play a critical role in the global transition toward sustainable energy systems. However, their practical deployment is often constrained by the inherent limitations of catalysis driven by the single physical field, resulting in insufficient hydrogen-production efficiency. While existing reviews have extensively examined individual hydrogen production pathways, a unified framework that systematically bridges single-field fundamentals and multi-field coupling mechanisms with quantitative assessment of field-induced performance enhancement remains lacking. This work systematically reviews the developmental trajectory of hydrogen production technologies from single-physical-field catalysis to multiphysical-field coupling. Firstly, the fundamental principles and latest advances in hydrogen production driven by single physical fields—including photocatalysis, thermocatalysis, electrocatalysis, piezocatalysis, and microwave-assisted catalysis—are summarized, with detailed discussion of their reaction mechanisms and representative catalytic systems. Building upon this foundation, the review further focuses on multiphysical-field coupling strategies aimed at overcoming the above limitations. Coupled-field hydrogen production systems are broadly categorized into external-field-enhanced photocatalysis (including photo-thermal, photo-electrical, photo-magnetic, and photo-acoustic coupling), external-field-enhanced thermocatalysis (including microwave-assisted and plasma-enhanced systems), and external-field-enhanced electrocatalysis (including thermo-electrical, magneto-electrical, electric-field-enhanced, and stress-enhanced systems). The synergistic mechanisms by which auxiliary external fields regulate charge-carrier dynamics, surface reaction energy barriers, and overall hydrogen production intensification are discussed in depth. Notably, the performance enhancement induced by different physical-field coupling strategies is quantitatively assessed relative to the corresponding baseline systems, providing quantitative insight into the strengthening effects of auxiliary physical fields. Finally, the major challenges currently facing multiphysical-field-coupled hydrogen production technologies, as well as their future prospects, are highlighted. This review aims to provide a systematic framework for understanding the evolution of hydrogen-production technologies and the mechanisms of multiphysical-field coupling, while offering guidance for the mechanistic interpretation, quantitative evaluation, practical implementation, and sustainable development of coupled hydrogen-production systems.

title: Technology trajectories and critical raw materials in sodium-ion battery innovation: An LLM-assisted patent analysis
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: Sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) are emerging as a promising complement to lithium-ion batteries for cost-sensitive and resource-resilient energy-storage applications. Despite growing technological and industrial interest, the structure of SIB innovation remains insufficiently understood because existing patent studies have largely focused on aggregate filing trends. To address this gap, this study develops a high-resolution patent landscape through large language model-assisted classification of 9670 patent families across technological domains, battery components, electrode material classes, assignee types, regions, and cathode-related critical raw materials. The results show that SIB innovation remains strongly materials-driven, with material-related inventions accounting for almost 86% of all patent families. Within this landscape, layered transition-metal oxides account for 51% of cathode-related patent families, while hard carbon represents 44% of anode-related patent families. Innovation activity is also highly concentrated geographically, with more than 94% of the analyzed patent families including at least one Chinese assignee. At the organizational level, companies focus more strongly on near-term material pathways, whereas public organizations show greater engagement with alternative chemistries. Furthermore, critical raw materials (CRMs) continue to play a central role in SIB cathodes: 76% of cathode patent families require at least one CRM, 15% include one conditionally, and only 9% contain no CRM. The degree of this exposure varies substantially across cathode classes, with manganese, nickel, phosphorus, and vanadium emerging as the most prominent CRMs. Overall, these findings show that the strategic value of SIBs depends on material selection, regional innovation capacity, and chemistry-specific CRM exposure, with implications for research, industry, and policy.

title: Operating-point-dependent power-flow linearisation for joint siting, sizing, and dispatch of long-duration energy storage in distribution grids
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: Long-term energy-storage planning in distribution grids involves long time series, non-linear network constraints, and mixed-integer siting and sizing decisions. Especially detailed AC formulations are computationally challenging for long optimisation horizons. To address this challenge, we propose an operating-point-dependent linearisation of the AC power-flow equations using sensitivity coefficients and integrating them into a mixed-integer linear program for the joint siting, sizing and dispatch of different flexibility options over long time horizons. An iterative AC power-flow validation and relinearisation procedure is used to ensure approximation accuracy. Different approaches to select the linearisation points are benchmarked, either by using each operating point or by clustering approaches, using k -medoids while retaining the original injection and network data. The method is evaluated on SimBench distribution networks and benchmarked against non-linear AC-OPF formulations. Operating-point-dependent linearisation enables computationally tractable storage planning over long time horizons while preserving detailed network information. Clustering can reduce computational effort by about 40 % , provided that the original operating-point data are retained. The linearised model deviates from the lossless AC-OPF benchmark by approximately 0.3 % in storage power and 0.6 % in energy capacity. To demonstrate the use of the method, we develop a case study where household flexibility and grid scale storage are co-optimised in a full-year planning problem. The results show that aggregate household flexibility primarily affects storage sizing, whereas its spatial distribution influences local grid conditions and optimal siting.

title: Stochastic assessment of eight emergency electricity supply configurations for urban shelters: Performance limits and the role of vehicle-to-shelter
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: Emergency electricity planning for urban shelters requires comparing heterogeneous supply resources under uncertain, time-varying demand. This study assesses eight specified emergency electricity-supply configurations, including two Vehicle-to-Shelter (V2S) arrangements, for a 1000-person shelter during a 72-h grid outage. A common framework combines paired Monte Carlo simulation, hourly supply–demand matching, continuous resource-state evolution, and access-conditioned variance decomposition, while retaining configuration-specific constraints on power, usable energy, infrastructure continuity, resource access, and deployment timing. Across nine demand and disaster-severity scenarios, adequacy declined as shelter services expanded and cold-season demand increased, while access-dependent resources were additionally constrained by infrastructure continuity, allocation, and arrival. High coverage of the specified diesel-generator configuration depended strongly on its usable energy in the most demanding scenario, where a 20% stock reduction lowered mean energy coverage ratio (ECR) from 0.819 to 0.659. Similar aggregate coverage also concealed different temporal risks. Under hot conditions with moderate disaster severity, a mobile power-supply truck and a local-plus-external V2S arrangement had nearly identical mean ECRs (0.368 and 0.367) under baseline access assumptions but different temporal shortfall patterns. The truck provided no support before allocation and arrival, whereas locally parked EVs supplied limited early power. Access-state differences accounted for most observed ECR variance for the access-dependent configurations in the two examined scenarios, distinguishing conditional resource capability from unconditional shelter adequacy. These findings support mechanism-based screening by power, endurance, immediate availability, and credible access arrangements, while suggesting a potential role for V2S as a conditional supplement rather than a universal substitute for dedicated backup supply.

title: A continental dilemma: Is centralized or decentralized renewable hydrogen cheaper?
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: Hydrogen is a strong candidate on the path towards the decarbonization of the transportation, energy, and industry sectors. In addition to being a well-known element, hydrogen is mainly produced from fossil fuels, with the renewable production chain still requiring development. In this context, this work evaluates the technical and economic potential of hydrogen production using solar photovoltaic (PV) energy and electricity purchased from the Brazilian grid, and evaluates two layouts: (i) centralized production of solar PV energy and hydrogen at the same site and (ii) decentralized production of energy and hydrogen powered by the Brazilian interconnected grid (SIN). The use of PV energy is found to decrease the levelized cost of hydrogen ( L C O H ) when compressed, from 14.00 USD / kg to 13.24 USD / kg in the centralized case and to 9.11 USD / kg in the decentralized case. However, a system powered only by P V energy had a cost of 18.23 USD / kg ; this corroborates the fact that the highest verified cost is from the purchase of energy from the grid. From the analysis of the design parameters, increasing the electrolyzer power and the size of the PV field reduces the L C O H , due to the economies of scale of both pieces of equipment. The optimization shows that it is possible to reach an L C O H for compressed hydrogen of 9.89 USD / kg for the centralized system and values of 5.88 USD / kg for the decentralized system.

title: A retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)-enhanced framework for knowledge-guided campus-scale building retrofit design
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: Urban-scale building envelope optimization is constrained by the computational burden of iterative simulation. This study proposes a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)-enhanced framework that replaces the search phase of conventional optimization: literature-screened envelope solutions are retrieved from a curated corpus and then cross-checked through physics-based EnergyPlus simulation, rather than located through exhaustive parametric search. The corpus comprises 20,247 initially identified publications screened to a core of 338 studies, together with an experimentally characterized database of 502 envelope materials, of which 65 were used in the assemblies evaluated here. A three-stage progressive retrofit strategy — conventional high-performance insulation; vacuum insulation panels, aerogel and phase change materials (PCMs); and optimized PCM hybrid assemblies — was applied to seven reference buildings on Yonsei University's 86-building campus in Seoul, Korea. A systematic literature review established that whole-building field-measured savings are systematically 0.25–0.75× of simulation-only upper bounds, a correction embedded directly in the retrieval thresholds and screening criteria. The seven reference buildings produce a simulated mean building-level EUI reduction of 21.5%, ranging from 9.5% in high window-to-wall-ratio modern buildings to 39.6% in thermally deficient heritage structures, while campus-wide analysis of all 86 buildings yields 15.7% (124.4 to 104.9 kWh/m 2 ·year). EnergyPlus models were not calibrated against sub-metered operational data, so all reported reductions are simulation-based screening estimates. The framework offers a scalable, computationally efficient route to envelope retrofit planning for large institutional portfolios and urban decarbonization programs.

Here, common solvents entering a flexible luminescent porous polymer restrict intramolecular motion of the AIEgen units, suppressing nonradiative decay and enhancing quantum yield 1.8-fold. This reversible, optically readable rigidification offers a design principle for responsive porous materials.

title: Discerning between Excimer and Singlet Fission Sites Using Modulated Magnetic Field Photoluminescence
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Magnetic field effects play a key role in the characterization of organic electronic materials. In particular, the microscopic processes underlying singlet fission and triplet–triplet annihilation have been clarified in recent years through the observation and subsequent theoretical explanation of magnetic field effects in these processes. Here, we study magnetic field effects on the luminescence of 5,12-bis((triisopropylsilyl)ethynyl)tetracene, a well-studied material in which both singlet fission and triplet–triplet annihilation occur. By performing highly sensitive modulated-field magneto-photoluminescence experiments we observe magnetic field effect lineshapes with rich detail, allowing a precise characterization of triplet exciton dynamics. By additionally filtering these magnetic field effects by luminescence wavelength, we can identify the excimer state by its unique magnetic field signature. Finally, we show that a theoretical explanation of these field effects requires a model that explicitly accounts for quantum coherences, which highlights the importance of detailed spin dynamics modeling in understanding magnetic field effects, even at room temperature.

title: Cathode Surface Reconfiguration via Solvent Chemistry for Durable All-Solid-State Lithium Batteries
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Electrode surfaces and interfaces critically dominate the performance of all-solid-state lithium batteries. However, established additive-oriented strategies physically isolate the cathode from the electrolyte without improving the restricted Li+ transport pathways of the cathode surface. Here, we propose a solvation-mediated chemical etching mechanism governing cathode surface reconfiguration, driven by competition between solvent coordination and lattice stabilization. The solvent coordination, coupled with electron and proton transfer, weakens transition-metal–oxygen covalency and destabilizes lattice-bound surface species, shifting the interfacial energy landscape toward solvation-favored states. This triggers selective transition-metal dissolution and oxygen modulation, ultimately reorganizing confined surface regions into continuous Li+ transport networks. Using micron-sized single-crystalline Li- and Mn-rich cathodes as a model, we demonstrate the formation of a Mn- and O-deficient interfacial layer equipped with a three-dimensional Li+ diffusion network. This functional layer accelerates Li+ diffusion and anionic redox kinetics while suppressing transition metal migration and oxygen release. Consequently, charge-transfer resistance drops drastically (from 585 to 67 Ω) and Li+ diffusion increases 90-fold at 4.8 V, enabling 80.3% capacity retention after 2800 cycles at 2C. This solvent-driven reconfiguration provides a scalable framework for stabilizing diverse cathodes in next-generation advanced batteries.

title: Extraframework Cations Promoted Ultratrace Acetylene Capture by Coordinatively Unsaturated Nickel Sites in FAU Zeolites
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Removal of ultratrace alkynes to produce polymer- and electronic-grade olefins is an important but extremely challenging task. Here, we report a dual-cation strategy in FAU-type zeolites that enables the unprecedented capture of acetylene at concentrations of parts per million (ppm). The optimized Ni–Ba–Y adsorbent delivers high dynamic uptakes of 0.37–0.82 mmol·g–1 at acetylene concentrations of 500–10,000 ppm, with acetylene/ethylene selectivity exceeding 100 under industrial relevant conditions. Neutron powder diffraction (NPD) and theoretical calculations reveal that Ba2+ at Site I modulate the coordinatively unsaturated Ni2+ centers at Site II, enhancing π-back-donation to adsorbed acetylene. Process simulations demonstrate that adsorptive separation using Ni–Ba–Y achieves over 200-fold higher space-time productivity (STP) of ethylene and reduces energy consumption by over 44% compared with conventional catalytic hydrogenation processes. This dual-cation strategy will promote the design of zeolite adsorbents for challenging industrial separations.
