title: G:C:G:C-Flanked i-Motifs Are Thermodynamically Favored and Their Sequences Highly Enriched in the Human Genome
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract i-Motifs are biologically relevant noncanonical DNA structures whose stability is strongly influenced by capping interactions. Among these, minor groove tetrads (MGTs) are among the most powerful stabilizing elements identified to date, yet the molecular factors governing their effects and their potential biological significance remain poorly understood. Here, we present a systematic experimental and computational analysis of 16 MGT-stabilized i-motifs (MGTiMs), encompassing all combinations of terminal tetrad composition and orientation within a common sequence scaffold. NMR spectroscopy confirms that all sequences adopt closely related architectures, enabling direct comparison of the effects of tetrad identity and orientation on stability. Thermal denaturation experiments reveal that the stability hierarchy, previously observed in selected structures (G:C:G:C ≳ G:C:G:T ≫ G:T:G:T), is broadly maintained across the series, although substantial positional effects are observed. Molecular dynamics simulations and energy decomposition analyses suggest that differences in electrostatic interactions and local conformational flexibility contribute to these trends. Notably, genome-wide analysis of the human genome reveals a strong enrichment of sequences capable of forming the most stabilizing tetrads, with motifs containing two G:C:G:C tetrads reaching a 45-fold enrichment relative to random expectation. Interestingly, this most abundant genomic motif is also the only one that undergoes pronounced pH-driven conformational transitions, highlighting the unique structural plasticity of these architectures. Together, these findings reveal how tetrad composition and positional context govern MGTiM stability and identify NN-type motifs as a particularly enriched class of structurally distinctive genomic sequences.

title: Tritium breeding lifetime assessment of a ceramic-based blanket in a fusion tokamak device
source: Nuclear Fusion - latest papers
abstract: Achieving tritium self-sufficiency is a critical requirement for the viability of future fusion power plants. Here, a comprehensive assessment of the operational lifetimes of ceramic breeder materials under neutron irradiation within a tokamak environment is presented, focusing on the evolution of the tritium breeding ratio (TBR) over reactor-relevant timescales. This is defined here as the operational timeframe at which the TBR is maintained above a critical threshold of 1.10. Using the depletion capabilities within the OpenMC neutronics code, both conventional ceramic breeders (Li TiO , Li SiO , and advanced ceramic breeder—ACB) and emerging hybrid breeder-multiplier ceramics (Li PbO , Li Be O ) are assessed for operational lifetime strategies. Initial optimisation identifies breeder-to-multiplier volumetric ratios that maximise TBR at time zero, followed by time-dependent simulations to quantify TBR degradation due to lithium depletion during service. It is shown that while higher initial multiplier fractions enhance TBR, they also accelerate lithium depletion, reducing blanket lifetime. Conversely, hybrid ceramics with intrinsic neutron multiplication show reduced sensitivity to additional multipliers. A novel layer-wise optimisation approach, varying breeder and multiplier distributions radially and poloidally, is shown to extend blanket lifetimes and maintain TBR above the critical threshold for longer periods demonstrating lifetime limitations may be elsewhere within the breeder blanket. Verification against FISPACT-II confirms the accuracy of the OpenMC depletion methodology utilised. The results highlight the importance of spatially optimised material distributions and lithium inventory management in maximising breeder blanket longevity. This work provides a robust framework for the design of next-generation solid breeder blankets, offering practical strategies to minimise replacement frequency and support sustainable fusion energy.

title: Entropy Engineering Accelerates High-Temperature Oxygen Evolution Reaction Rate via Spin Manipulation
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The high-temperature oxygen evolution reaction (OER) activity is closely correlated to the spin state of transition metals in perovskite anodes. However, the roles of entropy engineering in modulating the spin state and influencing high-temperature OER kinetics remain poorly understood. Herein, we demonstrate that entropy engineering of La0.7Sr0.3FeO3−δ to (SmNdPrLaBaSrCa)FeO3−δ (SNPLBSCF) induces a transition of B-site Fe species from high-spin to low-spin states. This transition enhances the d–p hybridization of Fe–O bonds, lowers the energy barriers for electron transfer and oxygen ion migration, and finally accelerates the high-temperature OER kinetics. Consequently, the SNPLBSCF anode in a solid oxide electrolysis cell (SOEC) achieves a current density of 3.64 A·cm–2 at 800 °C and 1.6 V, outperforming most reported anodes. This work not only provides fundamental insights into the spin state-activity relationships of perovskite oxides but also offers a viable strategy for the rational design of highly efficient SOEC anodes through entropy engineering.

title: Resolving Chlorine Sites in Pharmaceuticals by Integrated Site-Resolved Zeeman-Perturbed NQR, Solid-State NMR, and Electron Diffraction Crystallography
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Many active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) and high-value chemicals feature covalently bonded chlorine functionalities that influence molecular packing, stability, and bioavailability. However, site-resolved structural characterization of chlorine sites in powders remains challenging, especially in systems with multiple chemically or crystallographically nonequivalent sites, disorder, or hydration sensitivity. We report here a novel combined 35Cl nuclear quadrupole resonance (NQR), 35Cl Zeeman-perturbed NQR (Zp-NQR), 35Cl solid-state NMR, and three-dimensional electron diffraction (3D ED/microcrystal electron diffraction) approach to characterizing powdered chlorine-bearing chemicals. Case studies of ketoconazole and chloramine-T demonstrate the utility of the approach in characterizing local structural heterogeneity and the hydration state. The role of crystal packing and noncovalent interactions on the spectroscopic observables is provided through an analysis of chlorzoxazone and five of its cocrystals, of which three are novel. Compared to ultrahigh-field NMR spectra alone, NQR and Zp-NQR spectra provide improved sensitivity to small changes in the electric field gradient and in the degree of disorder around chlorine. Experimental NQR/Zp-NQR data combined with gauge-including projector augmented-wave density functional theory (GIPAW-DFT) provide local structural constraints for a partially dehydrated chloramine-T phase. The refinement protocol does not require single crystals, and in the case of NQR experiments, intact tablets containing APIs are analyzed directly without further treatment or grinding. As a proof of principle, commercial tablets are shown to contain ketoconazole in the same crystalline form as that seen for the pure API. The general approach could be extended to other complex solids incorporating quadrupolar nuclei and is not limited to solid-form screening, polymorph identification, and differentiation of salts and cocrystals.

title: Direct-to-Biology Bifunctional Screening Reveals Noncanonical Mechanisms of Targeted Protein Degradation
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Targeted protein degradation (TPD) has emerged as a powerful strategy for modulating protein function through small-molecule-induced proximity between a protein of interest (POI) and typically an E3 ubiquitin ligase to promote its proteasomal degradation. Despite significant progress, most degraders co-opt a narrow set of E3 ubiquitin ligases, motivating mechanistically agnostic strategies for discovering new routes to degradation. Here, we pursued a “degrader-first” approach using direct-to-biology (D2B) synthesis to construct and screen a 114-member library of BRD4-targeting bifunctional molecules to identify chemically tractable ligases that support TPD. Multiple compounds were found to induce Cullin-RING ligase (CRL)-dependent degradation, and two top hits were selected for mechanistic characterization. Unexpectedly, neither operates through canonical heterobifunctional E3 recruitment. Instead, one undergoes oxidative activation to generate a reactive electrophile that promotes degradation through DCAF11- or DCAF16-containing CRL4 complexes in a cell-context-dependent manner. The second acts through a bivalent bromodomain-binding mechanism that likely induces target conformational contraction and potentiates endogenous CRL3–SPOP-mediated ubiquitination. These findings highlight the capacity of D2B discovery approaches to expose noncanonical modalities of TPD while underscoring the importance of rigorous mechanistic deconvolution in interpreting screening-derived degraders.

title: Enantioconvergent N -Alkylation of Indoles with Alcohols Promoted by an Axially Chiral Iridacycle
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Achieving chemo- and enantioselective N-substitution of indoles presents significant challenges for catalytic method development. Herein, we report an enantioconvergent N-substitution of indoles with racemic secondary alcohols enabled by a newly developed axially chiral biaryl-supported iridacycle and chiral phosphoric acid. This borrowing-hydrogen process proceeds through an intriguing sequence involving transfer hydrogenation of indole, enantioselective reductive amination of an indoline intermediate, and subsequent rearomatization. Controlled reaction temperatures also enable selective access to the N-substituted indolines prior to rearomatization. The catalytic process accommodates diverse indoles and unactivated secondary alcohols without additional stoichiometric reagents, providing a direct and atom-economical approach to enantioenriched N-substituted indoles, including analogs of established drug candidates.

title: Halogenated Triazole-Based Metal–Organic Framework Achieves Ultra-Selective CO2 Capture under Humid Conditions
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Selective CO2 capture from humid, N2-rich flue gas requires adsorbents that combine extreme CO2/N2 discrimination with robustness under realistic conditions. However, only a few MOFs are able to combine ultrahigh selectivity, humidity tolerance, scalable synthesis, and structural durability. Here, we introduce CALF-20-X (X = Cl or Br) halogentriazolate–oxalate Zn-MOFs and a PVDF composite, integrating these attributes into an ultramicroporous framework. The halogenated Zn-MOFs are obtained by means of solvent-minimized liquid-assisted grinding followed by water-incubation route, producing a highly crystalline material. Halogen functionalization polarizes the triazolate C–H donor, thereby promoting directional C–H···O(CO2) contacts and enhancing electrostatic complementarity, as evidenced by an experimental isosteric heat of adsorption of 48 kJ/mol. Furthermore, this halogen substitution significantly restricts the size of the pore window inhibiting N2 uptake, and leads to the formation of perfectly CO2-fitted pockets. These combined features enabled a CO2 excellent adsorption of 2.89 mmol g–1 at 0.15 bar and 298 K, and CO2/N2 selectivity higher than 4074 for CALF-20-Cl, exceeding leading physisorbent benchmarks. The highly selective CO2 capture was confirmed by dynamic breakthrough experiments performed on a CALF-20-Cl@PVDF composite under humid conditions over numerous cycles, thus demonstrating its robust performance under flue-gas-relevant conditions. Competitive CO2/H2O breakthrough experiments, supported by GCMC simulations, demonstrate that CO2 sorption is favored at 21% relative humidity (RH), resulting in a 56% suppression of water uptake, and even remains competitive at RH > 50% and 318 K, a temperature relevant for carbon capture from point sources. These results highlight halogen-driven structural engineering for regenerable and humidity-tolerant next-generation CO2-selective MOF adsorbents with complete retention of the performance metrics.

title: Elusive *CH–*CHO Coupling Pathway for High-Performance CO2 Electroreduction to n-Propanol
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The electrocatalytic reduction of CO2 to high-value n-propanol represents a promising yet challenging route toward sustainable carbon utilization. However, its practical implementation is severely hindered by low selectivity and activity, primarily originating from the high energy barrier involved in the rate-limiting *C2–*C1 coupling step. Herein, we have successfully constructed an elusive *CH–*CHO coupling pathway on a stable Janus Cu2+/Cu0 catalyst, enabling low-barrier *C2 intermediate formation and highly selective n-propanol production. Leveraging the strong electron-accepting capacity of Cu2+ sites, key *CHO intermediates are strongly adsorbed and driven toward deep reduction to *CH species, effectively overcoming the critical five-electron transfer bottleneck for *CH generation. Meanwhile, adjacent Cu0 sites provide moderate and balanced adsorption of *CHO intermediates, allowing their asymmetric coupling with the Cu2+-stabilized *CH via a markedly low energy barrier, synergistically steering the reaction along the favorable *CH–*CHO pathway. In situ fiber-optic guided ATR-FTIR spectroscopy provides evidence for the coexistence of *CHO and *CHx-related intermediates, while DFT calculations further support the proposed *CH–*CHO coupling pathway. Accordingly, the Janus Cu2+/Cu0 catalyst achieves a high n-propanol Faradaic efficiency of 18.1% at a partial current density of 72.4 mA cm–2, alongside remarkable stability. This work establishes the *CH–*CHO pathway as a powerful strategy for kinetically favorable C–C coupling, opening a new mechanistic avenue for efficient conversion of CO2 to multicarbon via electrosynthesis.

title: An Allosteric CLR N-Terminal Swing-Out Mechanism for RAMP-Mediated Adrenomedullin Receptor Selectivity
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Three receptor activity-modifying proteins (RAMP1–3) form heterodimers with the calcitonin (CTR) and calcitonin-like (CLR) G protein-coupled receptors and determine their selectivity for six CGRP family peptide agonists. These ligand–receptor systems are drug targets for migraine headache, diabetes and obesity, and circulatory system disorders. Here, we used molecular dynamics simulations and pharmacological assays of receptor chimeras and point mutants to identify a crucial allosteric component of the mechanism by which RAMP2 and RAMP3 modulate CLR to confer selectivity for two adrenomedullin (AM) peptides. We found that the extracellular domain (ECD) of RAMP2 and RAMP3, but not RAMP1, stabilized a partially unwound “swing-out” conformation of the CLR ECD N-terminal α-helix to accommodate the unique binding mode of the midregion of the AM peptides. The inability of the CTR N-terminus to adopt the swing-out conformation contributed to the distinct peptide selectivity profile of the three CTR-RAMP amylin receptors. By exploiting the CLR swing-out conformation, we engineered AM antagonist peptide variants with enhanced affinity and selectivity for CLR-RAMP2 and -RAMP3. Our results reveal the long-sought mechanism of RAMP-altered CLR ligand selectivity and have significant implications for drug development targeting the CLR- and CTR-RAMP complexes.

title: Chemical Programming of Stacking Order and Superconductivity Dimensionality in NbSe 2–x Te x Polytypic Heterostructures
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Layered transition-metal dichalcogenides exhibit electronic states highly sensitive to lattice symmetry, yet elucidating the structure–superconductivity relationship has been challenging due to the lack of a continuous structural evolution within a single material system. Here, we establish NbSe2–xTex as a model system, where Te substitution drives a sequential polytypic transition across the full composition range─from the low-Te 2H phase, through mixed 1H/1T heterostructured 4H and 6R polytypes at intermediate substitution, to ideal 1T and distorted 1T′ structures at high Te content. Combining comprehensive characterizations, we map both the structural evolution and the accompanying changes in spectral weight and orbital character near the Fermi level. Electrical transport measurements reveal a striking phase-dependent superconducting dimensionality: the 4H phase (NbSe1.4Te0.6) exhibits enhanced anisotropy and an anomalous boost in the in-plane upper critical field, while the 6R phase (NbSe1.2Te0.8) shows suppressed Tc (∼2.8 K) and three-dimensional-like behavior. The combined electronic-structure and superconducting results connect the stacking sequence to effective interlayer coherence and the local spin–orbit environment. SOC band calculations resolve the distinct symmetry constraints on the 4H and 6R electronic states. These mechanisms fundamentally differ from conventional approaches by leveraging intrinsic, composition-driven polytypism to modify interlayer coupling and band structure. Thus, by establishing a definitive phase diagram that directly correlates polytypism with superconducting dimensionality, our work provides a clear roadmap for the rational design of low-dimensional superconducting devices through stacking-sequence engineering.

title: A Unique Conformationally Assisted [2+2] Configuration in Cycloparaphenylenes Enables Efficient Laser Devices
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Two π-conjugated macrocycles, namely the well-known [12]cycloparaphenylene and a newly designed macrocycle combining benzenes and rigid stilbene units, are presented for the first time as light-amplifying gain media in distributed feedback (DFB) laser devices. Both systems show good photonic functionality arising from a four-state photonic cycle comprising a [2+2] state configuration (two delocalized and two conformationally distorted localized states). The mechanism involves the generation of two optically coupled states through excited-state structural distortion induced during internal conversion, which reduces light reabsorption losses and promotes rapid population inversion. Comprehensive steady-state absorption and fluorescence and transient absorption spectroscopy studies are conducted in order to reveal the nature of the low energy lying excited states. Furthermore, amplified spontaneous emission studies of the compounds in polystyrene thin films, followed by the preparation and characterization of optically pumped DFB lasers, were performed. The results reveal new properties of these multifunctional cyclic π-conjugated molecules and unique structure-property relationships.

title: Decoding Direct Regeneration of Spent LiFePO 4 : From Defect Evolution to Thermodynamic–Kinetic Barrier Engineering
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT The rapid growth of LiFePO 4 (LFP) batteries has made the sustainable recycling of spent cathodes increasingly important for the battery circular economy. Direct regeneration has emerged as the most promising strategy because it preserves the pristine framework, minimizes energy consumption, and maximizes material value. However, the underlying principles governing regeneration remain elusive, as exemplified by the apparent thermodynamic‐kinetic paradox that metallic lithium has been reported to be ineffective for restoring spent LFP, whereas weaker reductants can achieve effective recovery. These observations indicate that regeneration is governed not by thermodynamic driving force alone, but by the coupled effects of electron transfer, ion diffusion, and lattice defects. In this study, we introduce a multiscale defect framework that correlates defect formation energy (Δ H f ), migration barriers ( E a ), and electron‐transfer reorganization energy ( λ ) with different degradation states of spent LFP. A hypothesis that the dominant barrier evolves with degradation was proposed, enabling failure‐dependent strategies ranging from relithiation and phase‐boundary engineering to defect‐guided upcycling. By transforming regeneration from empirical optimization into rational barrier engineering, this perspective provides a unified understanding of diverse restoration pathways. Finally, emerging challenges, including impurity management, AI‐assisted diagnostics, and closed‐loop materials design, are discussed to guide the development of sustainable battery recycling technologies.

title: Hypoxia-Driven, Self-Accelerating Immolative Photosensitizer Enabling Effective and Safe Photodynamic Therapy
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Photodynamic therapy (PDT) is an emerging cancer treatment modality, but its clinical translation is hindered by the persistent post-PDT phototoxicity of existing photosensitizers. To address this challenge, we herein report a hypoxia-driven, self-accelerating immolative photosensitizer in which PDT itself drives posttherapy detoxification. This is demonstrated with AIE photosensitizers with an N-oxidation-mediated photoinduced electron transfer (PET) feature, which creates a charge-separation state with pronounced electron–nuclear hyperfine coupling feature, enabling efficient intersystem crossing. This N-oxidation thus converts the highly emissive fluorophore TBP into the robust type I photosensitizer TBPO. Critically, the N-O bond could be selectively cleaved by cytochrome P450 reductases under hypoxia, immolating TBPO back to TBP. Unlike previously reported ROS-driven immolative photosensitizers, this hypoxia-mediated immolation does not consume therapeutic ROS and is accelerated by PDT-aggravated hypoxia. Consequently, TBPO exhibits a self-propelled detoxification mechanism, ensuring an initial high PDT efficacy while minimizing residual phototoxicity after therapy. Moreover, this transition process is self-reported by the fluorescence light-up. This molecular design achieves both potent hypoxia-resistant PDT and fail-safe posttreatment safety, addressing two long-standing barriers to clinical PDT. This paradigm shift offers a general design principle for therapy-fueled self-detoxifying photosensitizers toward outpatient PDT without lifestyle restrictions.

title: Nanoscale Flexibility Enables Low-Enthalpy Cooperative Water Sorption
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Passive, sorption-based atmospheric water harvesting technologies (AWHTs) have attracted recent interest as an alternative to energy-intensive condensation-based technologies. Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) offer wide chemical tunability to design sorbents, but in practice, sorbents must retain moisture during humidity fluctuations, and small adsorption enthalpies are necessary for regeneration of the sorbent material. Here, we report that Cu(1,2,3-triazolate)2 nanoparticles with diameters less than 120 nm exhibit structural flexibility at the Cu2+ centers that enables a “breathing”-type cooperative water sorption. This cooperative structural phase change occurs only for nanoparticles that contain Cu2+, and not for the isomorphic magnesium triazolate. The phase change significantly decreases the onset pressures of adsorption and desorption compared to large particles and opens a practically useful hysteresis window in the isotherms, while maintaining small adsorption enthalpies (48 kJ/mol averaged over the isotherm, approaching the 44 kJ/mol latent heat of water at low RH). Mechanistic analysis indicates that adsorption initiates with weak electrostatic and dispersion interactions between water and triazolate rings brought into close proximity only by the distorted Cu2+ centers of the nanoparticles. Together, these results present a distinct water sorption mechanism and design strategy that leverages size- and metal-dependent lattice flexibility in a wide class of porous materials.

title: Radical Ring-Opening Polymerization of endo -Cyclic Monomers for Regioregularity Control in Vinyl Polymers
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Radical polymerization of vinyl monomers is inherently governed by propagation pathways that favor head-to-tail connectivity, limiting access to alternative backbone regioregularities. To address this challenge, we report the radical ring-opening polymerization (rROP) of endo-cyclic monomers, a class of monomers that has been largely unexplored in radical processes. Whereas many established rROP systems have been designed to introduce functional or cleavable units into polymer backbones, the present endo-cyclic monomers undergo selective rROP to generate carbon–carbon-backboned vinyl polymers enriched with nonhead-to-tail linkages. Copolymerization with conventional vinyl monomers was also achieved, providing access to copolymers with tunable backbone microstructures. In particular, using vinyl ketones and their corresponding endo-cyclic cyclodimers as structurally matched pairs, we accessed poly(vinyl ketone)s with systematically varied head-to-tail linkage contents. This control over backbone regioregularity translated into tunable macroscopic properties, including glass transition temperature and photodegradation kinetics, establishing regioregularity as a structural handle for controlling material properties. The strategy was also compatible with controlled radical polymerization, enabling the synthesis of well-defined block copolymers. Micelles assembled from these block copolymers further exhibited regioregularity-dependent sizes and photoresponsive behavior. These findings establish endo-cyclic rROP as a previously unrecognized strategy for controlling backbone regioregularity and properties in vinyl polymers.

title: Thermodynamic–Kinetic Synergy Enables Neon/Helium Separation in an Anion‐Pillared Metal–Organic Framework
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Separating neon (Ne) from helium (He) remains challenging because both gases are chemically inert and weakly interacting, while classical size‐sieving principles predict faster transport for the smaller He atom. Here we address this challenge with the anion‐pillared metal–organic framework (MOF) Ni(4‐DPDS) 2 CrO 4 , whose confined pores combine narrow apertures with electrostatically heterogeneous cavities. This environment provides multiple weak contacts that favor Ne adsorption while producing an inverse diffusional response relative to the expected size trend. At 77 K and 100 kPa, the framework adsorbs 50.63 cm 3 g −1 of Ne but only 0.40 cm 3 g −1 of He in static adsorption, with a kinetic Ne/He selectivity of 113.58. Fixed‐bed experiments afford He with a purity above 99.999%, followed by temperature‐driven recovery of Ne with a purity above 99.7%. The results show that coordinating adsorption thermodynamics with molecular transport offers a route to separating weakly interacting gases beyond equilibrium affinity or classical size sieving alone.

title: Catalytic Enantiodivergent Neophyl Rearrangement
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The neophyl rearrangement is a long-established radical 1,2-aryl migration, yet catalytic enantioselective control of this process has remained elusive. Here we report a cooperative photoredox and chiral Brønsted acid catalytic system for the enantioselective neophyl rearrangement of tertiary alcohol-derived olefins. The reaction affords 1,5-dicarbonyl compounds bearing azaarene-substituted all-carbon quaternary stereocenters with up to 97% ee. Changing the radical precursor alters the preferred mode of catalyst recognition and reverses the absolute stereochemical outcome with the same catalyst configuration, providing access to opposite product enantiomers. The reaction also accommodates racemic olefin substrates, and experiments with the individual substrate enantiomers show that the chiral catalyst can counter their intrinsic stereochemical preferences. The results reveal how changes in catalyst–substrate recognition can alter stereochemical control during a transient radical rearrangement.

title: A Novel Metal‐Hydrogen‐Bonded Organic Framework (M‐HOF) Cathode Material for High‐Performance Lithium–Sulfur Batteries
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium–sulfur (Li–S) batteries (LSBs) are highly promising for next‐generation energy storage devices, yet their practical application is hindered by severe polysulfide shuttling and sluggish sulfur conversion kinetics. Herein, a novel metal‐containing hydrogen‐bonded organic framework (HOF‐21) is constructed and integrated with carbon nanotubes and sulfur as cathode for Li–S batteries. The synergistic combination of hydrogen‐bonding networks and Cu coordination sites enables strong polysulfide anchoring and accelerates sulfur redox conversion. Experimental characterizations and theoretical calculations reveal that the unique framework structure containing metals and rich abundant hydrogen bonds effectively immobilizes soluble lithium polysulfides, while Cu active centers induce interfacial electronic coupling and optimize the thermodynamic conversion pathway of sulfur species. Benefiting from the adsorption–catalysis synergistic regulation, the HOF‐21/CNT@S cathode exhibits enhanced reaction kinetics, suppressed polysulfide migration, and improved interfacial stability. As a result, the assembled HOF‐21/CNT@S battery delivers excellent long‐term cycling stability with a capacity decay rate of only 0.06% per cycle over 500 cycles at 2 C at room temperature. Moreover, it maintains outstanding low‐temperature adaptability, achieving 76.8% capacity retention after 200 cycles at −10°C and 90.6% retention after 200 cycles at −20°C. This work provides a promising strategy for designing advanced cathode materials toward high‐energy‐density Li–S batteries.

title: Surface Texturing Boosts Silicon-Based Tribovoltaic Nanogenerators via Synergistic Edge Electric Field and Tribochemistry
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Silicon-based tribovoltaic nanogenerators (TVNGs) can directly convert sliding-induced interfacial processes into electrical output, but their performance is often limited by inefficient carrier generation and transport. Here, square-pillar arrays were fabricated on monocrystalline silicon to investigate how surface texture affects output magnitude and polarity. Texturing increased the peak current by approximately 25-fold, and both n-type and p-type textured devices exhibited positive current polarity. The p-type device also showed a gradual transition from negative to positive current during initial sliding. Output depended strongly on the longitudinal spacing between pillars and the number of simultaneously engaged transverse rows, whereas no clear monotonic dependence on pillar width was observed under the tested conditions. Among the counterface materials, GCr15 steel produced the highest and most stable output; H62 brass and 1060 aluminum produced lower or unstable currents accompanied by different transfer and oxidation features. Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) revealed a spatially nonuniform surface-potential distribution near pillar edges and a sliding-associated potential change in the trench-bottom region. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) detected SiO2 and substoichiometric silicon oxides on the silicon surface, as well as Fe2O3 in steel-derived wear debris. The strong suppression of output during nitrogen purging further indicates that the response is sensitive to the ambient atmosphere. Taken together, these observations are consistent with a mechanism in which texture-dependent contact and repeated edge encounters modify the interfacial state, while oxide-related transport and oxygen-sensitive tribochemistry contribute to carrier generation and collection. The proposed competition between the built-in electric field (BEF) and an evolving interfacial electric field (IEF) provides a framework for interpreting the polarity transition.

title: Electronic Structure and Charge Separation Modulation of Carbon Nitride by -B(OH)- Groups for Enhanced Photocatalytic Phenol Degradation via Peroxymonosulfate Activation
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Graphitic carbon nitride (CN) has emerged as a promising photocatalyst for peroxymonosulfate (PMS)-based advanced oxidation processes, but its performance is constrained by rapid charge recombination and poor PMS activation capability. Herein, we report a boron-doped CN featuring distinctive -B(OH)- groups (OH-BCN20), synthesized via one-step calcination of urea with trace boric acid. The -B(OH)- groups play a pivotal role in PMS activation by strategically modulating the electronic and band structure of CN. Under dark conditions, the electron-deficient B atoms in the -B(OH)- groups serve as primary active sites, facilitating PMS adsorption and subsequent oxidation to generate 1O2. Upon visible light irradiation, photogenerated holes tend to accumulate at B sites, and the resultant efficient charge separation promotes PMS activation. Consequently, the OH-BCN20/PMS/Vis system removes 99.5% of phenol (PE) under visible light, outperforming the CN/PMS/Vis system (38.8%). In the dark, the OH-BCN20/PMS system degrades 43.5% of PE in 60 min, whereas pristine CN shows no activity. This system also demonstrates robust performance in complex water matrices, achieves effective detoxification, and maintains stable continuous-flow operation for 12 h. This study uncovers the critical role of -B(OH)- groups in achieving efficient electronic and band structure modulation of CN, offering a novel paradigm for designing high-performance metal-free catalysts for wastewater treatment.

title: Harnessing Weak Intermolecular Interactions for Efficient PFOA Capture in a Fluorine-Rich Three-Dimensional Covalent Organic Framework Membrane
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Three-dimensional covalent organic framework (3D-COF) membranes with open porosity represent a promising class of next-generation materials, particularly for selective molecular separations. In this work, we synthesized a fluorinated 3D-COF membrane (Tam-Tfta) via a liquid–liquid interfacial polymerization reaction for the efficient removal of perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA). Owing to the abundance of fluorine functional groups within the COF backbone, the membrane achieved quantitative sequestration of PFOA from wastewater at environmentally relevant concentrations (1.0 μg L–1), while maintaining a high water permeance of ∼40 L m–2 h–1 bar–1. Mechanistic analysis reveals that the 3D-COF membrane enables favorable, orientation-assisted interactions within its pores, facilitating effective capture of amphiphilic PFOA molecules in contaminated water. This work represents one of the first demonstrations of a pure 3D COF membrane specifically engineered for removing PFAS.

title: Thickness-Driven Evolution of Third-Order Nonlinear Response in Ternary TMDC MoNbSe2
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Thickness variation in 2D materials is essential for nonlinear optical (NLO) applications. Since key nonlinear parameters such as nonlinear absorption, effective nonlinear coefficients, and carrier generation-recovery dynamics change from monolayer to few-layer thicknesses, systematic thickness-dependent measurements are needed to extract reliable NLO parameters and identify optimal regimes for applications including mode-locking, optical switching, and optical limiting. Here, third-order NLO responses of heterometallic ternary transition metal dichalcogenide (TMDC) MoNbSe2 nanoflakes are observed with varying thicknesses under two excitation wavelengths. Under 1 µm laser excitation, the saturable absorption (SA) behavior diminishes (β decreasing from –42 to –9.7 × 103 cm/GW) with decreasing thickness from approximately 63 to 3 nm, while under 1558 nm excitation, β varies from –10 to –7.6 × 103 cm/GW at low pump intensity and from 11 to 15.2 × 103 cm/GW at high intensities as the thickness is reduced to 3 nm. Notably, at 3 nm thickness under 1 µm excitation, only SA is observed, as the reduced thickness provides a limited carrier population, thereby only a small fraction of photons excites these carriers, while the rest are transmitted. In contrast, at 1.5 µm excitation reverse saturable absorption (RSA) dominates since the incoming lower photon energy promotes absorption through excited-state and defect-state pathways. These results validate wavelength-dependent NLO fundamentals and highlight the versatility of MoNbSe2 for miniaturized photonic technologies. Moreover, the observed SA response is leveraged for ultrafast photonic generation, enabling stable mode-locked pulse formation with a measured pulse duration of 766 fs at 1.5 µm with a repetition rate of 8.011 MHz. Collectively, this study aims to elucidate thickness-dependent NLO mechanisms, and the demonstrated broadband, wavelength-dependent NLO response and mode-locking performance establish MoNbSe2 as a strong candidate for next-generation ultrafast photonic components.

title: Engineering Nitroimidazole-Based Molecular Elements for Hypoxia-Responsive Oligonucleotide Materials
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Hypoxia-responsive oligonucleotides (ONs) offer a route to conditionally regulate nucleic acid activity in diseased tissues, but the chemical factors that govern their masking and activation remain insufficiently defined. Here, we synthesized four nitroimidazole-modified phosphoramidite monomers derived from adenine (Ah), guanine (Gh), thymine (Th), and cytosine (Ch) and incorporated the Th, Ah, and Gh building blocks into ONs by automated solid-phase synthesis. Using a common parent sequence, we compared Th-, Ah-, and Gh-modified ONs in terms of synthetic compatibility, duplex stability, and reductive release, and further evaluated selected Th-modified ONs in cellular and in vivo studies. Thermal denaturation studies showed that internal Th and Gh modifications caused substantial destabilization of DNA/RNA duplexes, whereas Ah modifications were better tolerated. Under nitroreductase/NADPH reduction conditions, the Gh modification showed the most efficient regeneration of the native ON, while Ah mainly formed reduced but uncleaved products and Th gave partial release. Although Gh provided favorable masking and release behavior, Th offered a more practical balance of synthetic accessibility and duplex inhibition. Th-modified ONs retained Clusterin-silencing activity in MIA PaCa-2 cells and showed hypoxia-associated recovery of activity, and enhanced and prolonged tumor-associated fluorescence in tumor-bearing mice compared with an unmodified control. These results highlight the importance of the tested nucleobase–attachment-site combinations in the design of nitroimidazole-modified ONs.

title: Microneedle-Enabled Metabolic-Redox Amplification Cascade for Suppressing Postoperative Tumor Recurrence
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Residual tumor cells can survive surgical resection by maintaining nutrient supply and antioxidant defenses, thereby driving postsurgical recurrence. Here, we develop a dissolvable microneedle platform, MN-MnO2/MPN, that integrates glucose depletion with redox catalysis to establish a localized metabolic-redox amplification cascade. MnO2 exhibits glucose oxidase-like activity, promoting glucose consumption and H2O2 generation, while the copper-tannic acid metal-polyphenol network facilitates stimulus-responsive Cu2+ release, glutathione depletion, and Fenton-like oxidative catalysis. These coordinated processes amplify intracellular oxidative stress, leading to mitochondrial dysfunction, lipid peroxidation, and tumor cell death. In a 4T1 incomplete-resection model, MN-MnO2/MPN markedly suppresses residual tumor regrowth, reducing tumor weight by approximately 80% and achieving 60% survival at day 38. Mechanistically, treatment decreased intratumoral glucose levels by approximately 60% and increased malondialdehyde levels by 2.5-fold, supporting coordinated metabolic deprivation and oxidative damage in vivo. Transcriptomic analysis further identified 3904 differentially expressed genes, with enrichment of metabolic, oxidative stress, and cell-death-associated pathways. This study shows the potential of locally deployable catalytic therapies that exploit the metabolic and redox vulnerabilities of postoperative residual tumors.

title: Dynamic Oxygen Spillover–Structure Feedback in Asymmetric Site Catalysts: Stability Regimes and Design Principles
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Oxygen spillover refers to the transfer of oxygen‐containing species, including adsorbed intermediates and lattice‐derived oxygen, from a donor site/domain to a functionally nonequivalent acceptor through interfacial or connected surface pathways. Despite extensive studies of surface‐confined spillover, its atomic‐scale dynamics in asymmetric multi‐site catalysts remain elusive. This minireview summarizes forward, reverse, and cross‐site oxygen spillover and the key factors regulating these processes. These factors are categorized into intrinsic material properties, including composition, coordination and interfacial structures, and extrinsic operating conditions, such as applied potentials and local electrolyte environments. Moreover, we elaborate on how integrating in situ/operando spectroscopy with theoretical calculations elucidates the structure–activity relationships and dynamic structural evolution at elevated current densities. In particular, drawing on these mechanistic insights, we discuss rational design strategies for asymmetric multi‐atom site catalysts. Specifically, we emphasize how interface engineering, defect control, and self‐optimization methods promote the synergy of spillover effect and structural stability. Finally, we outline the future research direction and emphasize the urgent need to achieve higher space–time resolution in situ characterization and scalable synthesis of uniform asymmetric site catalysts for practical applications.

title: Injectable Hydrogels for Programmable Protein Release
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Injectable and degradable hydrogels provide a promising route for controlling the spatiotemporal release of protein therapeutics, yet achieving programmable release kinetics across proteins of different sizes remains challenging. Here, dextran–oxanorbornadiene (OND)/PEG–thiol hydrogels are described that integrate a degradable hydrogel network with tunable Michael addition reactivity to enable hydrolysis-gated and chemically programmable protein release. The OND linkers serve dual functions as crosslinkers forming the hydrogel network and as covalent tethers for protein cargos, allowing kinetic control over tethering efficiency and release rate through the choice of OND variant, precursor mixing sequence, and degree of protein functionalization. Using model proteins of different sizes and structural flexibilities—green fluorescent protein (GFP, 27 kDa), immunoglobulin G (IgG, 150 kDa), and the trimeric ectodomain of the HIV-1 glycoprotein (350 kDa)—the system demonstrates a transition from diffusion-dominated to hydrolysis-gated, non-first-order release behavior. Two mechanistically distinct tethering regimes were identified: reaction-rate-dominated tethering for IgG and competition-limited tethering for GFP, providing complementary routes for controlling cargo retention and release. Additional formulation-level modulation through network density and crosslinker topology provided orthogonal control over release rate and protein loading capacity. Representative cargos subjected to covalent tethering and release preserved protein structure and function after release. Collectively, this study establishes a modular framework for designing injectable OND hydrogels that achieve predictable and customizable release kinetics, offering a versatile platform for long-acting delivery of biologic therapeutics.

title: A Metabolically Coupled Photochromic Protein AND-Gate for Living Materials
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Engineered living materials (ELMs) capable of real-time logical operations would offer transformative opportunities for adaptive sensing and biosecurity. However, conventional synthetic biological logic gates rely heavily on transcriptional regulation, which results in sluggish responses, or depend on exogenous chemical reductants that compromise environmental safety and living autonomy. Here, we report an artificial metabolically coupled photochromic protein, engineered via combined site-specific unnatural amino acid incorporation and cysteine mutagenesis to reconfigure the chromophore microenvironment. At the protein level, this dual engineering is proposed to redirected excited-state energy dissipation from radiative decay toward nonradiative charge transfer, associated with enhancing photoreduction kinetics while enabling living bacteria to produce photochromic responses using intracellular reducing equivalents as “logical fuel”. At the living system level, combining this protein with an intracellular “metabolic clearance” mechanism established a precise “Logic 0” state. By integrating the engineered bacteria into 3D-bioprintable hydrogel matrices, we demonstrated a “metabolic–physical” dual-locking platform, in which encrypted visual data remains hidden under the tested conditions unless simultaneously triggered by specific illumination and metabolic substrate supply. This work links cellular metabolic state with optical responsiveness, offering a approach for designing living materials that combine rapid response with information security.

title: Identification of Potent Target VDAC1 for Hepatocellular Carcinoma Therapy with the Natural Chloroxanthone–Xanthone Heterodimer Molecule Inducing Ferroptosis
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a major cause of cancer‐related mortality, underscoring the need for actionable targets and effective small‐molecule therapeutics. Voltage‐dependent anion channel 1 (VDAC1), a key regulator of mitochondrial homeostasis, remains incompletely explored as a therapeutic target in HCC. From the endophytic fungus Penicillium sp. RM, we isolated two pairs of enantiomeric heterodimers ( 1 and 2 ) and their monomers ( 3 and 4 ). Penirmxanthone A ( 1 ) is the first reported chloroxanthone‐xanthone heterodimer, whereas penirmxanthone B ( 2 ) features a previously undescribed chloroxanthone‐gentisin scaffold. In vitro, (+)‐ 1 suppressed aggressive phenotypes of HCC cells and induced ferroptosis. Chemical proteomic, biophysical, and genetic analyses identified VDAC1 as a direct and functionally required target of (+)‐ 1 . Mechanistically, (+)‐ 1 engages VDAC1 through K239 and N241, destabilizes the V‐Set and Transmembrane Domain Containing 2 Like (VSTM2L)‐VDAC1‐Hexokinase 2 (HK2) complex, promotes VDAC1 oligomerization, and impairs mitochondrial membrane potential and energy metabolism, culminating in ferroptosis. VDAC1 knockout attenuated these effects, whereas VDAC1 re‐expression restored them. In vivo, VBIT‐4 diminished (+)‐ 1 ‐induced antitumor and ferroptosis‐related effects. Collectively, these findings identify (+)‐ 1 , to our knowledge, as the first natural product that directly targets VDAC1 to promote its oligomerization and induce ferroptosis, highlighting VDAC1 oligomerization as a potential therapeutic target in HCC.

title: Efficient Depolymerization of Polyester Plastic Enabled by Ultrathin Co-Doped ZnO Nanosheets with Abundant Oxygen Vacancies
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The chemical recycling of polyester plastics is a promising sustainable route to resource recycling and environmental protection, yet its success hinges on the development of efficient heterogeneous catalysts. Herein, a high-gravity-assisted strategy using rotating packed bed (RPB) is proposed to continuously and rapidly synthesize ultrathin Co-doped nanosheets (Co/ZnO-RPB) for depolymerizing polyester plastics. Compared to the counterpart of batch-type stirred tank (Co/ZnO-ST), the optimized nanosheets exhibit a 60% reduction in thickness, accompanied by a 2.3-fold enhancement in doping efficiency and a 1.3-fold increase in oxygen vacancy concentration. The as-prepared Co/ZnO-RPB possessed outstanding performance for PLA methanolysis at 105 °C, achieving a methyl lactate (MeLA) formation rate of 521.7 g gcat–1 h–1, which is 1.8 times higher than that of Co/ZnO-ST, exceeding most reported catalysts. Comprehensive characterization and in situ infrared spectroscopy reveal the synergistic mechanism of PLA methanolysis. Oxygen vacancies enhance the electrophilicity of the carbonyl carbon while driving the cleavage of methanol to generate nucleophilic species, which further drives ester bond cleavage. More importantly, the Co/ZnO-RPB exhibits remarkable versatility by effectively depolymerizing other polyester plastics and various real-life polyester wastes. This work offers a valuable guidance to the challenge of waste polyester plastics accumulation.

title: Self-Assembly–Galvanic Replacement Route to Conformal Ag Nanoflower Interfaces for Dendrite-Suppressed Zn Anodes
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Rechargeable aqueous Zn anodes are severely limited by sluggish interfacial kinetics and morphological instability. Herein, we report a simple and vacuum-free self-assembly/galvanic replacement strategy that converts a silver nanoplate dispersion into a conformal Ag nanoflower scaffold on Zn foil (Zn@AgNF). This porous and highly wetting metallic interface provides continuous electron-transport pathways and a favorable interfacial environment for Zn nucleation, thereby promoting more uniform Zn deposition and improved interfacial kinetics. Ex situ morphological observations suggest a progressive deposition evolution toward compact Zn deposits with reduced surface oxidation. Symmetric cells exhibit reduced nucleation and growth overpotentials, narrow voltage hysteresis across a wide current-density range, and stable cycling at 10 mA cm–2. In rechargeable Zn–air full cells, Zn@AgNF decreases round-trip polarization and stabilizes interfacial impedance, while improving the full-cell Coulombic efficiency and cycling endurance under the tested conditions (5 mA cm–2 and 1 mAh cm–2). These advantages are maintained in gel electrolytes, in which the cells tolerate repeated bending up to 180°. This work demonstrates a simple solution-based interfacial engineering strategy for improving Zn deposition stability in aqueous Zn-based energy-storage systems.

title: Dynamic Network Engineering of Soy Protein-Based Ionic Hydrogels via Freeze-Locking and Metal Coordination for Intelligent Human–Machine Interaction
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The simultaneous achievement of high ionic conductivity and mechanical robustness remains a fundamental challenge for conductive hydrogels, as excessive ionic species often disrupt polymer networks and compromise structural integrity. Herein, a dynamic network engineering strategy integrating PVA freeze-locking, reversible Fe3+ coordination, and ionic conduction is developed to construct a robust ionically conductive hydrogel (IL-PPM0.1-Fe) for intelligent wearable electronics. The freeze-locked PVA crystalline domains establish a rigid physical framework, while reversible Fe3+–MSPI coordination interactions contribute to network reinforcement and energy dissipation. Meanwhile, the incorporation of VBIMBr introduces imidazolium-containing ionic species into the hydrogel system. The resulting hydrogel achieves a tensile strength of approximately 1.5 MPa, a fracture strain of 673%, and an ionic conductivity of 16.2 S/m, while maintaining mechanical integrity over 500 tensile loading–unloading cycles at 100% strain. The sensor exhibits a strain sensing range of 1–500% (GF = 2.14), a pressure sensitivity of 0.21 kPa–1 at 0–1 kPa, and rapid response and recovery times of 230 and 192 ms, respectively. Furthermore, the hydrogel enables human motion monitoring, handwriting recognition, and proof-of-concept Morse-code-based human–machine interaction. This work demonstrates a promising strategy for combining mechanical robustness, ionic conduction, and multifunctional sensing in wearable electronics.

title: Revealing Cu–Mn Electronic Structure in Activated CuMn/Al2O3 Catalyst By Decoupling of Overlapping X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy Spectra
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Mn-promoted Cu-based catalysts demonstrate high efficiency and stability in various chemical processes, including methanol synthesis. XPS investigations of catalytic reactions and active catalytic centers in Cu–Mn-based catalysts face certain problems: it is challenging to determine the Mn oxidation state because of the strong overlap of Cu and Mn photoelectron and Auger spectra. In this study, a strict background subtraction based on a comprehensive set of standard samples as a reference was applied to separate the net Mn photoelectron spectra from the overlapping Cu signals, which reveals the Mn oxidation state with accurate quantitative analysis. Together with XAS, XRD, and HRTEM evidence, the results jointly support a strong Cu–Mn interaction and changes in their electronic states in the CuMn/Al2O3 catalyst during activation and passivation, providing new insights into the nature of the catalytic centers.

title: Biodegradable Periodic Mesoporous Organosilica Nanoparticles for Enhanced Rifampicin Activity Against Multidrug-Resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Its Biofilm
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Multidrug-resistant (MDR) and biofilm-associated bacterial infections are increasingly prevalent in healthcare settings, and they create a serious global health problem by increasing the morbidity and mortality rates. Nanomaterial-based alternative therapeutic approaches have therefore been widely explored as potential strategies for improving the treatment of MDR infections. Here, we report a drug delivery system based on biocompatible and biodegradable surface-engineered periodic mesoporous organosilica nanoparticles (nanoPMOs), designed to enhance the antibacterial and antibiofilm efficiency of the antibiotic rifampicin against the high-priority MDR Gram-negative pathogenic bacterium, Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Mannose functionalization appeared to improve the association of the nanoPMOs with bacterial cells and biofilms, while the acid-cleavable imine linkages enabled faster nanoparticle degradation and rifampicin release under acidic conditions. Compared with free rifampicin, the rifampicin-loaded nanoPMOs effectively killed planktonic bacteria and reduced the biomass of preformed biofilms under the tested in vitro conditions. The rifampicin-loaded nanoPMO formulations also showed low nonspecific cytotoxicity and hemolytic activity at the concentrations examined.

title: Terminal Ligand Engineering of Clover‐Shaped Windows in Ligand‐Driven Local Pore‐Space‐Partitioned MOFs for Stepwise Enhancement of Propylene/Ethylene Separation
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Ethylene (C 2 H 4 ) and propylene (C 3 H 6 ) are core chemical feedstocks, and high‐purity products are critical for downstream polymer production. However, existing adsorbents generally suffer from poor compatibility between pores and target gas molecules. Herein, a ligand‐driven pore space partition strategy was proposed, whereby a cage‐like metal‒organic framework (JLU‐MOF113) was constructed through the self‐assembly of a benzothiadiazole‐functionalized ligand and trinuclear iron cluster. In the framework, the oriented thiadiazole rings on the ligands enable local pore space partition, forming clover‐shaped ultramicroporous windows. Taking JLU‐MOF113 as the parent framework, 1,2,4‐triazole (trz) and tetrazole (taz) were successfully introduced to replace coordinated H 2 O based on terminal ligand engineering. While further blocking the pore windows, the pore environment was optimized, resulting in the preparation of isostructural JLU‐MOF114/115. Through such stepwise regulation, the microenvironment of local pores in MOFs was successfully tailored, enabling a stepwise enhancement in separation selectivity for C 3 H 6 /C 2 H 4 mixtures. Among them, JLU‐MOF115 exhibits excellent selectivity that surpasses many known MOFs and can separate 73.8 L/kg −1 of C 2 H 4 with a purity of 99.95% from equimolar C 3 H 6 /C 2 H 4 mixtures. This work enriches MOFs with locally partitioned pore characteristics and provides a novel design strategy for the improvement of gas separation performance in MOFs.

title: Efficient Chirality Transfer Enables Amplified Circularly Polarized Luminescence in Chiral Metal Halides Hybrid Structures
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Chiral organic‐inorganic hybrid metal halides have aroused considerable interest for chiroptical applications. However, developing effective structural design strategies and elucidating the underlying chirality transfer mechanisms remain challenging. Herein, utilizing a structure‐directing strategy, two pairs of enantiomeric hybrid manganese chlorides including one‐dimensional (1D) structures [ R ‐/ S ‐(C 6 H 11 NO 2 ) 3 Mn]·[MnCl 4 ] (denoted as P ‐/ M ‐PCA‐2Mn) and R ‐/ S ‐(C 6 H 11 NO 2 )MnCl 2 (denoted as P ‐/ M ‐PCA‐Mn) were synthesized based on the chiral ligands ( R / S )‐(‐/+)‐piperidine‐3‐carboxylic acid (( R / S )‐(‐/+)‐C 6 H 12 ClNO 2 ). This approach also demonstrates generality and can be extended to systems incorporating different ligands. Magnetic susceptibility measurements revealed that antiferromagnetic spin arrangement may contribute to the 7‐fold emission efficiency enhancement in P ‐PCA‐Mn. Furthermore, the luminescent dissymmetry factor | g lum | value increased from 1.3 × 10 −3 in P ‐PCA‐2Mn to 4.2 × 10 −2 in P ‐PCA‐Mn, which is associated with stronger intramolecular hydrogen‐bonding interactions, more pronounced structural distortion, and an enhanced magnetic transition dipole moment, collectively suggesting their potential contributions to the improved circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) performance. Through integration with liquid crystals, stepwise CPL amplification was achieved, elevating | g lum | to the 10 −1 order of magnitude, which exhibits the enantioselectivity of asymmetric photopolymerization. This work confirms the effectiveness of a structure‐directing strategy in boosting both luminescence efficiency and chirality transfer in chiral hybrid metal halides, and presents a novel and efficient platform for regulating CPL properties.

title: Two-Stage Machine Learning-Assisted Multiplex Catecholamine Quantification in Artificial Urine on a Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering Paper
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Catecholamines, including dopamine, epinephrine, and norepinephrine, are important biomarkers of neurological and neuroendocrine disorders. However, their simultaneous quantification in body fluids remains challenging because of their similar molecular structures, which produce highly overlapping Raman spectroscopic signatures. Here, we develop an integrated platform combining an iron-nitrilotriacetic acid (NTA-Fe)-functionalized surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) paper with a two-stage machine learning pipeline for catecholamine quantification in artificial urine. The SERS paper enables rapid drop-and-measure detection, achieving limits of detection of 7.18, 9.01, and 6.80 μM for dopamine, epinephrine, and norepinephrine in artificial urine, respectively. For samples with unknown compositions, the pipeline first classifies the catecholamines present (92.19% group-level accuracy) and then quantifies single-component samples via intensity-ratio calibration and mixtures via trained partial least squares regression models (global root-mean-square error: 2.27 μM). This work establishes a functionalized SERS paper platform coupled with machine learning as a proof of concept for the identification and quantitative analysis of structurally similar metabolites in complex mixtures.

title: Catalytic Manganese Ferrite Nanoparticles Improve Therapeutic Response in Glioblastoma Spheroids through Hypoxia Mitigation
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Glioblastoma (GBM) is an aggressive primary brain tumor characterized by treatment resistance, high recurrence rate, and dismal survival, features influenced by tumor hypoxia, a clinically well-established driver of radio- and chemoresistance. Manganese ferrite nanoparticles possess catalase-like activity capable of generating oxygen from tumor-endogenous hydrogen peroxide, offering a strategy to alleviate tumor hypoxia and re-sensitize GBM cells to chemotherapy. In this study, two manganese ferrite compositions (Mn2FeO4 and MnFe2O4) were synthesized using flame spray pyrolysis, characterized, and evaluated for their ability to reduce hypoxia. Nanoparticle internalization and distribution were confirmed in both patient-derived ZH757 and commercial U87MG GBM spheroid models. Both ferrite formulations decreased the hypoxic cell fraction in GBM spheroids after 17 days, without inducing cytotoxicity in normal fibroblasts. Therapeutic in vitro efficacy was assessed on the previously established GliaMimic treatment evaluation platform, which longitudinally monitors tumor progression during a 17-day in vitro treatment regimen of single-fraction radiation (4 Gy) plus multicycle temozolamide (10, 50, 100 μM TMZ) followed by a treatment-free interval. Nanoparticle-treated tumor spheroids exhibited in combination with radio- and chemotherapy enhanced early cytotoxicity and reduced viability and metabolic activity at the end of treatment, compared to the radiation plus TMZ control alone, with treatment benefits generally becoming more pronounced at higher TMZ doses. Notably, after treatment cessation, nanoparticle-treated groups displayed lower post-treatment progression, likely indicating sustained post-treatment efficacy. These findings advance the mechanistic understanding of catalytic nanoparticle-mediated tumor oxygenation, providing a crucial in vitro foundation for its application as an adjuvant strategy to improve therapeutic efficacy in GBM.
