title: Localized High-Concentration Electrolyte with Nonfluorinated Diluent for Wide-Temperature Sodium-Ion Batteries
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Localized high-concentration electrolytes (LHCEs) have been extensively investigated to improve rechargeable battery performance, yet most rely on costly fluorinated diluents. Herein, we develop a 1M LHCE using toluene as nonfluorinated and low-cost diluent for wide-temperature sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). The 1M LHCE features a compressed solvation structure and preserved ion-transport pathways, enabling the antimonene alloy anode to deliver stable capacities of 555.2 mAh g–1 over 600 cycles at 25 °C and 573.2 and 512.3 mAh g–1 at 50 and –20 °C, respectively. Na3V2(PO4)3//antimonene full cells further demonstrate stable operation under 50 and –20 °C. Mechanistic investigations reveal that the 1M LHCE forms an adaptive solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) that dynamically regulates composition and thickness, which becomes thicker and more organic-rich after sodiation but thinner and more inorganic-rich after desodiation. Such “breathable” SEI effectively accommodates large volume changes and ensures efficient Na+ transport. This work provides a rational electrolyte design strategy for wide-temperature SIBs.

title: Interfacial State‐Perturbed Triplet Energy Transfer in Dye‐Sensitized Upconversion Nanoparticles for Early HIV Diagnosis
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Early diagnosis of HIV infection is pivotal for curbing AIDS progression and enabling timely therapeutic interventions. However, current immunoassays remain constrained by inadequate sensitivity for detecting trace levels of the HIV‐1 p24 antigen during the seroconversion window period. In this study, we discover that subtle perturbations in the interfacial binding state of a carboxylated near‐infrared dye, Cypate, on sub‐7 nm NaGdF 4 :Yb 3+ /Er 3+ upconversion nanoparticles (UCNPs) dramatically modulate triplet energy transfer (TET) efficiency, resulting in a remarkable upconversion luminescence (UCL) response with a signal‐to‐background ratio as high as 375. By leveraging this interfacial state‐perturbed TET as a signal transduction model, we further develop a TET‐sensitized UCL immunosorbent assay (TET‐ULISA) for HIV‐1 p24 antigen detection. In this platform, the target p24 triggers alkaline phosphatase (ALP) to generate phosphate ions, which competitively displace Cypate from the UCNP surface, disrupting TET and producing a dramatic UCL response. The resulting TET‐ULISA exhibits high sensitivity for p24 antigen with a limit of detection as low as 112 fg mL −1 , representing an 860‐fold improvement over the corresponding ALP‐based method by employing the identical immunoassay steps, thus enabling early HIV diagnosis within the critical serological window period.

title: Full‐Process Synergistic Optimization of Buried Interfaces via Molecule‐Assisted Co‐Assembly for Inverted Perovskite Solar Cells
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Self‐assembled monolayers (SAMs) are promising hole‐selective contacts for inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs), yet insufficient substrate anchoring and weak buried‐interface interactions limit device efficiency and stability. Here, we report a co‐assembled SAM (Co‐SAM) strategy that enables full‐process synergistic optimization of the perovskite buried interface by introducing tris(4‐fluorophenyl)phosphine oxide (TFPPO) into SAMs. TFPPO suppresses SAM aggregation in solution via its strongly polar P═O group and anchors onto NiO x , with its 4‐fluorophenyl arms proposed to interact with unanchored hydroxyl groups of SAMs to strengthen anchoring and refine their arrangement. Furthermore, TFPPO optimizes the interfacial chemical states while serving as an effective template to direct high‐quality perovskite crystal growth. Consequently, inverted PSCs based on the regulated SAMs achieve power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) of 26.98% (stabilized PCE of 26.40%) and 20.65% for normal‐bandgap (1.54 eV) and wide‐bandgap (1.78 eV) devices, respectively. Moreover, a representative Co‐SAM‐modified device retains 97% of its initial efficiency after 1856 h of maximum power point tracking (ISOS‐L‐1), and Co‐SAM‐modified devices retain 92.36% of their initial efficiency after 2408 h of continuous aging at 65°C (ISOS‐D‐2).

title: Exploring enhanced self-esteem reactivity in response to social prediction errors in adolescence
source: Scientific community and society : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Self-esteem is a cornerstone of mental health across the lifespan. Throughout life, but particularly during adolescence, self-esteem is shaped by social appraisals. Previous work in adults has shown that momentary fluctuations in self-esteem are explained not only by whether we are liked by others but also by whether we are liked more or less than expected (social prediction errors). Here, we examine age-related differences in how social experiences shape self-esteem in 141 participants aged 10-40 years using an experimental social evaluation task and ecological momentary assessment. In the experiment, self-esteem reactivity to unexpected social feedback follows a non-linear age-related pattern, peaking in late adolescence. In daily life, self-esteem reactivity to perceived pleasantness of social interaction and naturalistic social prediction errors is stronger in younger participants. Individual differences in experimental and daily-life self-esteem reactivity are associated, highlighting heightened self-esteem malleability during adolescence.

title: CD300LD drives osteoclastogenesis and inflammatory bone loss by sensing cholesterol and activating FES SYK STAT3
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Osteoclasts are essential for bone remodeling and homeostasis. Their excessive activation drives pathological bone loss disorders such as periodontitis and arthritis. Current osteoclast-inhibiting therapies are limited by adverse effects and poor specificity, underscoring the importance to identify new regulators of osteoclastogenesis. Here, we conducted a pooled CRISPR–Cas9 screen targeting cluster of differentiation (CD) genes to uncover novel modulators of osteoclast differentiation and identified CD300LD, a single-pass transmembrane protein, as a potent driver of osteoclastogenesis. Cd300ld deletion impaired osteoclastogenesis in cell line and primary bone-marrow–derived macrophages. In vivo, myeloid-specific Cd300ld knockout mice exhibited significantly reduced alveolar bone loss and osteoclast numbers in experimental periodontitis, as well as attenuated joint inflammation and bone erosion in arthritis models, whereas bone remodeling during skeletal development remained unaltered. Mechanistically, cholesterol acts as extracellular activator for CD300LD to activate osteoclastogenesis. Cd300ld deficiency intracellularly inhibited phosphorylation of FES, SYK, and STAT3. Consistently, loss of Fes, Syk or Stat3 recapitulated the Cd300ld-deficient phenotypes, establishing a CD300LD–FES–SYK–STAT3 signaling axis essential for osteoclast differentiation. Together, these findings identify CD300LD as a critical, previously unrecognized driver of osteoclastogenesis and highlight it as a promising therapeutic target for inflammatory bone loss.

title: Iron supplementation in iron-deficient Kenyan infants: a randomised controlled trial of vaccine immunogenicity
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Iron deficiency is common in early infancy, but whether supplementation improves vaccine immunogenicity is uncertain. In this randomised, double-blind trial in coastal Kenya (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04744818), 288 breastfed, iron-deficient infants aged six weeks received daily oral iron (3 mg/kg/day; n = 143) or control (n = 145) until 24 weeks during routine immunisation; follow-up continued to 52 weeks. Primary outcomes were diphtheria and pertussis IgG responses during supplementation. Secondary outcomes were antibody responses to oral and inactivated poliovirus, Haemophilus influenzae type b, tetanus, hepatitis B, and 10-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccine. Vaccines were given at 6, 10 and 14 weeks. Iron supplementation reduced iron deficiency (OR 0.49, 95% CI 0.34–0.71; p

title: Mechanistic insights into intracellular phase separation and maturation of FUS LC revealed by in-cell NMR
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Fused in sarcoma (FUS) forms dynamic biomolecular condensates through phase separation, a process associated with stress responses and neurodegenerative diseases. Here, we use in-cell NMR spectroscopy to directly observe condensate formation of the FUS low-complexity (LC) domain in living cells. We identify a two-step process: initial droplet formation followed by time-dependent maturation, characterized by reduced internal mobility. Deletion mutant analysis reveals that while initial condensate formation is driven by collective multivalent interactions, the reversible amyloid core (RAC) region is essential for the subsequent maturation. Intracellular droplets form at concentrations well below the in vitro threshold, which cannot be explained by macromolecular crowding alone. Notably, droplet formation is suppressed under nutrient starvation, suggesting that ATP-dependent cellular activities indirectly promote FUS condensation. These findings demonstrate that the metabolically active intracellular environment modulates FUS condensate behavior, providing mechanistic insights into early events in pathological aggregation and establishing a general framework for studying condensates in cells.

title: Evolutionary Neuroskeletal Biology
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Nerves reach deep into bone, where they influence how the skeleton grows, remodels, and repairs. Yet almost everything we know about neuroskeletal biology comes from mice and humans. The influence of nerves on bone is largely unknown in other vertebrates, whose physiology differs markedly from that of mammals: birds mobilize a fifth of their skeletal minerals to build each eggshell, some lizards regrow their tails, salamanders cannot regenerate after denervation, and fish maintain their skeleton without bone cells. In this Perspective, we outline a comparative framework for understanding bone innervation and detail what this framework can offer fields ranging from evolution and paleontology to medicine.

title: Tailoring the Na + Transport Microenvironment With an Anion‐Capturing Interface Enables Low‐Temperature, Fast‐Charging Sodium‐Ion Batteries
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Na + desolvation and diffusion across the solid‐electrolyte interface (SEI) are two bottlenecks to fast charging at low temperatures in hard‐carbon sodium‐ion batteries. Here, we design an anion‐capturing interface that provides a customized interfacial environment to enhance interfacial dynamics at low temperatures. We demonstrate that phosphate can promote the formation of a homogeneous inorganic SEI by inducing anion enrichment near the inner Helmholtz plane. The phosphorus‐rich interface exhibits multiple benefits, including the formation of a built‐in electric field and a reduced energy barrier for Na + interphase diffusion. The hard carbon–phosphate interface (NP‐HC) anode maintains a capacity of 183.6 mAh g −1 at 0.5 A g −1 (−30°C). The pouch cell utilizing the NP‐HC anode achieves a 90.2% capacity retention after 1000 cycles at a 2 C rate. Even so, NP‐HC pouch cells can operate stably even at temperatures as low as −40°C, indicating their potential to enhance the performance of sodium‐ion batteries under harsh conditions.

title: Preventing data leakage in neural decoding
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Neural decoding is a widely-used machine learning technique for investigating how behavior, perception and cognition are represented in neural activity. However without careful application data leakage can occur, where information from the test set contaminates the training set, leading to biased estimates of decoding performance and potentially invalidating biological conclusions. Here we show that leakage can be introduced in neural decoding studies by common supervised and unsupervised preprocessing steps, including dimensionality reduction. We reveal that in some cases leakage can paradoxically decrease decoding performance relative to unbiased estimates, and we provide theoretical analyses explaining how this occurs. We also show that, for autocorrelated neural time series, randomized k-fold cross-validation can dramatically overstate decoding performance. Based on these findings, we provide detailed recommendations for avoiding data leakage in neural decoding.

title: Hepatokine AGP2 mediates physical exercise-induced bone augmentation through liver-bone signaling communication
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Physical exercise promotes bone health. However, its underlying mechanisms remain incompletely elucidated. Here, we identified the hepatokine AGP2 as an osteoanabolic mediator of exercise. Exercise increases circulating AGP2 levels in mice and humans. Hepatocyte-specific Agp2 knockout substantially attenuates exercise-induced bone formation, whereas hepatic AGP2 overexpression prevents bone loss in ovariectomized mice. Mechanistically, exercise-induced lactate promotes hepatic Agp2 expression through histone H3K14 lactylation. Secreted AGP2 directly binds the Wnt co-receptor LRP5, activates Wnt/β-catenin signaling, promotes osteoblast differentiation, and suppresses osteoclast activity. Recombinant AGP2 administration also alleviates bone loss in mouse models of osteoporosis. Thus, these findings delineate a critical role of liver-bone crosstalk in mediating the beneficial effects of exercise on bone metabolism, highlighting AGP2 as a key mediator in exercise-induced bone anabolism and suggesting AGP2 as a potential therapeutic target for the treatment of metabolic bone disorders.

title: A small RNA regulates iron homeostasis and host mucus colonization in Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Symbiotic bacteria in the human intestinal microbiota provide many pivotal functions to human health and occupy distinct biogeographic niches within the gut. Yet the molecular basis underlying niche-specific colonization remains poorly defined. To address this, we conducted a time-resolved dual RNA-seq experiment to simultaneously monitor the transcriptional co-adaptations of human commensal Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron and human gut epithelial cells in a hypoxic, mucus-producing, epithelial co-culture system. Comparative transcriptomic analysis of mucus-associated versus supernatant Bacteroides populations unveiled small RNAs (sRNAs) that are differentially regulated between spatially segregated subpopulations. Among these, we identified IroR as a key sRNA that facilitates B. thetaiotaomicron adaptation to iron limitation and host glycan availability, partly by modulating expression of capsule-associated surface states. This work provides new insights into the spatiotemporal dynamics of gut colonization and underscores a previously underappreciated role for bacterial sRNAs in shaping mutualistic interactions between the human microbiota and the gut epithelium.

title: Electrochemical PVC Recycling Unlocks Efficient Ring‐Closure Toward Amine‐Bearing Ketene Acetals as Novel Monomers for Poly(Amino Ester) Synthesis
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT A paired electrochemical synthetic strategy for the upcycling of poly(vinyl chloride) (PVC) is reported, enabling simultaneous cathodic dechlorination of the polymer backbone and anodic formation of cyclic halo acetals (CHAs) as monomer precursors. The process channels liberated chloride into cyclic acetal structures, which are converted into cyclic ketene acetals and subsequently polymerized via radical ring‐opening polymerization (rROP) to access degradable polyester and poly(amino ester) materials. Electrochemical cyclization unlocks the synthesis of previously unavailable nitrogen‐containing cyclic ketene acetal monomers in remarkably high yields. Combined experimental and computational studies reveal a pronounced heteroatom effect on cyclization efficiency, attributed to conformational preorganization induced by an increasing gauche effect upon ether and amide incorporation. A nitrogen‐containing ketene acetal monomer was polymerized and copolymerized with established ketene acetals, affording new functional, biodegradable polymer materials. Successful copolymerization with methyl acrylate demonstrates the incorporation of hydrolysable moieties into otherwise persistent olefinic materials. Importantly, cathodic PVC dechlorination proceeds independently of the anodic transformation, highlighting the broad applicability of this paired‐electrolysis strategy in an undivided cell. Overall, this work establishes a versatile electrochemical PVC recycling process while simultaneously generating previously inaccessible monomer building blocks for biodegradable polymer synthesis.

title: Spatial Confinement Enables In Situ Growth of the Nano-Sn@Sn3(PO4)2 Anode for Sodium-Ion Batteries
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Nanoarchitecturing improves capacity utilization and mitigates mechanical stress of Sn anodes for elevated energy density sodium-ion batteries (SIBs), yet substantial surface energy induces nanoparticle aggregation. Traditional heterotopic coatings cannot sustain long-term mechanical confinement upon repeated volume variation of Sn. Herein, we propose a dealloying-induced phase transformation and spatial confinement strategy to in situ construct a robust Sn3(PO4)2 coating on Sn nanoparticles. Sn3(PO4)2 provides spatial confinement for the homogeneously dispersed Sn nanoparticles, while the nano-Sn (∼20 nm) within the Sn3(PO4)2 framework effectively alleviates mechanical stress and suppresses volume expansion. Consequently, Sn@Sn3(PO4)2 exhibits attractive structural integrity and electrochemical performance, with a reversible capacity of 772 mAh g–1, 83% capacity retention after 3600 cycles, and 583 mAh g–1 at 5 A g–1. Moreover, the Sn@Sn3(PO4)2||Na3V2(PO4)3 full cell delivers a favorable cycling stability and rate performance. This in situ reconstruction strategy guides electrode surface engineering and facilitates the application of Sn-based anodes in future SIBs.

title: Hydroxyl‐Orchestrated Crystallization and Affinity Sites in Covalent Organic Framework Membranes for One‐Step Selective Ternary Ion Separation
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT One‐step selective separation of multiple coexisting ions from complex aqueous media remains a formidable challenge. Here we report hydroxyl‐orchestrated covalent organic framework (COF) membranes that couple framework crystallization with hydrazone‐carbonyl pocket‐site formation, enabling ternary separation of Cs + , Sr 2+ and UO 2 2+ in a single step. Hydroxyl substitution decelerates interfacial polymerization while reinforcing intralayer hydrogen bonding to stabilize ordered frameworks, yielding high crystallinity. Concurrently, hydroxyl‐orchestrated enol‐imine to keto‐enamine tautomerization promotes the formation of hydrazone‐carbonyl pocket sites for selective UO 2 2+ chelation. The optimized membrane achieves a UO2 2+ uptake of 336 mg g −1 and a Cs + permeation flux of 0.26 mol m −2 h −1 , while exhibiting suppressed Sr 2+ permeation. Under ternary conditions, Cs + /Sr 2+ and Cs + /UO 2 2+ separation factors reach 81.5 and 326.9, with stable performance over repeated cycles. These findings establish hydroxyl‐orchestrated crystallization and pocket‐site engineering as a powerful approach for multi‐component ion separations.

title: Single-Molecule DNA Sequencing with Nanopores
source: Chemical Reviews: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract DNA sequencing is indispensable in healthcare, agriculture, environmental protection, and understanding of biology. DNA sequencing with nanopores uses a unique principle where individual DNA strands are threaded through a ring-like nanopore, which acts as a read head to electronically detect the bases. Due to the simple principle, nanopores enable sequencing at previously unachieved speeds and read lengths as well as direct sensing of epigenetically modified bases. The electrical nature also allows highly portable devices to be used in the clinic or the field. This review places DNA nanopore sequencing within the context of other DNA sequencing technologies and explains its functional principle and the essential components of commercial nanopore sequencing platforms. The advantages of nanopore sequencing are demonstrated with relevant case studies, and nanopore sequencing is compared to other technologies in terms of sequencing parameters such as read length, throughput, cost per base, and accuracy. A brief outlook discusses how the current shortcomings of nanopore sequencing can be addressed with future advances.

title: Protective effect of seasonal vaccines against human-derived bovine H5N1 influenza virus
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Since early 2024, highly pathogenic avian influenza H5N1 virus (clade 2.3.4.4b) has caused outbreaks in U.S. dairy cattle, infecting other mammals including humans. Here, we evaluate the protective efficacy of two commercially available seasonal influenza vaccines against a human-derived bovine H5N1 isolate, A/Texas/37/2024, in influenza-naïve female ferrets. All unvaccinated ferrets develop severe disease and succumb to infection or meet humane euthanasia criteria. Immunisation with an inactivated influenza vaccine reduces viral titres in multiple respiratory and extrapulmonary tissues and delays disease progression but does not prevent fatal outcomes. By contrast, five of six ferrets immunised with a live attenuated influenza vaccine survive challenge and show more effective control of viral replication in the nasal mucosa. Live attenuated vaccination induces stronger T-cell responses, while the absence of detectable neutralising activity against the challenge virus suggests that cellular immunity, rather than neutralising antibodies, may contribute to protection. These findings demonstrate that seasonal live attenuated influenza vaccination can provide cross-protection against lethal infection with an antigenically distinct bovine-derived H5N1 virus, potentially through cellular immune responses in the respiratory tract.

title: Integration of Mott neurons and spintronic memories for event-driven spiking neural networks
source: Nature Nanotechnology
abstract:
Abstract
                  Spiking neural networks provide energy-efficient, event-driven computing, but separating volatile neuronal dynamics from non-volatile memory imposes costly signal transfer and conversion. Here we demonstrate a hybrid compute-and-store core that directly integrates thermally coupled vanadium dioxide Mott leaky integrate-and-fire neurons to spintronic memory. The neurons require no external resistive or capacitive elements for temporal integration and write their output spikes into either domain-wall racetracks or spin–orbit torque magnetic tunnel junctions without amplifiers or analogue-to-digital converters. In racetracks, spike number and amplitude are converted into domain-wall displacement, spatially preserving temporal histories and enabling up to six spikes per processing cycle. Distinct spike trains generated from encoded input patterns produce separable non-volatile states, demonstrating event-based processing and read-out. A network model parameterized by experimental leaky integrate-and-fire neuron dynamics achieves 96.3% accuracy on MNIST digit recognition. Functional coupling of a 500-nm leaky integrate-and-fire neuron to a 100-nm spin–orbit torque magnetic tunnel junction further establishes nanoscale compatibility. The demonstrated compute-and-store core consumes 51.9 nJ per spike-to-memory conversion, with sub-200-nm vanadium dioxide devices indicating operation near 200 pJ, offering a scalable route towards dense, low-power edge neuromorphic systems for real-time sensory processing.

title: Skeletal muscle proteomics reveals metabolic phenotype–specific adaptations to exercise training in health, obesity, and type 2 diabetes
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Exercise training improves metabolic health, including whole-body insulin sensitivity, yet the molecular mechanisms remain incompletely understood. We applied proteomics and phosphoproteomics to skeletal muscle biopsies from lean men, and men with obesity or type 2 diabetes (T2D), obtained before and after 8 weeks of high-intensity interval training (HIIT) under basal and insulin-stimulated conditions. Before HIIT, protein expression showed a stepwise progression from lean to obesity to T2D. HIIT induced more pronounced proteomic remodeling in obesity and T2D compared with lean men, characterized by increased mitochondrial and decreased proteasomal contents. Phosphoproteomic responses were diagnosis dependent, revealing distinct insulin signaling adaptations. Mechanistically, AMP-activated protein kinase γ2 (AMPKγ2) emerged as a prominent HIIT-regulated protein, exhibiting increased incorporation into AMPKα2β2 complexes across all phenotypes, and AMPKγ2 overexpression in human myotubes increased basal glucose oxidation. These findings elucidate molecular pathways underlying exercise-induced insulin sensitization and suggest AMPKγ2 as a candidate regulator for exercise-induced metabolic adaptation.

title: Cryo-EM reveals a transmembrane allosteric site and activation mechanism for the SERCA calcium pump
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Impaired sarco-endoplasmic reticulum Ca
                    2+
                    -ATPase (SERCA) activity contributes to defective calcium handling and cellular dysfunction in cardiovascular and metabolic diseases, yet the structural basis of small-molecule SERCA activation has remained unknown. SERCA is a ubiquitous P-type ATPase that restores cytosolic Ca
                    2+
                    to the sarco-endoplasmic reticulum and is essential for cardiac Ca
                    2+
                    cycling and cellular energy homeostasis. Here, we used cryogenic electron microscopy to define how two chemically distinct activators, CDN1163 and UM-52, enhance SERCA function. Structures at 2.6 Å and 3.1 Å resolution show that both compounds bind the same previously unrecognized activation hotspot in the transmembrane domain, a shallow groove formed by helices M3 and M4 and capped by M1. Despite limited chemical similarity, both activators share conserved interactions with Ser265 and Trp272 and stimulate Ca
                    2+
                    -dependent ATPase activity. Activator binding promotes a catalytically competent, calcium-bound E1-like conformation of SERCA that may involve altered protein-lipid interactions. These findings establish a structural framework for rational design of potent next-generation SERCA activators.

title: Multimodal motion and behavior switching of multistable ciliary walkers
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: The collective motion of arrays of cilia—tiny, hairlike protrusions—drives the locomotion of numerous microorganisms, enabling multimodal motion and switching between gaits to navigate complex environments. Inspired by this multimodal motion, we introduce multistable soft walkers with millimeter-scale flexible cilia that buckle under the walkers weight, coupling multistability and actuation within a single physical mechanism. When placed on a vibrating surface, the propulsion direction of ciliary walkers is selected through the buckled states of their cilia, allowing multimodal motion and switching between modes in response to perturbations. We first show that bimodal walkers with left-right symmetric cilia can reverse direction upon encountering obstacles. Next, we demonstrate that walkers with isotropic cilia exhibit both translational and rotational motion and switch between them in response to environmental interactions. At increasing densities, swarms of such walkers collectively transition from predominantly spinning to translational motion. Last, we show that the shape, placement, and number of cilia controls the modes of motion of the walkers. Our results establish a rational, physically grounded strategy for designing minimalist soft robots where complex behaviors emerge from feedback between internal mechanical states and environmental interactions, laying the foundation for soft robotic collectives that operate without onboard sensing or centralized control.

title: Ultra-generalized hologram synthesis via domain-adaptive wavefront learning
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Deep learning–based computer-generated holography is essential for creating lifelike three-dimensional (3D) visuals in extended reality and immersive human-digital interaction. However, current data-driven approaches predominantly rely on a 3D-solution search strategy that couples scene representation with physical parameters. This paradigm leads to physical overfitting, restricting models to fixed wavelengths and depths and preventing generalization across diverse 3D data formats. Here, we report a 2D-solution search technique, wavefront-aware neural encoding (WNE). This method is a universal framework that overcomes these limitations via domain-adaptive wavefront learning. By compensating for feature distribution shifts induced by varying data formats and physical parameters, WNE maps various wavefronts into a unified feature domain compatible with a frozen, pretrained encoder. This mechanism enables ultra-generalized hologram synthesis: A single pretrained network can encode high-fidelity phase-only holograms for diverse 3D representations, from conventional layer-based data to emerging Gaussian splatting. Outperforming previous analytical and neural encoding methods in image quality, WNE establishes a robust, plug-and-play engine for diverse holographic applications.

title: Evolution of trans-regulatory architecture and gene expression dosage compensation after genome duplication
