title: Strengthening Metal–Oxygen Bonds via Ionicity–Covalency Asymmetric Connection: 4f Electronic Configuration Effect
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Precise control over the characteristics of metal–oxygen (M–O) bonds by regulating the electron redistribution between the metal and oxygen under perturbation conditions is crucial for maintaining the structural stability of transition-metal oxides. However, its development has always been hindered by the strong coupling between orbital hybridization and charge localization. Herein, by leveraging the strong ionicity of the Ce–O bonds in CeO2, we constructed an ionicity–covalency asymmetric bonding network, in which the ionic Ce–O is atomically coupled with the covalent M–O (M = Ni/Co). The reduced Ce–O coordination in this special structure weakens the O 2p → Ce 4f charge transfer and further elevates the ionic character of Ce–O bonds, thereby activating the reversible 4f electronic configuration transition. Critically, this configuration undergoes reversible transformation under potential fluctuation, reshaping charge redistribution within the M–O bonding motifs and then suppressing irreversible M–O bond degradation. Harnessing this mechanism enables transition-metal oxides to express a robust framework for the whole structure under repeated redox cycling. Incorporating this resulting CeO2/NiCo2O4, a large-scale alkaline water electrolysis (AWE) stack delivers significantly stable operation for over 350 h at 6 A under a 12-h intermittent experimental protocol. This finding offers a fundamental insight into the dynamic charge distribution in M–O bonds under potential perturbation for universal structural protection.

title: Synthetic Control of Quantum Phases in Organic Conductors: Molecular-Level Disorder Engineering and Pressure-Induced Superconductivity
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Structural randomness is a dominant factor governing electronic properties; however, the intrinsic effects of a disordered potential remain elusive due to the lack of a synthetic platform capable of introducing purely random potentials without carrier doping or altering the fundamental band structure. Here, we demonstrate the synthetic control of superconducting and insulating phases by exploiting the unique conformational flexibility of molecular conductors. Through precise thermodynamic control during crystal growth, we selectively synthesize the structurally ordered superconductor κ-(BEDT-TTF)2Cu[N(CN)2]Br (κ-Br; BEDT-TTF = bis(ethylenedithio)tetrathiafulvalene) and the structurally disordered insulating polymorph, κ″-(BEDT-TTF)2Cu[N(CN)2]Br (κ″-Br), possessing the exact same chemical composition. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations confirm the metastable nature of κ″-Br, showing a packing arrangement of BEDT-TTF molecules and an electronic band structure nearly identical to those of superconducting κ-Br, but featuring a disordered anion layer. Optical conductivity spectra reveal low-energy excitations without a distinct gap, indicating that the insulating behavior originates from disorder-induced carrier localization. Furthermore, κ″-Br undergoes a pressure-induced insulator–superconductor transition, in stark contrast to postsynthetic X-ray irradiation which induced irreversible structural damage. This work represents the first demonstration of synthetic control of an ordered superconductor and a disordered insulator driven solely by orientational disorder in organic conductors. Our study provides new avenues for manipulating strongly correlated electron systems and for investigating the intrinsic effects of randomness, free from carrier doping or structural perturbation of conducting layers.

title: Electrochemical Allylic Carboxylation of Unactivated Alkenes with CO2
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract As both alkenes and CO2 are abundant and easily available feedstocks, carboxylation of alkenes with CO2 represents an attractive and sustainable strategy to synthesize value-added carboxylic acids. Despite substantial advances in carboxylation of π-bonds in alkenes, the carboxylation of C–H bonds in alkenes, which preserves the C═C bond in the synthesis of valuable unsaturated carboxylic acids, remains a longstanding challenge, particularly for unactivated alkenes owing to their intrinsically low reactivity. Herein, we report the first electrochemical allylic carboxylation of unactivated alkenes with CO2, providing a direct and selective approach to hard-to-obtain β,γ-unsaturated carboxylic acids. Moreover, this reaction exhibits a broad substrate scope, good functional group tolerance, and applicability to late-stage diversification. Mechanistic studies indicate that the electrogenerated CO2 radical anion acts both as the carboxylation reagent and the hydrogen-atom abstraction species for the subsequent desaturation process, further uncovering the synthetic utility potential of the CO2 radical anion.

title: Tunable diffusive memristor arrays for neuromorphic temporal computing
source: Nature Materials
abstract: The dynamic behaviour of diffusive memristors enables bio-realistic emulation of artificial neurons and synapses, yet scaling from individual devices to neuromorphic systems remains challenging. Stochasticity in ionic motion and filament evolution limits both the uniformity and tunability of these devices, hindering reliable system-level implementation. Here we present a framework for tailoring the relaxation dynamics of diffusive memristors via intrinsic and extrinsic tuning. Percolation in a thin platinum interfacial layer and grain boundaries in a polycrystalline hafnium oxide matrix spatially confine active metal-ion migration; this guided transport substantially improves device uniformity. Purpose-designed programming protocols enable tuning of relaxation time over two orders of magnitude. A prototype hardware system integrating a 28 × 14 array of tailored diffusive memristors and a memristive system-on-chip implements the hierarchy-of-time-surfaces algorithm, achieving 91.14% recognition accuracy on a downsampled neuromorphic-MNIST dataset. These results demonstrate a scalable approach towards robust and energy-efficient neuromorphic hardware for next-generation artificial intelligence.

title: Micro 3D Printing of Silica Aerogels via Bath‐Mediated In Situ Sol–Gel Reaction
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Silica aerogels are attractive thermally insulating materials owing to their extremely low density and nanoporous silica networks, but their integration into miniaturized devices for thermal management remains limited by the difficulty of patterning fragile aerogel structures at microscale resolution. Here, we report a bath‐mediated in situ sol–gel reaction printing process for microscale 3D printing of silica aerogel architectures. In this strategy, a pre‐hydrolyzed, silanol‐rich precursor solution stabilized in an acidic medium is deposited into a basic bath, where an abrupt pH change triggers instantaneous siloxane condensation and forms silica gel filaments. This pH‐mediated sol–gel printing process enabled the fabrication of silica aerogel structures with filament linewidths as small as 8 µm in single‐layer patterns and approximately 20 µm in multilayer 3D structures. The printed filaments exhibited an interconnected nanoparticle network with a high specific surface area of 988.3 m 2 g −1 , an average pore size of 18.4 nm, and a low thermal conductivity of 0.023 W m −1 K −1 . On microheater device platforms, the printed aerogels provided localized thermal insulation that could be modulated by adjusting the printed architecture. This work provides a route for integrating nanoporous silica aerogels as spatially controlled thermal insulation components in miniaturized thermal management systems.

title: Alloy Engineering of Chiral‐Anomaly Transport Signatures into a Group‐IV Semiconductor
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Integration of chiral transport phenomena into the CMOS platform underlying modern computation has the potential to transform information processing. However, transport signatures associated with the chiral‐anomaly have remained confined largely to low‐symmetry, difficult‐to‐process materials and have been essentially unexplored in conventional CMOS‐compatible semiconductors. Here, we show that dilute carbon alloying drives the group‐IV semiconductor germanium–tin (GeSn) into a distinct magnetotransport regime. Carbon‐alloyed GeSn (CGeSn) films exhibit pronounced negative longitudinal magnetoresistance together with a robust planar Hall effect. The magnetic field, angular, temperature, and composition dependence of these responses follow the transport phenomenology of the chiral‐anomaly and closely mirror that reported for established topological materials. Remarkably, these signatures emerge in a material whose global topological electronic structure is as of yet unexplored, revealing an unexpected transport regime beyond current theoretical descriptions of GeSn‐based alloys. The systematic evolution of this behavior with carbon incorporation demonstrates that material design approaches focused on dilute alloy engineering provide a powerful route to realizing chiral‐anomaly transport signatures in conventional semiconductors. These results establish CGeSn as a CMOS‐compatible platform for exploring emergent chiral transport phenomena and motivate the development of a microscopic theory capable of explaining their origin.

title: Spatially Synchronized Ion‐Electron Transport Enables Millimeter‐Thick Cathodes for Ah‐Level Aqueous Cu‐S Batteries
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Thick conversion electrodes are essential for practical high‐energy aqueous batteries, yet their electrochemical reactions become increasingly heterogeneous when ionic and electronic pathways are spatially decoupled across the electrode depth. Here, sulfated cellulose nanofibrils (SCNFs) and PEDOT:PSS are integrated to construct a nanocellulose‐enabled architecture that synchronizes ionic and electronic transport in millimeter‐thick aqueous Cu‐S cathodes. The SCNF framework directs conformal PEDOT:PSS assembly along continuous nanofibrils, creating collocated electronic pathways and hydrophilic Cu 2+ ‐transport channels within one fibrillar scaffold. Electrochemical analysis, Raman mapping, and X‐ray computed tomography reveal that this integrated network converts localized sulfur conversion into a homogeneous and reversible through‐thickness reaction. Consequently, the optimized cathode retains 98.6% of its capacity after 1000 cycles at 5 A g −1 and delivers an areal capacity exceeding 179 mAh cm −2 at an ultrahigh sulfur loading of 112 mg cm −2 . In a high‐loading pouch‐cell configuration, the optimized cathode further achieves a capacity of approximately 3 Ah. Furthermore, a decoupled Zn‐S configuration design delivers an energy density of 651 Wh kg −1 based on sulfur and zinc active materials. This work establishes spatial synchronization of ionic and electronic transport as a broadly applicable design principle for practical high‐loading conversion electrodes.

title: Chloride‐Induced Microstructure–Covalency Coupling Enables Ultrafine Nanoparticle Exsolution for High‐Performance CO 2 Electrolysis
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient CO 2 electrolysis in solid oxide electrolysis cells (SOECs) requires active cathode catalysts that combine abundant active interfaces, rapid charge transfer, and long‐term structural stability. Perovskite exsolution can generate robust metal nanoparticles (NPs), but achieving a dense population of ultrafine nanocatalysts remains challenging. Here, we report a chloride‐assisted exsolution strategy in Sr 2 Fe 1.3 Ni 0.2 Mo 0.5 O 6‐δ (SFNM)‐based cathodes, demonstrating for the first time that Cl doping links grain‐boundary (GB) engineering with metal–oxygen covalency regulation to direct FeNi NP exsolution. Electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) analysis shows that the SrCl 2 ‐derived molten‐salt flux effect creates a faceted, GB‐rich perovskite morphology, increasing the GB density by approximately 78.9% and providing abundant nucleation sites for exsolution. X‐ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) and theoretical calculations further reveal that Cl substitution attenuates metal–oxygen hybridization, promotes oxygen‐vacancy formation, and facilitates outward segregation of Fe and Ni. This chloride‐triggered dual regulation yields a highly populated FeNi NP surface, accelerating CO 2 electroreduction and lowering polarization resistance. Consequently, the reduced Cl‐doped SFNM cathode (R‐SFNMCl2) achieves 2.73 A cm −2 at 800°C and 1.5 V, while sustaining stable operation for 400 h with only minor degradation. This work establishes a new halogen‐mediated exsolution design paradigm for developing high‐performance SOEC cathode catalysts.

title: Dual Charge Extraction Pathways at Perovskite/Organic Hetero‐Contacts for Optoelectronics
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Charge extraction at the hetero‑contact between perovskites and organic charge‑transport layers (OCTLs) is central to the performance of perovskite optoelectronic devices, yet the microscopic mechanisms governing this process remain insufficiently resolved. Here we indicate a hybrid interfacial state that emerges broadly at perovskite/OCTL hetero‐contacts containing heteroatoms capable of coordinating to surface Pb 2+ sites. Using ultrafast spectroscopy supported by electronic‑structure calculations, we determine the energetic position and temporal evolution of this state and show that it mediates an additional, fast charge‑extraction pathway alongside the conventional valence‑band route. This dual‑pathway mechanism helps overcome interfacial energy barriers and large valence band maximum‐highest occupied molecular orbital (VBM‐HOMO) offsets that typically limit extraction efficiency. Our findings establish a general coordination‑driven origin for hybrid interfacial states and provide design principles for engineering charge‑selective contacts in next‑generation perovskite optoelectronic devices.

title: Impact of helium cooling channels and flow channel inserts on magnetohydrodynamic mixed convection in a liquid metal blanket
source: Nuclear Fusion - latest papers
abstract: On the pathway toward full simulations for a liquid metal blanket, this study extends the work of Chen et al (2022 Nucl. Fusion62 026042) on mixed convection in a full-scale dual coolant lead lithium blanket by considering a more realistic case. In this study, the model incorporates the complex geometry of characteristic sub-components, including helium cooling channels and flow channel inserts (FCIs), to investigate their impacts in several key metrics: (1) Magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) pressure drop, (2) electromagnetic coupling, (3) velocity distribution in both the bulk and gap regions, (4) flow behavior in blanket components, and (5) heat transfer. Based on the MHD-UCAS platform, these multi-region, multiphysics direct numerical simulations are performed on a highly refined mesh of cells under conditions relevant to the fusion reactor: the applied magnetic field of 5 T ( ), the PbLi velocity of 0.1 m s–1 in poloidal ducts ( ), and maximum volumetric heating of 30 MW m–3 ( ). The computational results incorporate the influence of the helium cooling channels and the FCIs on electromagnetic coupling, thereby altering the MHD pressure and flow distribution. Simultaneously, the FCIs divide the flow into bulk and gap regions, where localized reverse flow is observed mainly within the gap regions of the rear poloidal ducts. The anisotropic conductivity introduced by helium channels alters the velocity and temperature distributions, further complicating the MHD flow. In addition, localized hot spots exceeding the design temperature limit are found near the top of the U-turn and in the outlet reduced activation ferritic/martensitic steel walls, suggesting that enhanced cooling is required in these locations.

title: AI-based digital pathology defines spatial border ecosystems in triple-negative breast cancer
source: Science
abstract: The invasive tumor border in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is currently poorly understood. We integrated digital pathology and spatial multi-omics to define border ecosystems in TNBC. AI-based digital pathology identified five border ecosystems, three associated with prognosis. Spatial multi-omics analyses further resolved the spatial niche, molecular mechanisms and clinical relevance of these ecosystems. Immune-infiltrated borders contain a triadic immune niche associated with favorable prognosis and immunotherapy sensitivity. Tumor–stroma borders harbor a MIF + fibroblast exclusion niche that blocks immune infiltration and suppresses T cells function, predicting poor prognosis. Tumor–adipose borders, featured an FLT1 + endothelial niche, promote hypoxia, vascular leakage, and tumor dissemination. Targeting this niche inhibits tumor progression. Collectively, these findings establish a spatial resource that might enable border-directed therapeutic strategies in TNBC.

title: A fast radio burst at redshift 2, three billion years after the Big Bang
source: Science
abstract: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) are millisecond-duration radio transients from extragalactic sources. Their frequency and polarization properties are affected by plasma and magnetic fields along the line of sight to Earth. We report radio observations of FRB 20240304B and near-infrared follow-up to identify its host galaxy. The host is a low-mass, clumpy, star-forming galaxy at redshift 2.148 ± 0.0013, corresponding to 3 billion years after the Big Bang. This FRB occurred during the peak of cosmic star formation and probes ionized gas over ~80% of cosmic history. The highly scattered burst emission implies that there is a population of FRBs that are undetected by current surveys.

title: Mechanisms of nucleosome disruption shape epigenetic inheritance pathway choice
source: Science
abstract: Maintaining cell identity requires duplicating the genome and epigenome during S phase. As DNA is copied, histones extracted from parental nucleosomes are transferred to nascent strands, which preserves the position of epigenetic marks. How the replisome coordinates these processes is unclear. Using reconstitution with purified yeast proteins, kinetic measurements, structural biology, mass spectrometry and genomics, we examined nucleosome-replisome encounter and histone transfer. Parental nucleosomes can be unwrapped ahead of the fork by the MCM helicase, aided by FACT and Ctf4, or by Tof1. Nucleosomal DNA unwrapping by MCM creates a FACT binding site, helping strip histones off DNA. Ctf4 enhances FACT-stimulated histone extraction, retains parental histones and hands them to Tof1, en route to lagging-strand redeposition. Thus, extraction via Ctf4 commits histones to lagging-strand transfer.

title: Binding kinetics enable tumor-selective MAPK and growth suppression by a Type 1 RAF inhibitor
source: Science
abstract: Targeting the RAS/MAPK pathway has long been constrained by dose-limiting toxicity in normal tissues at doses required for durable tumor control. Although Type 1.5 RAF inhibitors improved selectivity in BRAF(V600X)-monomer tumors, a comparable strategy for RAF dimer-driven cancers, including those with RAS mutations, has been lacking. We describe ELV-3111, a potent Type 1 RAF inhibitor that inhibits RAF dimers and exploits binding kinetics for tumor selectivity. ELV-3111 primes RAF in normal tissues, and its rapid dissociation during drug clearance generates drug-free RAF dimers that paradoxically activate MAPK signaling. RAS-mutant tumors are spared, where RAF is already primed. Combined with a MEK inhibitor, ELV-3111 restored normal tissue signaling while deepening tumor pathway inhibition, producing regressions across RAS- and BRAF-mutant experimental models. Thus, inhibitor dissociation kinetics provide a generalizable source of therapeutic index.

title: Stereodivergent telomerization of linear functionalized dienes with amines
source: Science
abstract: Despite the importance of divergent synthesis to obtain different isomers for medicinal and material chemistry, divergent stereocontrol over four distinct selectivity factors remains a fundamental challenge. The telomerization reaction is limited to the transformation of simple unfunctionalized 1,3-dienes to circumvent intractable stereoisomeric mixtures. Here, we report an orthogonal telomerization platform using linear functionalized 1,3-dienes as the substrates, which simultaneously dictates geometric, regio-, diastereo-, and enantioselectivities. We prepared diverse types of γ-amino esters from identical, readily available unsaturated esters and amines via synergistic palladium and acid catalysis, with each precisely obtained out of hundreds of potential telomers. We developed several chiral phosphoramidite ligands to promote the transformation. This study showcases the potential of multidimensional stereomanipulation for the industrially valuable telomerization reaction.

title: Magic state cultivation on a superconducting quantum processor
source: Science
abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires a universal gate set, but the necessary non-Clifford gates represent a significant resource cost for most quantum error correction architectures. Magic state cultivation offers an efficient alternative to resource-intensive distillation protocols; however, testing the proposal’s assumptions represents a challenging departure from quantum memory experiments. We present an experimental study of magic state cultivation on a superconducting quantum processor. We implement cultivation, including code-switching into a surface code, and develop a fault-tolerant measurement protocol to bound the magic state fidelity. Cultivation reduces the error by a factor of 40, with a state fidelity of at least 0.9999(1) (retaining 8% of attempts). Our results experimentally establish magic state cultivation as a viable solution to one of quantum computing’s most important challenges.

title: Electron-Deficient β-Diketone Ligand Enabled Ni-Catalyzed Remote Dicarbofunctionalization of Alkenes
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract A nickel-catalyzed remote migratory dicarbofunctionalization of alkenes was realized with high efficiency and excellent regioselectivity without the assistance of a directing group. The formation of a thermodynamically stable allyl-metal intermediate and the use of an electron-deficient β-diketone ligand are the keys to the success of these remote diarylation and arylalkenylation. This protocol features a broad substrate scope and excellent functional group compatibility, providing a series of remote diarylated and arylalkenylated hydrocarbons in high yields. Notably, the allyl group represents one of the most synthetically useful handles in synthetic chemistry, and the synthetic values of this process have been demonstrated by the formal synthesis of allocolchicinoids, and by the preparation of a RARγ selective retinoid agonist in a highly efficient and step-economical manner.

title: Transport due to density gradient driven TEM & UM in advanced tokamak plasma configurations: role of negative triangularity and magnetic shear reversal
source: Nuclear Fusion - latest papers
abstract: Advanced tokamak configurations can modify microturbulence through changes in magnetic equilibrium, trapped-particle dynamics, resonance conditions. In this work, global gyrokinetic simulations are used to study density-gradient-driven trapped-electron turbulence in tight-aspect-ratio shaped plasmas, focusing on the role of negative triangularity and reversed magnetic shear. In the positive versus negative triangularity comparison, negative triangularity is found to stabilize high- modes and reduce saturated particle diffusivity by approximately . Energy-exchange diagnostics show that this reduction is associated with a weaker participation of weakly trapped electrons, while zonal-flow shearing remains comparable between the two configurations. In the reversed-shear case for positive triangularity, despite larger linear growth rates, the saturated electron diffusivity is reduced by approximately as compared to positive magnetic shear case. This reduction is attributed to the diminished radial support of the perturbation in the reversed magnetic shear region. The combined effect of reversed magnetic shear and negative triangularity is further investigated, revealing that although both independently reduce saturated transport levels, their combination leads to enhanced nonlinear transport.

title: Experimental and numerical investigation of backstreaming positive ions in an RF-driven negative ion source
source: Nuclear Fusion - latest papers
abstract: Backstreaming positive ions (BSPIs) are an unavoidable byproduct in high-power negative ion-based neutral beam injection systems, posing a critical challenge to the long-pulse operational stability of ion sources due to the significant heat loads and material erosion they induce. This paper presents a comprehensive experimental and numerical investigation into the generation, spatial distribution, and thermal effects of BSPIs in the dual-radio-frequency (RF)-driver negative ion source at the HONOR test facility of CRAFT. Using a water-flow calorimetry diagnostic system, the dependence of the BSPI power fraction (PBSPI/Pbeam) on key operational parameters was systematically studied. The results show that the PBSPI/Pbeam ratio increases monotonically with the source filling pressure, rising from ∼2.05% at 0.3 Pa to ∼3.15% at 0.57 Pa. A non-monotonic dependence on beam energy is observed, with the ratio peaking at ∼2.65% at 161 keV. This trend is attributed to the competition between the improved geometric transmission efficiency of BSPIs—resulting from reduced beam divergence at moderate energies—and the intrinsic decrease in collision cross-sections at higher energies. Furthermore, the ratio is found to decrease with increasing extracted beam current, which is explained by the space-charge-induced beam divergence that reduces the geometric transmission efficiency through the acceleration grids. Distinct BSPI bombardment traces on the backplate exhibit an array pattern corresponding to the plasma grid apertures. Coupled thermal-fluid-solid simulations, incorporating the measured heat loads, indicate that under typical high-power conditions (190 kV, 16.2 A), the maximum backplate temperature remains well below the material safety limit. This work clarifies the key mechanisms governing BSPI generation and validates the thermal reliability of the backplate design, providing a solid basis for the development of high-power negative-ion-based neutral beam injection (NNBI) systems.

title: VEGF-Rich Engineered Apoptotic Extracellular Vesicles Loaded with Quercetin for Androgenetic Alopecia Treatment
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Androgenetic alopecia (AGA) is a progressive hair loss disorder characterized by follicular miniaturization, oxidative stress-induced dermal papilla cell apoptosis, downregulated angiogenic genes, and insufficient vascularization in the perifollicular microenvironment. Current pharmacotherapies are limited by transient efficacy and side effects, necessitating novel delivery systems that simultaneously address the vascular insufficiency and oxidative burden to halt and reverse follicular miniaturization. In this study, we constructed genetically engineered apoptotic extracellular vesicles (ApoEV) from adipose mesenchymal stem cells (AMSCs) that were functionalized with vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) to promote angiogenesis and loaded with Quercetin (QUE) for antioxidant defense (VEGF ApoEV@QUE). The VEGF ApoEV@QUE significantly promoted human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) proliferation, migration, and tube formation. In addition, it promoted dermal papilla cells (DPCs) proliferation, protected DPCs from oxidative stress by activating the Wnt/β-catenin and AKT/GSK3β signaling pathways. In the AGA mouse model, subcutaneous injection of VEGF ApoEV@QUE accelerated the telogen-to-anagen transition, increased hair follicle density, and enhanced perifollicular vascularization compared to monotherapies. Biosafety analysis revealed no overt systemic toxicity in this short-term model. This study demonstrates that engineering ApoEV to co-deliver surface-anchored angiogenic factors and intracellular antioxidants provides an enhanced dual-action therapeutic strategy for AGA.

title: An Injectable Hydrogel Integrating Antibacterial and Antioxidant Functions for the Treatment of Periodontitis
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Periodontitis is a chronic inflammatory disease initiated by microbial dysbiosis and sustained by a dysregulated host response, in which excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS), mitochondrial dysfunction, and persistent inflammation contribute to progressive periodontal tissue destruction. Here, we developed LAEPL-SA, an injectable composite hydrogel prepared by conjugating α-lipoic acid (LA) to ε-poly-l-lysine (EPL) and incorporating the resulting LAEPL into a sodium alginate (SA) network. The system was designed to simultaneously reduce the microbial challenge and excessive oxidative/inflammatory injury within the periodontal microenvironment. EPL contributed direct cationic antibacterial activity, whereas LA provided antioxidant and cytoprotective effects associated with reduced ROS accumulation. LAEPL-SA exhibited favorable injectability, self-healing behavior, rheological stability, wet hydroxyapatite-surface retention, and antibacterial activity. Compared with LA-SA, LAEPL-SA showed stronger antioxidant effects and improved protection against oxidative injury. In H2O2-stimulated human periodontal ligament stem cells, LAEPL-SA reduced intracellular and mitochondrial ROS accumulation, restored mitochondrial membrane potential, decreased apoptosis, and suppressed inflammatory responses. In a ligature-induced rat periodontitis model, LAEPL-SA reduced oxidative stress and inflammation, preserved mitochondrial ultrastructure, decreased osteoclast activity, and alleviated alveolar bone resorption. These protective effects were accompanied by activation of the Nrf2/HO-1 antioxidant pathway. Collectively, LAEPL-SA provides a multifunctional local therapeutic platform that integrates antibacterial activity with attenuation of excessive oxidative and inflammatory stress for periodontitis treatment.

title: Comparative Study of Naphthalene Diimide Terminal Groups for Buried-Interface Modification in Perovskite Solar Cells
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract SnO2 serves as a leading electron transport material in n–i–p perovskite solar cells (PSCs), yet its practical deployment is constrained by interfacial defects and energy-level mismatch. Herein, two naphthalene diimide (NDI) derivatives—DPNDI with pyridine terminals and NDI-N with dimethylamino terminals—are introduced at the SnO2/perovskite buried interface to investigate the effects of terminal groups on interfacial chemistry, crystallization, and charge dynamics. Theoretical calculations and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) confirm that DPNDI coordinates Pb2+ via pyridine N, while NDI-N coordinates via carbonyl O. Both form a dipole layer that retards crystallization, reduces defects, and minimizes voids and strain. NDI-N has a larger dipole due to intramolecular charge transfer from the dimethylamino groups to the NDI backbone, which improves SnO2 conductivity and reduces the conduction band offset to 0.08 eV, facilitating electron extraction. Consequently, the power conversion efficiency (PCE) increases from 19.88% (control) to 21.81% (DPNDI PSCs) and 24.17% (NDI-N PSCs). Unencapsulated NDI-N devices show superior storage stability, retaining 68.97% of initial PCE after 1000 h in N2 vs 50.22% for control. Under continuous maximum power point tracking (MPPT) in air, however, the encapsulated control device retains only 87.74% of its initial efficiency after 500 h, markedly lower than the 92.67% retained by encapsulated NDI-N devices.

title: Molecular Dipole Engineering of NiO Hole Injection Layers for Suppressed Exciton Quenching and High-Performance Quantum Dot Light-Emitting Diodes
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Conventional poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene)(styrene sulfonate) (PEDOT), the most widely used hole injection layer (HIL) in quantum dot light-emitting diodes (QLEDs), suffers from intrinsic acidity and hygroscopicity, limiting device stability and long-term performance. To address these limitations, inorganic nickel oxide (NiO) nanoparticles (NPs) have emerged as a promising alternative HIL owing to their superior chemical robustness and favorable energy levels. However, the practical performance of NiO-based QLEDs remains constrained by surface defect states, including Ni3+ species and oxygen vacancies, which induce interfacial non-radiative recombination and hinder efficient hole injection. Here, we report a self-assembled monolayer (SAM)-assisted interfacial engineering strategy using 4-bromomethyl benzoic acid (4-BMBA) to passivate NiO NP surfaces and optimize the NiO/quantum dot interface. The 4-BMBA SAM simultaneously suppresses defect-mediated exciton quenching, improves energy-level alignment, and facilitates hole injection, resulting in significantly enhanced charge balance. Photoluminescence and time-resolved photoluminescence measurements reveal suppressed non-radiative recombination and prolonged exciton lifetime, while impedance spectroscopy demonstrates reduced interfacial resistance and a lower charge injection barrier. Consequently, the optimized QLEDs exhibit a low turn-on voltage of 2.2 V, a maximum luminance of 54,660 cd m–2, an external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 20.34%, and a current efficiency (CE) of 28.89 cd A–1. These results represent one of the highest reported performances among QLEDs employing inorganic HILs for II–VI and III–V colloidal quantum dots. This work establishes SAM-mediated defect passivation as an effective strategy for simultaneously regulating interfacial chemistry and charge injection in inorganic HIL-based QLEDs, providing a versatile platform for next-generation high-efficiency and stable quantum dot optoelectronic devices.

title: Intrinsic High-κ Elastic Dielectrics from Dual-Fluorinated Polyurethane Urea Enable Low-Voltage Stretchable Organic Transistors
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Low-voltage operation in intrinsically stretchable transistors fundamentally relies on gate dielectrics that reconcile intrinsic stretchability with a high dielectric constant (high-κ). However, reconciling enhanced dielectric performance with robust mechanical resilience remains a persistent challenge. Here, we report a molecular engineering strategy to synthesize a series of functionalized polyurethane urea (PUU) by rationally incorporating distinct functional groups into the hard-segment domains. Among the synthesized variants, the difluorinated analogue (2F-PUU) achieves an optimal trade-off, combining a high κ of 7.06 at 1 kHz, exceptional stretchability up to 1623%, strain-insensitive dielectric behavior, solvent reprocessability, and an ultralow surface roughness of 0.273 nm. Stretchable organic transistors employing 2F-PUU as the gate dielectric operate at a low voltage of –10 V and sustain stable electrical performance under 50% tensile strain. Moreover, a 5 × 5 transistor array based on 2F-PUU delivers a 100% fabrication yield, with a peak mobility of 0.51 cm2 V–1 s–1 and a maximum on/off current ratio exceeding 104. Collectively, this work establishes a viable molecular design roadmap for intrinsically stretchable high-κ dielectrics, paving the way toward low-power, mechanically durable stretchable organic electronics.

title: Metallic–Ionic Copper Cooperative Interfacial Engineering Enables Stabler and Fast-Charging Silicon Anodes
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Silicon is considered one of the most promising anode materials for next-generation lithium-ion batteries because of its exceptionally high theoretical capacity. Nevertheless, its practical use is constrained by coupled mechanical degradation, unstable solid electrolyte interphase evolution, and sluggish charge transport during cycling. Herein, we propose a previously unexplored metallic–ionic cooperative interfacial engineering strategy that fundamentally reconstructs the silicon interface through the synergistic integration of a hydrogen-bonded mucic acid network and hybrid Cu0/Cu+/Cu2+species. Unlike conventional metal modification, the coexistence of metallic and ionic copper forms a multifunctional interface that can simultaneously accommodate stress, improve electron/Li+ transport, and regulate the chemical evolution of the interfacial phase, resulting in the formation of a thin, dense, inorganic SEI rich in LiF, which suppresses the continued decomposition of the electrolyte and interfacial degradation. Benefiting from this integrated regulation mechanism, the optimized Si@MA*Cu anode exhibits an ultralow electrode thickness expansion of only 4.5% after 200 cycles, corresponding to a 97.3% reduction relative to pristine silicon, together with a reversible capacity of 1550.0 mAh g–1 after 400 cycles at 1 A g–1 and a high–rate capacity of 1375.5 mAh g–1 at 5 A g–1. Electrochemical tests show faster charge transfer, enhanced Li+ diffusion, and dominant pseudocapacitance, while DFT calculations reveal that hybrid Cu states reconstruct interfacial electronic structure, boost Fermi–level electronic density, strengthen Li adsorption, and lower Li+ migration barriers. This study establishes a paradigm for metal-ion synergy by combining mechanical adaptation, interfacial phase control, and charge transport, providing a general interfacial design principle for developing durable, fast-charging, and high-energy alloy-type battery electrodes.

title: Tuning Surface Termination of Perovskite Nanocrystals to Control Interfacial Charge Transfer and Photocatalytic Efficiency
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Efficient extraction of photogenerated charge carriers remains a major challenge in metal halide perovskite nanocrystal (MHP NC) photocatalysis because of rapid electron–hole recombination at the nanocrystal surface. Although interfacial binding between the NC surface and charge-acceptor molecules is known to facilitate charge separation, the influence of nanocrystal surface termination on this process remains largely unexplored. Herein, we investigate how the surface termination of CsPbBr3 nanocrystals (CPB NCs) regulates interfacial binding with para-substituted aniline (PSA) hole acceptors bearing –SH, –COOH, and –NH2 anchoring groups and how these interactions influence photocatalytic performance. Ultrafast spectroscopic studies reveal a complete reversal in hole-transfer efficiency upon changing the surface termination from Pb-rich to Br-rich, demonstrating that surface-dependent preferential interactions govern interfacial charge-transfer dynamics. These findings are further validated through the photoreductive homocoupling of phenacyl bromide via C–C bond coupling, where Pb-rich CPB NCs exhibit significantly superior photocatalytic activity owing to stronger coordination-like interactions with the anchoring groups. Overall, this work establishes surface termination as a critical design parameter for controlling interfacial charge transfer and provides a rational strategy for developing highly efficient perovskite nanocrystal photocatalysts.

title: Sequential Defect Engineering Enables External-Reductant-Free In Situ Formation of Cu2S Electron Reservoirs in a TiO2/SCN/Cu2S S-Scheme Heterojunction for Noble-Metal-Free Photocatalytic H2 Evolution
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Noble-metal-free photocatalytic H2 evolution is often limited by the need for external reductants to generate low-valence cocatalysts and by poorly controlled interfacial charge transport. Here, we establish a sequential defect-engineering strategy that uses trace sulfur in sulfur-doped carbon nitride (SCN) as an intrinsic reductant and sulfur source to construct Cu2S directly on a preformed TiO2/SCN heterojunction. This sequence simultaneously avoids noble metals and external reducing agents while promoting intimate Cu-S interfacial bonding and the formation of oxygen and copper vacancies. The resulting TiO2-SCN-Cu2S S-scheme heterojunction delivers 38.06 mmol g−1 H2 in 6 h (average rate: 6.34 mmol g−1 h−1), 21-fold higher than TiO2-SCN and 1.57-fold higher than a TiO2-SCN-Pt benchmark containing 3.6 wt % Pt, tested at the same total catalyst mass. Experiments, density functional theory (DFT) calculations, finite-difference time-domain (FDTD), and machine-learning trend analysis collectively show that the copper-addition sequence controls copper speciation, defect population, light harvesting, and interfacial charge separation. This work identifies sequentially programmed Cu2S formation and vacancy generation as an integrated design strategy for reductant-free, noble-metal-free S-scheme photocatalysts.

title: Smart pH-Switchable Nanozyme-Hydrogel Platform with Phycocyanin-Stabilized Mn-Doped Prussian Blue for Synergistic Photothermal-Multienzyme Cascade Therapy of Infected Wounds
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Infected wound healing remains a major clinical challenge due to persistent bacterial infection, excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS), prolonged inflammation, and impaired tissue regeneration. Here, we develop a smart composite hydrogel (PPB/PB-Mn@PC) by integrating Mn-doped Prussian blue nanozymes surface-modified with phycocyanin (PB-Mn@PC) into a dynamic polyvinyl alcohol/pullulan/borax (PPB) hydrogel. The system features pH-responsive accelerated release of PB-Mn@PC in the acidic infected microenvironment, combined with excellent self-adaptive filling, self-healing, and tissue adhesion properties. The PB-Mn@PC nanozymes exhibit superior photothermal conversion efficiency under 808 nm laser irradiation and multienzyme-mimicking activities. Notably, their catalytic behavior dynamically switches: predominant SOD/CAT-like ROS scavenging under neutral conditions for cytoprotection, and enhanced POD-like activity under acidic conditions that supports bacterial killing without a proportional increase in freely diffusible ·OH, thereby limiting collateral oxidative burden. In vitro, the composite hydrogel demonstrates excellent biocompatibility, efficient broad-spectrum antibacterial activity (including biofilm disruption), ROS scavenging, and promotion of macrophage M2 polarization. In vivo, in S. aureus-infected full-thickness wound models, the smart hydrogel significantly reduces bacterial burden, accelerates wound closure, enhances re-epithelialization, collagen deposition, and angiogenesis, while effectively suppressing pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-6 and TNF-α). This work presents a rationally designed smart hydrogel platform that integrates dynamic mechanics, intelligent microenvironment-responsive release, and synergistic photothermal-multienzyme therapy, offering a promising strategy for the efficient management of infected wounds.

title: Infrared–Thermal Co-driven CO2–Ethanol Coupling to Diethyl Carbonate Enabled by Electron-Rich Lattice Oxygen
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The conversion of CO2 into value-added chemicals represents a promising pathway for CO2 mitigation and utilization. The direct synthesis of diethyl carbonate (DEC) from CO2 and CH3CH2OH is particularly attractive owing to its high atom economy. However, the direct thermocatalytic synthesis of DEC remains inefficient because of unfavorable thermodynamics and the substantial kinetic barrier for coupling CO2 with ethoxy species (CH3CH2O*). Herein, an IR-thermal co-driven catalytic strategy was developed over reconstructed CeO2 (CeO2-500), enabling a DEC formation rate of 9.3 mmol g–1 h–1 without any dehydrating agent, representing a 3.1-fold enhancement compared with unreconstructed CeO2. This enhancement is attributed to the reconstruction-induced local defect structures in CeO2, which create an electron-rich lattice oxygen environment that strengthens CO2 adsorption and activation. Meanwhile, local structure modulation enhances IR light absorption and generates mildly oxidative charge carriers, which accelerate CH3CH2O* formation and promote its coupling with activated CO2 to form the key CH3CH2O-CO* intermediate, thereby boosting DEC formation. Thermal energy facilitates the transport of IR-induced charge carriers and lowers the kinetic barrier for DEC formation. This work provides an IR–thermal co-driven catalytic strategy for efficient CO2 conversion into value-added carbonates.

title: Low-Hysteresis and Overshoot-Free Capacitive Strain Sensor for Silent Speech Recognition
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Conventional capacitive strain sensors suffer from mechanical hysteresis, signal overshoot, and delayed response due to viscoelastic relaxation in solid dielectric materials. We address these limitations through a synergistic structure–material design combining an auxetic porous conductive framework with a solid–liquid hybrid dielectric. The auxetic architecture reversibly deforms to suppress hysteresis, while the confined ionic liquid eliminates viscoelastic relaxation, enabling rapid, stable signal output with negligible overshoot. In situ scanning electron microscopy characterization reveals dynamic liquid-bridge formation and rupture during deformation, establishing the mechanistic link between multiphase dielectric evolution and capacitance modulation. Our sensor demonstrates exceptional performance: <2% hysteresis, 57 ms response time, negligible overshoot, gauge factor of 3.1, and stability over 8500 cycles. A wearable silent speech recognition system validates its practical applicability, achieving a classification accuracy of 93.9%. This work establishes a generalizable design strategy for soft strain sensors with simultaneously suppressed hysteresis, minimal overshoot, and fast response, enabling next-generation wearable electronics and intelligent interfaces.

title: Ice Plant-Inspired Hierarchical Nanofibrous Film for Outdoor-Stable Passive Radiative Cooling
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Daytime radiative cooling provides a low-energy approach for passive thermal management. However, existing materials primarily focus on cooling intensity, often neglecting critical issues such as nighttime overcooling, pollutant adhesion, and long-term stability. Inspired by the bladder-like epidermal structures of Mesembryanthemum crystallinum leaves, this work developed a biomimetic nanofibrous film based on poly(vinylidene fluoride-co-hexafluoropropylene) (P(VDF-HFP)). To translate this natural hierarchical morphology into an effective light-regulating structure, P(VDF-HFP) nanofibers were used as the supporting framework, while TiO2 was introduced as a surface scattering and functional component. Through a precursor-based strategy and electrospinning, a uniform hierarchical inorganic particle/polymer fibrous structure was constructed. This multiscale architecture enhances solar scattering and regulates mid-infrared emission. The film achieves an AM1.5G-weighted solar reflectance of 90.5% over 0.3–2.5 μm, while its infrared emission is mainly concentrated within the atmospheric window. This spectral selectivity supports daytime heat dissipation while limiting radiative heat loss outside the atmospheric window. Outdoor tests demonstrated that the nanofibrous film exhibited a temperature up to 5.8 °C lower than that of a commercial white fabric reference under identical conditions. Moreover, it retained high whiteness after 230 h of UV irradiation and exhibited photocatalytic pollutant-degradation capability. This bioinspired hierarchical design offers a practical strategy for developing flexible radiative cooling materials with high reflectance, selective emission, and environmental stability.

title: Supramolecular Manipulation of Copper Nanoclusters Boosts Chiral Optical Performances
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) performance of chiral metal nanoclusters is generally limited by random ligand motion, which induces non-radiative decay and impairs chiral coupling, resulting in low photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQYs) and weak intrinsic chirality. Here in this study, drawing inspiration from the art of marionette puppetry, where a puppeteer controls a puppet through strings attached to strategic points, we construct hydrogen-bonded organic superstructures (HBOSs) composed of cyanuric acid and 1,3,5-triazine-2,4,6-triamine to manipulate chiral glutathione-capped copper nanoclusters (GSH-Cu NCs). The hydrogen-bonding interactions between HBOSs and GSH-Cu NCs act as the "strings" that precisely direct their spatial arrangement and effectively restrain random ligand motion. The manipulation processes harness the orientation of nanoclusters and balanced the electric and magnetic dipoles, therefore boosting the chiral optical performances including increased PLQY to 94.15% and amplified CPL over an order of magnitude to –1.39 × 10–2. Additionally, the composites also exhibit thermally reversible fluorescence between –20 and 20 °C, demonstrating the reversible nature of hydrogen-bonding interactions. The red-emitting GSH-Cu NCs/HBOSs phosphors are integrated with commercial phosphors onto an InGaN chip, yielding white light-emitting diodes that exhibit near-ideal CIE coordinates of (0.33, 0.34) and a high color rendering index of 92.1. Our study offers a strategy to overcome the trade-off between electric and magnetic dipoles which further provides insights for the design of next-generation high-performance optoelectronic devices.

title: Fe,Ni Co-modification Balances Activity and Stability in RuO2 for Anion Exchange Membrane Water Electrolysis
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Anion exchange membrane water electrolysis (AEMWE) needs oxygen evolution anodes that combine high-current-density performance with long-term operational stability, yet RuO2, the most active benchmark oxide catalyst, dissolves under sustained anodic operation. Catalyst development almost always selects compositions by activity measured at 10 mA cm–2 in three-electrode cells, a regime far below device conditions. Here, we synthesize a library of transition-metal-modified RuO2 catalysts and show that this selection criterion fails in an operating electrolyzer. Screening across Mn, Fe, Co, and Ni modifiers identifies RuO2–FeNi as the optimal balance, with a Tafel slope of 47 mV dec–1 and a Ru mass activity of 1357 A gRu–1 at 400 mV overpotential, 14 times that of commercial RuO2, despite the smallest electrochemically active surface area in the series. In a membrane electrode assembly, RuO2–FeNi reaches 1 A cm–2 at 1.82 V in polarization measurements at 80 °C. In a separate 200 h durability test at 250 mA cm–2 and 60 °C, its cell voltage rises by 274 mV, most of it within the first 25 h, whereas RuO2–Fe, which reaches twice the current density at 1.82 V, rises by 560 mV within 64 h under the same protocol. Density functional theory traces the activity of RuO2–FeNi to Fe/Ni co-incorporation, which renders Ru electron-deficient, downshifts the Ru 4d band center, and moderates the adsorption of oxygenated intermediates; higher compositional complexity introduces electronic disorder without further benefit. Intermediate compositional complexity, selected by device-level testing rather than by screening activity, emerges as the design target for Ru-based AEMWE anodes.

title: Sequence‐Retentive Upcycling of Polyamide 66 Into Quasi‐Alternating Biodegradable Polyesteramides With Closed‐Loop Recyclability
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Polyamide 66 (PA66) is a durable engineering plastic with poor biodegradability and limited energy‐efficient recycling options, posing environmental challenges. Herein, we report a sequence‐retentive, one‐pot, two‐step depolymerization‐repolymerization strategy for the upcycling of waste PA66 into biodegradable polyesteramides (PA66‐EX). Rather than depolymerizing PA66 into constituent monomers, adipic acid‐assisted acidolysis selectively converts PA66 into carboxyl‐terminated polyamide oligomers with tunable amide sequence lengths, which are reconnected through ester‐containing segments via in situ melt polycondensation with ethylene glycol. This sequence‐retentive strategy generates quasi‐alternating polyesteramide backbones that preserve PA66‐derived amide‐rich domains while uniformly introducing hydrolysis‐sensitive ester linkages. The resulting PA66‐EX materials combine biodegradability with high thermal and mechanical performance, showing melting temperatures of 180°C–197°C, 5% mass‐loss temperatures above 356°C, tensile strengths of 27–35 MPa, and elongations at break of 414%–745%. Enzymatic degradation increases systematically with ester content, confirming the role of ester linkages as accessible degradation sites. Moreover, PA66‐EX demonstrates polymer‐to‐polymer closed‐loop recyclability, largely retaining its molecular sequence characteristics, thermal properties, and mechanical performance over five consecutive, catalyst‐free hydrolysis‐repolymerization cycles. This work establishes a practical strategy for transforming waste PA66 into high‐performance biodegradable polyesteramides and provides a general sequence‐retentive molecular design principle for achieving circularity in condensation polymers.

title: Continuous Tuning of Magnetic Bistability via Consecutive Desolvation and Decoupled Structural Phase Transition
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving precise and continuous modulation of magnetic bistability remains a key challenge in advancing the practical utility of molecular magnetic materials. Herein, we exploit the consecutive desolvation and the following decoupled, thermally induced structural phase transition (SPT) to finely regulate the magnetic bistability in a mononuclear Fe III SCO complex. This complex evolves from an abrupt SCO with a transition temperature ( T 1/2 ) of 264 K to a hysteretic two‐step transition ( T 1/2 ↓ = 132 K, T 1/2 ↑ = 155 K, ∆ T = 23 K), and finally to a locked high‐spin (HS) state, which occurs via single‐crystal‐to‐single‐crystal transformations. More importantly, a quantitative linear correlation between the SPT progression and the HS/LS ratio is established by fine‐tuning the annealing temperature and duration. This work demonstrates that the consecutive desolvation and decoupled SPT offer a new strategy for the continuous regulation of the key parameters of SCO‐based magnetic bistable materials.

title: 3D-Printed BiFeO3@TiO2 Heterojunctions with Post-UV Activation for Enhanced Visible-Light Photocatalytic Degradation of Acyclovir
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract A method for 3D-printed photocatalytically active hybrid materials is reported. To this end, methacrylate-based resins doped with TiO2 particles decorated with BiFeO3 nanoparticles (BiFeO3 @TiO2) are developed for digital light processing (DLP) 3D printing technique. Upon DLP printing, the BiFeO3 @TiO2 particles are embedded in a polymer matrix, deactivating the materials for photocatalytic processes. However, after 24 h post-print UV activation, the resin is locally decomposed, exposing the BiFeO3 @TiO2 particles and thereby activating the materials with respect to their photocatalytic performance. Comprehensive characterization (TEM–EDS, XPS, FTIR, PL, TGA, reflectance) confirms the activation of the material's surface, yielding improved charge-separation efficiency. Under 440 nm irradiation, the UV-activated monolith achieved 71% acyclovir degradation, with a pseudo-first-order rate constant of 0.050 h–1, 2.7 times higher than that of unactivated structures and 7.5 times higher than that of a 3D-printed TiO2 (P25) reference sample. The photocatalyst retained 96% of its initial activity after six consecutive 24 h photocatalytic cycles, demonstrating excellent long-term stability. This print–activate strategy provides a practical route for overcoming catalyst encapsulation in DLP-printed photocatalysts and enables reusable visible-light-active monolithic architectures for water-treatment applications.

title: Atomic-Scale Visualization of MnOH x Reconstruction via Hydrogen Spillover for a Poisoning-Resistant Oxidation Pathway
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Hydrogen spillover offers a route to modulate oxide surface chemistry, yet how it governs the reaction pathways of oxide-catalyzed CO oxidation remains elusive. Here, we show that hydrogen spillover hydroxylates MnOx on Pt(111) to form the MnOHx overlayer, with dynamically reconstructed triangular domains. High-pressure scanning tunneling microscopy reveals that MnOHx exhibits a distinct CO oxidation pathway without carbonate accumulation at room temperature. Microscopy, spectroscopy, and theory identify bridging hydroxyls within MnOHx interior domains as the key reactive motifs that react with CO. Consistent with this mechanism, hydrogen spillover also enhances CO oxidation over MnOx/Pt nanoparticle catalysts, linking atomic-scale insight to practical catalytic performance. These findings demonstrate that tailoring hydroxyl configurations can suppress poisoning and redirect oxidation pathways, offering a strategy extendable to other low-temperature oxidation reactions.

title: Modulation of Oxygen Vacancy Charge-State Evolution via Rare-Earth Praseodymium Doping for Improving the Photostability of Amorphous InZnO Thin-Film Transistors
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Metal oxide thin-film transistors (MOTFTs) used as backplanes for large-area and high-resolution OLED displays require simultaneously high carrier mobility and operational stability. Light-induced instability arising from the generation and persistence of photocarriers in the oxide semiconductor remains a critical challenge. Trace praseodymium (Pr) doping substantially enhances the illumination stability of amorphous InZnO (a-IZO) TFTs while maintaining high electron mobility has been reported, yet the underlying electronic mechanism remains elusive. Here, combining first-principles calculations with experimental investigations, the mechanism of enhanced photostability in Pr:IZO MOTFTs was revealed. We found that redox-active Pr dopants act as dynamic charge buffers to regulate the photoinduced charge redistribution and oxygen vacancy (VO) charge state evolution in a-IZO. The localized Pr 4f electronic states participate in a reversible charge redistribution process during the photoinduced ionization–recovery cycle, which suppresses the evolution of VO toward kinetically trapped charge states, preserves the electronic accessibility of VO related gap states for carrier recapture, and reduces photoinduced lattice reconstruction. Time-resolved transient absorption measurements further confirmed that Pr incorporation accelerates photocarrier relaxation, shortening the characteristic fast decay lifetime from ∼47 to ∼6 ps. These findings establish a direct correlation between localized electronic state evolution and photoexcited carrier dynamics and may provide a new strategy based on redox-active cation engineering to overcome the long-standing mobility–stability trade-off in metal oxide semiconductors.

title: Hierarchically Porous Metal–Organic Frameworks as Multifunctional Platforms for Synergistic Chemo-Photo-Biocatalytic Enantioselective Synthesis
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) offer a promising platform for the precise customization of multifunctional composites, enabling the optimization of synergistic effects between catalysts and significantly enhancing both stability and catalytic performance. Despite this potential, this idealized system is still in the exploratory stage. Herein, we integrated a chemical catalyst with a photoenzyme-based enantioselective catalytic platform into a single system, achieving the sequential transformation from C2-alkylation to asymmetric Mannich reaction products. A hierarchically porous (HP) UiO-67 material was constructed as the supporting platform. Through a post-synthetic ligand exchange strategy, Pd(II) and Ru(II) catalysts were simultaneously immobilized, while wheat germ lipase (WGL) was encapsulated within the mesoporous channels, yielding the multifunctional catalyst WGL@HP-UiO-67-Pd/Ru. This catalyst afforded satisfactory yields of 62–94% in the C2-arylation reaction and enantioselectivities of 69–93% in the asymmetric Mannich reaction. In this sequential catalytic transformation, the multifunctional catalyst afforded an overall efficiency of 47.6%, corresponding to a 3.8-fold enhancement over the homogeneous catalyst system. These findings provide deeper insight into the role of multifunctional catalysis in sequential reactions and underscore its considerable promise for the asymmetric synthesis of organic compounds and pharmaceutical agents.

title: Dense Metalloporphyrin Arrays Enable Binuclear Cooperativity for Enhanced Electrocatalytic Oxygen Reduction
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT The oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) is central to clean energy technologies like fuel cells and metal‐air batteries, yet its efficiency relies on costly platinum catalysts. In nature, cytochrome c oxidase achieves efficient ORR at a heme iron‐copper binuclear center, where hydrogen bonding stabilizes key intermediates. Here, by mimicking this concept, we constructed a gallium–pyrazolate framework (Ga‐TPzP) with densely packed Co(II)‐porphyrin arrays. The precise arrangement of these sites at an optimal distance of 6.53 Å creates confined nanoreactors, enabling strong hydrogen bonds between coordinated H 2 O and adsorbed O 2 on two adjacent Co(II) centers. This unique binuclear cooperativity facilitates O 2 activation and stabilizes the *OOH intermediate, thereby lowering the kinetic barrier and significantly enhancing the ORR performance. As a cathode in a zinc‐air battery, Ga‐TPzP(Co) achieves a peak power density of 185 mW cm − 2 and can operate steadily for 150 h at 10 mA cm −2 , representing one of the best performance among all reported MOF‐based catalysts for this application.

title: Grain boundary effects on surface modifications of tungsten under fusion-relevant helium plasma irradiation: coarse-grained vs nano-grained microstructures
source: Nuclear Fusion - latest papers
abstract: Grain refinement is widely regarded as an effective strategy for improving radiation resistance in nuclear materials, but the influence of grain boundaries (GBs) on helium (He) plasma irradiation-induced surface modifications in tungsten (W) remains unclear. Here, we compare the surface morphology evolution and subsurface bubble distributions of coarse-grained and nano-grained W under fusion-relevant He plasma irradiation. The samples were exposed simultaneously to 90 eV He ions at 1173 K. Although both microstructures ultimately developed similar fuzz composed of nanoscale tendrils, their early-stage evolution of surface roughening exhibited distinct differences. In the nano-grained W film, ∼600 nm thick, surface roughening was initiated by anomalous bubble growth at grain junctions. In contrast, coarse-grained W exhibited pronounced crystallographic-orientation-dependent roughening. Subsequent tendril nucleation and growth occurred in both microstructures, preferentially at highly convex surface regions. Moreover, subsurface bubbles were confined mainly to a shallow region approximately 100–200 nm beneath coarse-grained W, whereas they permeated the entire nano-grained film. These results indicate that GB-mediated bubble dynamics primarily govern surface evolution during the fuzz-incubation stage, while interface curvature and capillary-driven diffusion dominate tendril nucleation and subsequent growth. Thus, GBs exert a decisive influence during early-stage surface roughening but have limited effect on the later development of fuzz. These findings provide insight into the distinct and common mechanisms governing He-induced surface modification in W with different grain sizes and support a capillary-growth framework for fuzz formation.

title: Comprehensive synthesis of K48/K63 ubiquitin pentamers by graph-empowered automation
source: Nature Chemistry
abstract:
Abstract
                  Linear, branched and heterotypic ubiquitin (Ub) chains regulate essential cellular processes, yet their structural and functional analysis remains limited by the difficulty of preparing defined, homogeneous samples. Here we establish a fully automated platform for the comprehensive synthesis of all 56 K48/K63-linked Ub tetramers and pentamers, by iterative cycles of K48- or K63-specific chemoenzymatic conjugations of chemically synthesized Ub monomers bearing a fast-cleaving lysine protecting group compatible with folded proteins. A graph-based digital encoding of Ub chain topologies enabled systematic enumeration and filtering of reaction pathways, guiding the selection of synthetic routes. This computational system generates reagent maps and executable code to direct iterative deprotection and conjugation cycles on a standard, laboratory liquid-handling robot. All 14 Ub tetramers and 42 Ub pentamers were obtained with high fidelity, as validated by SDS–PAGE and mass spectrometry. This work establishes a general framework for automated protein conjugate synthesis and provides access to the complete space of K48/K63 branched ubiquitin chains.

title: Binuclear copper enzymes enable selective radical (pseudo)halogenation
source: Nature Chemistry
abstract: Synthetically valuable new-to-nature reactions in copper enzymes remain largely underexploited in chemical synthesis. Now, the combination of binuclear copper enzymes and a photoredox catalyst can efficiently perform enantioselective decarboxylative (pseudo)halogenation starting from redox-active esters.

title: The power of O vacancies in electrocatalysis
source: Nature Chemistry
abstract: Non-stoichiometric oxide materials are essential to chemistry, but controlling their synthesis towards a tuneable number of unpaired electrons trapped in the oxygen vacancies remains challenging. title: Highway-Inspired Hollow Fillers to Improve CO2 Transport in Mixed-Matrix Membranes
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Inorganic fillers play a critical role in mixed-matrix membranes (MMMs) to improve membrane separation performance. However, it is faced with a persistent trade-off: low filler loading is insufficient to achieve significant performance enhancement, while high filler loading introduces stress defects that weaken membrane strength. Developing highly efficient porous fillers capable of delivering substantial separation improvements at low loading offers a solution to this challenge. Herein, we report the design of etched KMnF3 (KMnF3-EC) fillers inspired by the Maxwell dispersion theory and highway transport concepts. These fillers possess a hollow core and a highly porous shell, which maximize pore volume per unit mass of filler and create rapid gas transport pathways. Incorporation of KMnF3-EC fillers into Pebax membranes resulted in remarkable gas separation performance at an ultralow filler loading (1.5 wt %), yielding a 120% increase in gas permeability and a 57.1% enhancement in gas selectivity. Owing to such low filler loading, the membranes maintained excellent mechanical properties, with elongation at break exceeding 800% and a Young’s modulus above 100 MPa. Direct benchmarking against commonly used porous fillers revealed that KMnF3-EC improves gas separation performance with an order-of-magnitude greater efficiency. These findings provide a promising strategy for designing advanced fillers that overcome the challenging MMM performance–mechanical strength trade-off, thereby facilitating the development of durable and energy-efficient membrane separation.

title: Evolution of Color in Highly Transparent Emulsions
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT This paper presents highly stable, dynamically tunable and transparent colored emulsions. A typical system is formulated with 1‐octadecene droplets (0.5–1.0 µm) dispersed in a water–glycerol (volume ratio of 21:79) continuous phase stabilized by ethylene‐1,2‐bis(dodecyldimethylammonium bromide). By precisely engineering the refractive index matching between the two phases, the emulsion achieves nearly 100% transmittance at the matching wavelength λ c , exhibiting saturated, wavelength‐selective coloration. Owing to the distinct thermo‐optic coefficients (d n /d T ) of the two phases, the macroscopic color reversibly shifts from blue to purple, purplish‐red and orange–yellow ultimately reaching yellow, covering almost the entire visible spectrum between 25°C and 43°C. Composition titration experiments showed the relationship between the macroscopic color shift of the emulsion and the microscopic refractive index matching of the two phases. The scattering efficiency of a single emulsion droplet is calculated based on the van de Hulst approximation. The result reveals that the macroscopic vividness of colors originates from the cumulative scattering effects of a large number of droplets. As water and glycerol can mix in any ratio, this designing principle can not only be successfully applied to other olefins and diverse multi‐component oil combinations, exhibiting exceptional formulation adaptability, but also opens up potential applications for optical filters and sensors.
