title: Sustainable Depolymerization of Polyurethane Waste via Base‐Free Catalytic Hydrogenolysis
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Polyurethane (PU), the sixth most produced polymer globally, poses significant environmental challenges due to its stable cross‐linked structure, which hinders degradation and recycling. Although catalytic hydrogenolysis offers a promising route for recovering valuable monomers, current systems generally require strongly alkaline conditions and homogeneous catalysts, limiting their practical applicability. Herein, we report an efficient base‐free hydrogenolysis system using a supported amorphous molybdenum sulfide catalyst (a‐MoS x /Al 2 O 3 ) for the closed‐loop recycling of PU, achieving recovery rates of 94.6% for aromatic amines and 99.9% for polyols. Mechanistic investigations reveal that abundant sulfur vacancies not only promote the depolymerization of PU to generate isocyanates and polyols, but also catalyze the hydrogenation of isocyanates to amines. This suppresses repolymerization with polyols, ensuring complete depolymerization. The catalyst exhibits broad applicability across diverse PU types and real‐world PU waste, while maintaining its activity after regeneration. This work establishes a sustainable catalytic route for converting PU waste into high‐value monomers.

title: Impacts of energetic ion on the unstable spectra of kinetic ballooning modes and zonal flow generation
source: Nuclear Fusion - latest papers
abstract: Global gyrokinetic particle simulations are employed to investigate the interaction between energetic ions (EIs) and kinetic ballooning modes (KBMs) across different toroidal mode number ( ) regimes, encompassing linear dispersion relations, nonlinear wave-particle interactions, and wave–wave interactions. The results demonstrate that EIs exert non-perturbative destabilizing effects on low- KBMs, while stabilizing high- KBMs through thermal ion dilution. These opposing EI effects arise from the different strengths of finite Larmor radius (FLR) and finite orbit width (FOW) effects in low- and high- regimes. Single- and multi- nonlinear simulations reveal strong wave-particle interactions between EIs and low- KBMs, resulting in higher KBM saturation levels and enhanced EI transport. Additionally, although low-density EIs have little direct influence on zonal flow (ZF), they can indirectly increase the spatial scale of ZF in multi- simulations. Since ZF is generated via the beat-driven process and its structure is determined by the pump wave, the EI effects lead to the dominance of low- KBM components, thereby increasing the spatial scale of the ZF.

title: Confinement property in the JT-60SA first operation phase
source: Nuclear Fusion - latest papers
abstract: In JT-60SA, the global energy confinement time has been evaluated to be – s for 1 MA hydrogen discharges and compared with the ITERL-96P(th) scaling. Because local measurements of ion temperature , electron density and effective charge are not available in the first operation phase and the number of discharges and their parameter range are limited, the present results should not be considered definitive. As heating power increased, tends to shorten in the same trend as the scaling. is shorter than the scaling but approaches the scaling with increasing density. For 0.4–0.6 MW ohmic heating plasmas, increases with increasing collisionality and saturates. For 0.6–0.8 MW ohmic heating and electron cyclotron resonance heating (ECH) plasmas, continues to increase up to higher collisionality and reaches the scaling. The turbulence simulations with the trapped gyroLandau-fluid model assuming a linear profile show that the dominant turbulence mode is trapped electron modes. The linear growth rate decreases with increasing collisionality and saturates at a low level in the 0.4–0.6 MW ohmic heating plasma, suggesting the transition from the linear ohmic confinement regime to the saturated ohmic confinement regime. For 0.6–0.8 MW ohmic heating and ECH plasmas, the saturation occurs at higher collisionality, indicating that the linear confinement regime extends to higher collisionality. The global particle confinement time excluding recycling contributions, , has also been evaluated to be s, approximately twice , from the frequency responses in a density feedback control experiment. From and the effective particle confinement time including recycling , a recycling coefficient is obtained as . The sub-unity recycling coefficient indicates that wall recycling is insufficient to maintain plasma density, consistent with hydrogen retention due to the first hydrogen discharge with continuous gas injection.

title: Retained fuel removal from plasma-facing materials: effects of baking methods and hydrogen isotope exchange
source: Nuclear Fusion - latest papers
abstract: Tungsten (W) is a prominent plasma-facing material for deuterium–tritium (D–T) fusion reactors, yet T fuel retention in W poses critical challenges to safety and operational viability. This study systematically compares three baking methods—vacuum baking, H2 gas atmosphere baking, and hydrogen (H) plasma baking—for removing D retained in W at 513 K, simulating realistic conditions for T removal in reactors. Experimental results demonstrate that D removal efficiencies reach 75% for vacuum baking after 16 h, 83% for H2 atmosphere baking after 16 h, and 99% for H plasma baking after 1 h. The superior performance of H2 atmosphere and H plasma baking is primarily driven by hydrogen isotope (HI) exchange, with efficiency strongly dependent on the concentration of H introduced into W. Higher H concentrations promote more complete exchange, leading to significantly reduced D retention. A multi-isotope Fill Level model was developed to simulate the end-to-end H plasma exchange process. The simulation reproduces the experimentally observed D removal kinetics and the emergence of HD desorption, with the D retention in good agreement with measurements. The pronounced disparity between H2 atmosphere baking and H plasma baking is fundamentally governed by the quantity of H entering W: H plasma promotes significantly greater H ingress, thereby enhancing HI exchange and resulting in a drastic reduction in D retention. This work provides both experimental validation and modeling support for HI exchange as an efficient T removal strategy.

title: Protein Secondary Structure From Infrared Spectroscopy—Tricks to Use and Traps to Avoid
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Secondary structure analysis of proteins is one of the major applications of infrared spectroscopy in the life sciences. It requires high quality spectra and their adequate interpretation. This article aims to guide practitioners in generating and interpreting protein infrared spectra, as well as help readers and reviewers assess the quality of the resulting articles. It addresses common problems and mistakes, simple quality criteria and measures for improved spectrum quality and interpretation. Regarding experimental procedures, the text discusses avoidance of water vapor, effects of air bubbles, reduction of noise, and criteria for judging spectrum quality. The secondary structure analysis section focuses on a particular approach in which the amide I region of the spectrum is represented by fitted component bands. The following aspects of the approach are considered: application of band‐narrowing techniques, fitting of spectra, assignment of component bands and the accuracy of secondary structure analysis. The purpose is not to provide a single best practice protocol but to make the reader aware of the implications, limitations, pitfalls, and improvement potentials of the used procedures.

title: Nuclear factor I connects H3K27M to a targetable purine dependency in diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma is a lethal pediatric brainstem cancer with few effective treatments. Here, we integrate metabolomic, transcriptomic, chromatin, genetic and in vivo analyses to identify a purine-metabolic dependency associated with the H3K27M histone mutation. The histone H3 lysine 27-to-methionine substitution increases Nuclear Factor I transcriptional activity, which promotes coordinated expression of enzymes involved in purine biosynthesis and degradation, including 5-aminoimidazole-4-carboxamide ribonucleotide formyltransferase/inosine monophosphate cyclohydrolase and purine nucleoside phosphorylase. Sustained purine degradation limits feedback inhibition of purine synthesis, enabling continued purine production, utilization and catabolism. Genetic or pharmacological inhibition of the terminal de novo purine biosynthesis enzyme reduces tumor-cell fitness, slows orthotopic tumor progression and extends survival in mice. These results connect histone-mutation-associated chromatin remodeling to a Nuclear Factor I-regulated, therapeutically targetable purine dependency in diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma.

title: Choline kinase α promotes glycolysis and tumor growth by phosphorylating and activating enolase 1
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Tumor cells exhibit aberrantly upregulated glycolysis, in which glycolytic enzyme enolase 1 (ENO1) plays a critical role. However, how ENO1 activity is dynamically regulated in tumor cells remains elusive. Here, we demonstrate that hypoxic stimulation promotes the binding of p38 MAP kinase to choline kinase α (CHKα). p38 phosphorylates CHKα at S114, subsequently leading to CHKα to interact with ENO1. Importantly, CHKα functions as a protein kinase and phosphorylates ENO1 Y44 thereby enhancing the metabolic activity of ENO1 to increase glycolysis. Knock-in expression of CHKα S114A or ENO1 Y44F inhibits brain tumor cell glycolysis and proliferation, blunts brain tumor growth in mice with inhibited lactate production, and prolongs mouse survival. In addition, CHKα S114 and ENO1 Y44 phosphorylation levels are positively correlated with each other and associated with poor prognosis in glioblastoma patients. These findings highlight the critical regulation of glycolysis by the noncanonical function of CHKα and underscore the potential to target the moonlighting function of CHKα for cancer treatment.

title: Plant protoplasts display phytopodia
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Plant cells are encased in cell walls and are usually thought to behave like stiff, pressurized vessels. When the cell wall is digested, plant protoplasts form spherical shapes, further consolidating this model. Here we show that plant protoplasts can form phytopodia. More precisely, using plasma membrane markers, we reveal that 27 ± 1% of protoplasts from Arabidopsis seedlings show dot-like protrusions and 16 ± 7% of protoplasts show long (typically 1-20 μm, up to 200 μm) protrusions, hence the name “phytopodia”. We demonstrate that this behavior is independent of the plant species, the membrane marker or the osmolyte. Phytopodia can host microtubule bundles, which in turn can impact their shape. Actin is not required for the presence of phytopodia, and consistently, the movement of phytopodia is passive. Phytopodia can form de novo when increasing osmolarity and they can attach to artificial surfaces. Altogether, this calls for revisiting the dynamics and probing ability of the plant cell cortex in different osmotic and mechanical environments.

title: Chemical defects in semiconducting polymers and their impact on reproducibility and device performance
source: Nature Reviews Materials
abstract: Synthesizing semiconducting polymers often introduces structural defects, altering optoelectronic properties and directly impairing device performance. This Perspective details defect origins, evaluation methods and mitigation strategies, demonstrating how controlling structural variability resolves batch-to-batch inconsistency while unlocking novel materials design opportunities.

title: Tailorable deep eutectic solvents for sustainable lignocellulose refining: from platform design to value-added products
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: Efficient utilization of renewable carbon requires lignocellulosic biorefineries that can deconstruct plant cell walls while preserving the value of cellulose, hemicellulose and lignin. Deep eutectic solvents (DESs), constructed from programmable hydrogen-bond acceptors and donors, have emerged as tunable media for lignocellulose processing. This review discusses recent progress in the rational design of DESs for lignocellulosic biorefineries, focusing on binary, ternary, hydrated, biphasic, catalytic and biocompatible systems. By regulating acidity/basicity, polarity, hydrogen-bonding ability, viscosity, water tolerance, active sites and phase behavior, DESs can selectively disrupt lignin-carbohydrate complexes, stabilize or functionalize the components, and direct the downstream transformation of the components toward bio-based chemicals and functional polymeric materials. Component-oriented valorization routes are summarized, including cellulose-derived functional materials and platform chemicals, lignin-derived aromatics and functional polymers, and hemicellulose-derived furan chemicals. Key barriers to industrial deployment are also critically examined, including high viscosity, mass-transfer limitations, solvent loss, energy-intensive recovery, feedstock heterogeneity, incomplete mechanistic understanding and insufficient techno-economic and life-cycle assessment. Future opportunities are highlighted in artificial-intelligence-guided DESs discovery, novel membrane and electrodialysis DES-recovery technologies, DES-compatible chemo-biocatalysis and closed-loop process integration. Tailorable DESs are expected to evolve from empirical solvent systems into predictive, recyclable and product-oriented platforms for sustainable production of bio-based chemicals, materials and fuels.

title: Dominant role of Southeast Asian emissions in anthropogenic increases in global tropospheric ozone and southward tropical growth, 2000–2019
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: Widespread increases in tropospheric ozone (O3) have been reported over the past two decades, with changes in anthropogenic emissions, particularly in Asia, identified as an important driver. Here we use global model sensitivity simulations to quantify changes in global tropospheric O3 burden and associated radiative forcing (RF) attributable to anthropogenic emission changes from 2000 to 2019, and assess the contributions from different Asian regions. Changes in anthropogenic emissions increased the global tropospheric O3 burden by 12.0 ± 0.5 Tg and global mean RF by 0.030 ± 0.002 W m–2 under fixed 2015–2019 meteorological fields. The increase was larger during 2000–2010 than during 2010–2019 and occurred predominantly in the tropics. Southeast Asia was the largest regional contributor over 2000–2019, accounting for 5.7 ± 0.4 Tg of the simulated global tropospheric O3 burden increase and 0.020 ± 0.002 W m–2 of RF. During 2010–2019, the increase in tropospheric O3 burden attributable to anthropogenic emission changes was larger over 0–30°S than over 0–30°N, indicating a southward shift in the tropical response driven primarily by Southeast Asian emissions. East Asia shifted from a major positive contributor during 2000–2010 to a negative contributor during 2010–2019. These results highlight the increasing importance of anthropogenic emissions from tropical Asia in shaping the global distribution of tropospheric O3 and its climate forcing.

title: Liquid Metal Interlayers Enable Zero-Pressure Sulfide Solid Electrolyte Lithium Batteries
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Lithium metal anodes are essential for high-energy-density batteries with solid-state electrolytes (SSEs), but the lithium-SSE interface suffers from contact loss and current constriction during cycling. External stack pressure can enhance contact retention but adds system-level limitations and accelerates lithium filament penetration. Here, a room-temperature liquid sodium–potassium (NaK) interlayer is demonstrated to stabilize the lithium–sulfide SSE interface under nominally zero stack pressure by combining stress-free morphological adaptability with Li transport capability. In situ X-ray computed tomography and other analytical methods reveal that the liquid layer reconfigures to preserve interfacial contact during Li plating/stripping. Finite Li solubility in the NaK also creates a dissolved-Li-mediated electrochemical pathway that supports Li stripping from a distant reservoir. The dual mechanical and transport functions of NaK enable stable full-cell cycling (600 cycles, >2 mAh cm–2) with layered-oxide composite cathodes under nominally zero applied stack pressure. These findings highlight a fundamental interfacial design concept based on a compliant interlayer that accommodates morphological evolution while supporting Li transport under minimal mechanical confinement.

title: A bacteriocin from the commensal Streptococcus mitis prevents influenza infection-driven pneumococcal lung dissemination
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Streptococcus pneumoniae remains a major public health threat despite widespread use of vaccines and antibiotics. Its synergy with influenza A virus (IAV) often leads to secondary bacterial pneumonia, causing significant morbidity and mortality mainly in vulnerable populations such as children under 5 years old and adults over 65 years old. As pneumococcal pneumonia is preceded by nasopharyngeal colonization, preventing colonization represents a promising intervention strategy. While current interventions are somewhat effective, their impact is limited by serotype replacement and antimicrobial resistance. Here we show that colonization with the commensal S. mitis strain F22Ad significantly reduces pneumococcal density in the nasopharynx by day 10 post-infection and prevents dissemination to the lungs following IAV infection. This protective effect depends on bacteriocins encoded at the blp1 locus. Among these, Bac2v1 alone or in combination with Bac1 significantly reduces pneumococcal colonization. Notably, Bac2v1 exerts broad, serotype-independent inhibitory activity, impairing the growth of diverse epidemiologically relevant pneumococcal strains. These findings establish two precision-based, serotype-independent approaches to target pneumococcal colonization: using S. mitis F22Ad as a live biotherapeutic or administering a bacteriocin mixture produced by this strain. Both approaches have the potential to prevent pneumococcal disease and complement existing strategies.

title: Programming Sodium-Storage Kinetics through Linear Quinone Oligomerization
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Quinone-based organic cathodes enable reversible multielectron redox reactions but suffer from dissolution and sluggish sodium-storage kinetics. Here, two structurally homologous linear quinone oligomers, biphenyl–quinone dimer (2BQ) and terphenyl–quinone trimer (3BQ), are compared to elucidate how backbone extension regulates sodium storage. Compared with 2BQ, 3BQ exhibits reduced crystallinity, enhanced electrochemical utilization, a narrower HOMO–LUMO gap, and lower oxidation reorganization energy. Consequently, 3BQ delivers a reversible capacity of 350 mA h g–1 at 0.05C and retains 80% of its capacity after 500 cycles at 1C, with enhanced rate capability and cycling stability. Operando FTIR and state-dependent XPS reveal reversible C=O/C–O–Na conversion, while density functional theory calculations elucidate an extended multielectron sodiation sequence. These findings establish controlled linear quinone oligomerization as an effective, rational molecular design strategy to reduce apparent dissolution tendency and improve carbonyl-site utilization and sodium-storage kinetics, providing insights into the development of advanced organic cathodes for rechargeable sodium-ion batteries.

title: Sustained changes to urban mobility after COVID-19 reinforced socioeconomic inequalities in Argentina, Chile and Colombia
source: Scientific community and society : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Urban mobility is central to economic activity, social inclusion and access to services. COVID-19 caused disruptions to mobility globally, yet its long-term impacts in Latin America remain poorly understood. Using > 170 million anonymised and aggregated location records from Meta-Facebook users in Argentina, Chile and Colombia (April 2020-May 2022), we examine changes in overall mobility volume relative to pre-pandemic baselines across socioeconomic and rural-urban gradients. Two years after the pandemic onset, mobility in the highest-density urban cores remained ~ 25–50% below baseline across the three countries, while the top 33% most affluent communities had not returned to baseline. These differences are explained by the scale of the initial mobility shock rather than by subsequent recovery rates. Our findings reveal how a global shock can entrench disparities in human mobility, with implications for urban resilience and planning in unequal nations. Our study underscores the need for proactive policies to prevent long-lasting mobility inequalities.

title: A noncanonical reducing-domain architecture defines a distinct class of modular polyketide synthases
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Colibactin is a microbiome-derived genotoxin that damages the genomes of intestinal epithelial cells and has been linked to colorectal cancer. Its biosynthesis is encoded by a large gene cluster (pks/clb) that functions as a hybrid nonribosomal peptide synthetase - polyketide synthase assembly line, yet the structural basis of its assembly remains poorly understood. Here we show cryo-electron microscopy structures of colibactin biosynthetic enzyme ClbB that uncover a noncanonical architecture for a fully-reducing polyketide synthase module. Unlike metazoan fatty acid synthases and iterative polyketide synthases, ClbB arranges its condensing and reducing regions in a crossed configuration. Within its reducing region, the enoylreductase forms an inverted dimer and the dehydratase is positioned peripherally as monomers. Moreover, the dehydratase-enoylreductase unit is embedded within the ketoreductase fold. Bioinformatic analyses combined with deep-learning-based structure prediction indicate that this domain-embedding logic is broadly distributed across diverse bacterial phyla. These findings define a structurally distinct class of reducing polyketide synthase modules and provide an expanded structural framework for understanding how modular polyketide synthases coordinate multi-step chemistry. The work also extends design principles for engineering megasynthases for chemical biosynthesis and synthetic biology.

source: Chem
abstract: Converting CO2 into useful chemicals via reverse water-gas shift reaction offers a promising route toward sustainable carbon utilization. However, catalysts often struggle to coordinate hydrogen and CO2 activation while remaining stable under demanding reaction conditions. The present work developed high-entropy oxides with Li and Al dual-atom doping to promote cooperative alloy-oxide interfaces with coupled H2 and CO2 activation sites, thereby enabling fast, selective, and stable CO production. These findings provide a general strategy for integrating multiple functions into robust catalysts for challenging chemical transformations.

title: Dissociation‐Migration Trade‐Off in Gel Polymer Electrolytes Enables Extreme‐Condition Lithium Metal Batteries
source: Advanced Energy Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Gel polymer electrolytes (GPEs) are promising for lithium metal batteries (LMBs) under extreme conditions due to their relatively high ionic conductivity, enhanced safety, and intimate electrode contact. Despite these advantages, how polymer chemistry governs Li + transport and interfacial reactions remains poorly understood. Here, we establish a dissociation‐migration trade‐off principle using GPEs incorporating polymer motifs with distinct Li + affinities, revealing that intermediate polymer–Li + interactions balance carrier generation with Li + migration. The optimized GPE achieves an ionic conductivity of 4.78 mS cm −1 and a Li + transference number of 0.88 at 30°C, while suppressing excessive electrolyte decomposition and promoting stable electrode–electrolyte interphases with reduced organic accumulation and more uniform depth distributions of inorganic components. Consequently, Li||LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 cells operate across extreme conditions including −40–80°C, 4.6 V, and 4 C, retaining 80.8% capacity after 1100 cycles at −20°C. Furthermore, a 1 Ah pouch cell delivers 342.7 Wh kg −1 and retains 80.3% capacity after 200 cycles. This work provides a molecular framework for the rational design of GPEs that integrate efficient ion transport with interfacial stability.

title: Development and clinical validation of a multimodal AI framework to predict persistent fever during antibiotic therapy in hospitalized patients with cancer
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Among hospitalized cancer patients, persistent fever despite intravenous antibiotics often triggers treatment escalation and additional diagnostics. Earlier identification of patients at low risk for ongoing fever could support more selective decision-making. We developed and compared multimodal AI frameworks to predict persistent fever at the 48–72-hour reassessment window. Models integrated structured variables, time-series, notes, and chest imaging. Models were developed in a University Hospital Essen cohort and evaluated using holdout validation, two pooled regional hospitals, and MIMIC-IV ICU. A feature-level tabularized multimodal TabPFN model showed consistent discrimination, with AUC 0.84 (95% CI, 0.81–0.86) in cross-validation, 0.82 (95% CI, 0.77–0.87) in holdout validation, and 0.78 (95% CI, 0.74–0.81) in MIMIC-IV; other multimodal strategies showed comparable but more variable performance. Performance was primarily driven by temperature dynamics, while chest-radiograph imaging provided no incremental predictive value. In a clinician validation study, the multimodal model outperformed clinicians (Trial 1 balanced accuracy: 0.77 vs 0.60; Trial 2: 0.79 vs 0.57), while clinician balanced accuracy reached 0.71 (95% CI 0.67–0.75) in the AI-assisted condition, suggesting potential benefit of AI support. Overall, multimodal AI demonstrates potential to support 48-hour antibiotic reassessment and stewardship-oriented decision-making, although further prospective studies are needed.

abstract: Small earthquakes [i.e., those of magnitude ( M ) M 2 earthquake within a swarm sequence in California’s Brawley Seismic Zone. Inverting fiber-derived apparent source time functions revealed two distinct rupture episodes separated by 42 milliseconds, reflecting rupture arrest followed by dynamic renucleation. Analysis of a 3-hour sequence showed adjacent, largely nonoverlapping fault patches activated in succession, forming complementary slip partitioning. These fragmented failure patterns within the M 2 rupture and its sequence limited rupture growth, consistent with the absence of a dominant mainshock. Microearthquakes, which are now accessible by fiber-optic sensing, provide direct constraints on fault mechanics across scales bridging laboratory experiments and large earthquakes.

title: Rough fracture zone as a gateway to the 2025 Mw 8.8 Kamchatka earthquake
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract: Rough fault segments typically terminate giant earthquakes but are rarely reported to foster them. However, rupture characteristics of the 2025 moment magnitude ( M w ) 8.8 Kamchatka megathrust earthquake are consistent with initiation in a rough zone. Its early rupture was sluggish, lasting ~50 seconds with limited slip but strong, scattered high-frequency radiation. Rupture then propagated southward into a smoother segment, producing >20 meters slip with less intense high-frequency radiation. Using also the rupture characteristics of four M w 7+ foreshocks and aftershocks, we reveal variably sized seismic patches within the rough zone. We interpret these behaviors as manifestations of stress or frictional heterogeneities on the rough segment that favor localized failures yet can foster a giant rupture when spatially connected to a smooth, locked neighboring segment, a scenario previously underrecognized and meriting consideration in seismic hazard assessments.

title: Mitochondrial profiling links tumor genotype to metabolic and immune vulnerabilities in liver cancer
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract: Although oncogenic alterations influence tumor metabolism, how they impose distinct metabolic programs within a shared tissue remains poorly defined. We developed mitochondrial profiling platforms comparing metabolites and proteins in primary liver cancer (PLC) models. Analysis of six PLCs revealed that mitochondrial metabolism is dictated by oncogene identity. Kras-driven tumors required creatine metabolism to buffer energy, whereas c-MYC-driven tumors relied on oxidative phosphorylation. Among c-MYC-driven PLCs, Pten-deficient tumors accumulated mitochondrial phosphoethanolamine, a precursor of phosphatidylethanolamine (PE). Inhibition of PE synthesis selectively impaired Pten-deficient tumor growth and extended survival, partly through CD8+ T cell infiltration and sensitization to tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α-mediated cytotoxicity. Mechanistically, PE depletion increased the level of surface TNF receptors, promoting proinflammatory responses. These findings uncover genotype-specific metabolic liabilities and establish PE synthesis as a mechanism of immune evasion in PLC.

title: An engineered cohesion system reduces errors in aged mammalian eggs
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract: In humans, female fertility declines rapidly from approximately 35 years onward owing to a steep increase in eggs in which chromosomes have split prematurely or that harbor an incorrect number of chromosomes (aneuploid eggs). A leading cause of age-related aneuploidy in eggs is the premature separation of sister chromatids (PSSC), which is caused by a loss of cohesin from chromosomes. In this study, we created an artificial cohesion system that reduces PSSC in aged mouse eggs. We further engineered a separase-cleavable sequence into the system, allowing for its scheduled deactivation during anaphase. We demonstrated that the artificial cohesion system could be adapted to tether human chromosomes, providing a proof of principle for the future development of approaches to reduce PSSC in eggs from women of advanced reproductive age.

title: Integrating established and emerging tools to assess wildlife condition from the ground, up
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract: Metabolic energy links individual physiology to population-level dynamics, making wildlife body condition a cornerstone of conservation science. Emerging technologies, including unoccupied aircraft systems, make remote assessment of animal condition possible at unprecedented scales, and physiologically grounded validation is essential for strong inference. Here we examine the strengths and challenges of traditional and remote methods, using a comparative perspective that emphasizes both lipid and lean mass dynamics in evaluating wildlife health. We provide a framework that integrates complementary approaches to assess wildlife condition across diverse systems, matching emerging methods with the required physiological resolution, species characteristics, and temporal and spatial scales, while enhancing research ethics. Expanding capacity to track wildlife energetics from individuals to populations requires novel approaches and is vital for conservation in a changing world.

title: Counter-ion confinement reverses ion selectivity in subnanometer channels
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract: Ion transport in nano- and subnanometer channels is central to processes such as ion separation, energy conversion and storage, and nanofluidics. Conventionally, positively charged nanochannels favor anion transport and vice versa. We report that cationic covalent organic framework membranes with sub–one-nanometer channels exhibit selective cation transport. This reversal in selectivity arises from a counter-ion confinement effect, which inverts the electrostatic environment inside the channel wall and creates a secondary confinement region. The counter-ion confinement mechanism concomitantly suppresses coexisting ion competition in mixed-salt systems, enabling membranes to retain high selectivity under practical separation conditions. Our findings provide a design strategy for creating adaptive and highly selective membranes for precise ion transport and separation.

title: Abrupt surface water decline during 2023–2024 record warming
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract: Global warming is expected to accelerate the hydrological cycle, yet its impact on terrestrial water availability is uncertain. Using assimilated streamflow observations from 150 major basins and satellite data for over 1.2 million water bodies, we show a global-scale synchronized decline of streamflow and surface water storage during the 2023–2024 record-warm period, the largest reduction since 1991. South America accounted for 70.4 ± 4.2% of the global streamflow decline. This abrupt depletion was driven by compound ocean–atmosphere forcing, in which concurrent El Niño and tropical North Atlantic warming triggered large-scale atmospheric subsidence, moisture divergence, and amplified drought. These findings reveal that extreme warming can induce abrupt water losses even in humid regions, underscoring a critical vulnerability of global hydrology and water security.

title: A tryptophan cation radical determines radical transfer kinetics and catalytic rate in a ribonucleotide reductase
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract: Ribonucleotide reductase (RNR) is the sole enzyme responsible for de novo deoxynucleotide synthesis for DNA replication and repair. In the Escherichia coli class Ia RNR, a radical must traverse 32 angstroms along a pathway composed of amino acids spanning β and α subunits to complete each turnover. By incorporating unnatural amino acids to alter reduction potentials of pathway tyrosine residues, we (i) perturb the rates of radical transfer and show that they match the rates of deoxynucleotide production and (ii) directly observe a tryptophan cation radical (W 48 + •) as a kinetically competent pathway intermediate. Together, these results establish that radical transfer through W 48 in α 2 β 2 is the rate-limiting process, which controls the enzymatic activity of E. coli RNR.

title: Priming of AGO2 by type I interferons balances inflammation and antiviral immunity
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract: Argonaute-2 (AGO2)–mediated RNA silencing contributes to antiviral defenses in plants and insects and may contribute to mammalian immunity, too. However, it is unknown whether AGO2 is modified upon infection or inflammation in mammals. We identified that the ubiquitin ligase RING-finger protein 126 (RNF126) interacts with and ubiquitinates AGO2 to enhance its small interfering RNA or microRNA loading. Using data from cells in vitro and mouse tissues, we propose that RNF126 is induced by type I interferon (IFN-I) signaling and promotes the ability of AGO2 to silence proinflammatory genes and inhibit viral replication. Lipid nanoparticle delivery of RNF126 mRNA to mice inhibited inflammation and viral replication. These findings identify cross-talk of IFN-based immune signaling and AGO2-mediated RNA silencing and suggest that the RNF126-AGO2 axis helps to balance inflammatory and antiviral immune protection.

title: Atomic functional site scaffolding in biopolymers with RFdiffusion3
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract: The catalytic and other sophisticated functions of biomolecules arise from the placement of many atoms in three-dimensional space. We describe a generative artificial intelligence method for biopolymers, RFdiffusion3 (RFD3), which uses free-atom diffusion to satisfy complex sets of atomic constraints more rapidly and accurately than previous methods across several challenges, from enzyme design to RNA structure design. We demonstrate experimentally the power of the RFD3 pipeline for enzyme design by designing de novo phosphotriesterases with a complex active-site architecture that incorporates a carbamylated lysine coordinating two metal ions and zinc proteases specific for the transthyretin protein involved in amyloid diseases; in both cases, we obtained active catalysts in zero-shot 96 construct design campaigns.

title: Shared patterns of human milk composition link mammary gland function to infant growth
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract: The mammary gland produces nutrient-rich human milk (HM), yet how mammary functional state shapes HM composition and infant outcomes remains poorly understood. We used HM multiomics, including metabolomics, proteomics, micronutrients, macronutrients, and HM oligosaccharides, across 1543 samples from three cohorts, including two randomized trials, as a noninvasive readout of mammary functional state. Trajectory modeling and multiomic integration showed that maternal supplementation improved recovery from early growth faltering and revealed a shared HM compositional axis linking maternal nutrition to infant growth. Machine learning, with Human Protein Atlas–informed proteomics, identified seven HM biomarkers reflecting variation across key mammary domains, indexing milk synthesis, barrier integrity, and immune-repair activity. Elevated valerylcarnitine and low pantothenic acid emerged as metabolic signals linking mammary functional state to infant growth.

title: Nutritional interventions’ impacts on human milk: Three trials in low-resource settings
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract: Human milk (HM) composition is variable to support changing infant needs and is influenced by maternal diet and health. We harmonized HM data from three randomized trials in Burkina Faso (MISAME-III), Pakistan (Mumta-LW), and Tanzania (ELICIT) within the International Milk Composition (IMiC) Consortium to test how maternal nutrition affects HM composition. Balanced energy-protein (BEP) supplements or nicotinamide given to lactating mothers increased milk B vitamins, whereas macronutrients, oligosaccharides, bioactive proteins, and microbiome composition were physiologically buffered. Metabolomic and proteomic analyses revealed shifts in vitamin-related metabolites, triglyceride profiles, and intracellular protein representation. In a MISAME-III subset, maternal and infant blood showed concordant changes. Postnatal BEP improved infant growth only in the more undernourished cohort. Improved milk micronutrient quality across settings supports extending maternal supplementation into lactation.

title: Covalent–Ionic Bonding Regulation Enables Chemo‐Mechanical Stabilization of High‐Voltage O3‐Type Sodium Layered Oxide Cathodes
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Ni–Fe–Mn‐based O3‐type layered oxides are attractive cathode materials for sodium‐ion batteries, but their high‐voltage operation suffers from the coupling between phase transitions and lattice oxygen instability. In this work, guided by hard and soft acids and bases (HSAB) theory, we propose a covalent–ionic dual‐pathway decoupling strategy to stabilize high‐voltage O3‐type layered cathodes. The incorporation of Mg, Ti, and F constructs a rigid architecture in which a covalent Ti─O framework reinforces the transition‐metal octahedral skeleton to suppress detrimental phase transitions, while localized Mg─F ionic coordination stabilizes lattice oxygen through localized electrostatic anchoring to mitigate irreversible oxygen release. Through multiscale structural and spectroscopic analyses, we verify that this bonding regulation suppresses the O3→P3→OP2 multiphase evolution and lattice oxygen escape. The modified cathode maintains 76.32% capacity retention over 400 cycles at 1 C and exhibits robust cyclability across −10°C to 50°C; the assembled full cells achieve a reversible capacity of 166.27 mAh g −1 with an energy density of 330.22 Wh kg −1 at 0.1 C, and an initial capacity of 143.74 mAh g −1 with 72.06% retention after 500 cycles at 1 C. This work demonstrates a bonding‐regulation paradigm that decouples chemo‐mechanical degradation in high‐energy‐density layered oxide cathodes.

title: Synergistic Water‐Deficient Inner Helmholtz Plane and Asymmetric Dual‐Site Nonmetal Catalysts Enable Stable Ah‐Level Aqueous Zn–I2 Batteries at Elevated Temperatures
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT At elevated temperatures, intensified water‐induced side reactions and iodine dissolution severely hinder the development of aqueous zinc–iodine batteries. Herein, a marginally hydrophilic and conductive modification layer with a hexagonal layered structure is constructed to stabilize the anode interface. This approach establishes a water‐deficient inner Helmholtz plane and reduces the fraction of weak hydrogen bonds, thereby suppressing spontaneous Zn dissolution and water decomposition. Concurrently, interfacial electronic structure regulation increases the energy barrier for the hydrogen evolution reaction and promotes uniform Zn deposition along the Zn‐(002) crystal plane, effectively inhibiting dendrite growth. These effects are corroborated by theoretical calculations and in situ characterizations. Furthermore, asymmetric dual‐site nonmetal single‐atom–cluster structures are introduced into the cathode host to enhance iodine adsorption and accelerate conversion kinetics, thereby mitigating iodine dissolution. Benefiting from this synergistic design, the assembled coin‐type battery delivers a discharge capacity of 95 mAh g −1 after 60 000 cycles at 8 A g −1 . A sub‐ampere‐hour‐level plastic‐cased battery employing a high‐loading cathode with a theoretical areal‐capacity of 5.6 mAh cm −2 further demonstrates strong practical potential by maintaining excellent cycling stability at 3 C and at 50°C. An Ah‐level pouch battery also exhibits stable operation at 50°C.

title: Interface Engineering to Unlock Multi‐Electron Sn+/S2− Redox Reaction and High Lithium Anode Utilization
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT All‐solid‐state lithium–sulfur batteries (ASSLSBs) offer high theoretical energy density, yet their practical viability is impeded by sluggish cathodic redox kinetics and uncontrolled anodic dendrite growth. Here, we address these challenges by a dual‐interface engineering strategy that exploits halogen anion migration to in situ construct phase‐separated localized electrochemical microreactors (LEMRs) at both electrodes. At the cathode, an in situ‐formed Li 6 PS 5 Cl/LiCl/Li 2 S‐LiI internal LEMR activates the S 2− /S n+ ( n ≥1) multi‐electron redox reaction beyond the conventional S 2− /S 0 redox reaction while maintaining structural integrity. Concurrently, at the Li anode, an interfacial LiCl/C@LiI/LiCl‐LiI anode LEMR confines Li plating/stripping within the LEMR to suppress lithium dendrites. This dual‐LEMR architecture enables the optimized cells to deliver a capacity retention of 86.3% after 450 cycles at 3.6 mAh cm −2 and 80% after 70 cycles at a high areal capacity of 7.5 mAh cm −2 under a low N/P ratio of 0.78, and to achieve an ultra‐high areal capacity of 32.8 mAh cm −2 . This work highlights the potential of anion chemistry as an effective interface engineering strategy to overcome the kinetics and stability limits of all‐solid‐state lithium batteries, and provides a versatile framework for advancing high‐energy ASSLSBs.

title: Antigen‐Presenting Microrobots Program CAR‐T Cell Function
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Mechanical forces are emerging as key regulators of T‐cell function, yet how active motion‐ derived mechanical cues from artificial antigen‐presenting cells (aAPCs) influence T‐cell activation and fate remains largely unexplored. Here, we develop self‐propelled antigen‐presenting microrobots (CytoBots)—gas‐driven magnesium microparticles functionalized with anti‐CD3 and anti‐CD28 antibodies—that actively navigate suspension environments and mechanically engage T cells. Unlike immotile aAPCs, CytoBots generate motion‐dependent, force‐bearing stimulation that enhances T‐cell activation. Single‐cell force spectroscopy shows that CytoBots double receptor–ligand binding strength and extend bond lifetime threefold, supporting a role for motion‐enhanced mechanical interactions in T‐cell activation. CytoBot stimulation is associated with enhanced proximal T‐cell signaling, increased phosphorylation of AKT and mTOR, and metabolic changes characterized by elevated mitochondrial respiration and glycolysis‐associated activity. These responses accompany the enrichment of stem‐like and central memory T‐cell populations. In humanized tumor models, CytoBot‐expanded CAR‐T cells exhibit superior cytotoxicity, persistence, and antitumor efficacy. These findings establish microrobotic antigen‐presenting interfaces as a generalizable strategy for programming immune cell function through dynamic mechanotransduction, opening new opportunities for next‐generation cell therapies.

title: Electron Bridge Effect Enhanced Tandem Catalysis for Efficient Nitrate Reduction to Ammonia
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrochemical nitrate reduction reaction (NO 3 RR) offers a promising route for wastewater remediation and ammonia (NH 3 ) synthesis under mild conditions. However, the activity of NO 3 RR is hindered by the high activation barrier of nitrate (NO 3 − ), as well as the low generation efficiency and restricted migration of active hydrogen (H ads ). The development of electrocatalysts that combine efficient synergistic active sites, rapid electron transfer, and unimpeded H ads migration pathways is crucial for enhancing NO 3 RR performance. Here, we report a molten salt etching strategy to successfully prepare a ternary metal boride MoCoB electrocatalyst. In this catalyst, Mo site can efficiently adsorb and activate NO 3 − , while Co site is responsible for H 2 O dissociation and H ads supply. Meanwhile, B site builds an electronic bridge to enhance the electron transfer and proton migration between Mo and Co sites. Benefiting from the synergistic mechanism of electron bridge effect‐enhanced tandem catalysis, MoCoB achieves an NH 3 yield rate of 61.89 mg h −1 mg cat −1 with a Faradaic efficiency of 98.73%. Furthermore, a Zn‐NO 3 − /ethanol hybrid battery assembled with MoCoB cathode demonstrates high power density and durable long‐term cycling stability, and the production of high‐value ammonium acetate. This work provides guidance for designing efficient NO 3 RR electrocatalysts and offers insights into reversible zinc‐based battery.

title: Low‐Temperature‐Locked Crystallization Enables Stress‐Relaxed Antimony Selenide Thin‐Film Solar Cells
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Absorber quality is critical to the performance of thin‐film photovoltaics, particularly for antimony selenide (Sb 2 Se 3 ). Due to its quasi‐one‐dimensional crystal structure, the migration, rearrangement, and orientation evolution of Sb 2 Se 3 chains play a pivotal role in determining crystallization and microstructural behavior. However, rapid heating (as with conventional thermal annealing) typically induces competitive chain orientation and nonuniform stress relaxation. This results in defect generation, orientational disorder, and complex crystallization pathways that severely constrain device performance. To address these issues, we propose a low‐temperature pretreatment to precisely regulate the crystallization kinetics of Sb 2 Se 3 absorbers. Low‐temperature pretreatment applied to amorphous Sb 2 Se 3 films prior to annealing effectively suppresses atomic diffusion and structural disordering, while preserving short‐range ordered chain segments as structural motifs for subsequent crystallization. During the subsequent annealing process, progressive stress relaxation facilitates chain reorientation and crystal reconstruction, thereby influencing local Sb‐Se compositional evolution, promoting grain growth, and enhancing preferential orientation. This progressive ‘low‐temperature‐locking stress‐relaxation‐oriented reconstruction’ process markedly reduces residual stress and defect density, while improving charge transport and suppressing non‐radiative carrier recombination. As a result, our pretreated device achieved a power conversion efficiency of 9.78%. This strategy offers a general route to fabricating high‐quality, low‐stress, low‐defect chalcogenide films for efficient and stable photovoltaics.

title: SEI Evolution on Siloxene Anodes in Solid and Liquid Electrolytes via an Ion‐Sieving/Electron‐Conducting Interfacial Layer
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Silicon anodes suffer from severe volume expansion and unstable solid electrolyte interphase (SEI), which limit their use in both liquid and solid‐state batteries. Here, a two‐dimensional siloxene‐based LP@SONS, is constructed by anchoring polypyrrole nanoparticles and lithiated‐Nafion onto siloxene nanosheets. This architecture combines electron‐conducting pathways with a Li + ‐selective ion‐sieving layer, homogenizing Li + flux, restricting anion/solvent penetration, and buffering strain. The stable and compositionally identical platform enables direct comparison of SEI evolution in liquid and solid electrolytes. In liquid cells, the SEI grows in a bulk‐permeated (3D) manner, whereas solid electrolytes confine growth to a planar solid–solid contact, yielding a LiF‐rich, planar‐confined (2D) SEI that passivates rapidly. Remarkably, LP@SONS promotes thinner, more uniform, LiF‐rich interphases in both systems. As a result, it delivers high reversible capacity, excellent rate capability, and long‐term cycling in liquid and solid‐state batteries, with only ∼5% thickness expansion after 100 cycles. This work clarifies how electrolyte contact geometry governs SEI dimensionality and offers an interfacial engineering strategy for high‐capacity anodes.

title: Single‐Atom Based Dual‐Metal‐Active‐Site Catalysts for N2 Conversion to Ammonia and Urea Synthesis: Geometric Coupling, Electronic Polarization, Reaction Partitioning, and Intermediate Steering
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT N 2 conversion is increasingly recognized not as a simple activation process of an inert molecule, but as a coupled reaction network that requires synchronized N 2 adsorption, electron/proton transfer, intermediate hydrogenation, C─N coupling, product release, and side‐reaction suppression. Single‐atom catalysts provide atomic precision, well‐defined coordination environments, and tunable electronic structures, but their isolated active centers often struggle to satisfy the multiple and sometimes conflicting requirements of complex N 2 conversion. Single‐atom‐based dual‐metal‐active‐site catalysts are therefore emerging as cooperative catalytic architectures that integrate an atomically dispersed metal single atom with a second metal site in the form of an isolated atom, cluster, or nanoparticle. This review establishes a structure‐function framework for understanding these catalysts, focusing on dual‐site adsorption geometry, asymmetric electronic polarization, bifunctional reaction partitioning, and intermediate‐specific stabilization. Recent advances in ammonia and urea synthesis are discussed to reveal how dual sites regulate N 2 activation, proton supply, intermediate evolution, and selective C─N bond formation. Particular attention is given to metal‐metal interactions, support‐mediated charge redistribution, hydrogen transfer, and pathway‐dependent intermediate binding. Finally, key challenges, including precise dual‐site construction, quantitative synergy identification, and practical compatibility, are highlighted to guide the rational design of next‐generation dual‐site catalysts for sustainable N 2 conversion.

title: Dark Horse Absorbers for Indoor Photovoltaics: Toward Cheaper, Safer, and More Stable Alternatives
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Indoor photovoltaics (PVs) have emerged as a promising solution for powering low‐power electronic and Internet of Things (IoT) devices by harvesting energy from artificial light sources. The development of low‐cost, non‐toxic, and stable absorber materials is central to enabling sustainable and scalable development of indoor PVs. Among various candidates, chalcogenide and kesterite absorbers such as Se, Sb 2 S 3 , Sb 2 (S,Se) 3 , GeS, Cu 2 ZnSnS 4 and Cu 2 ZnSn(S,Se) 4 have recently attracted attention due to their earth abundance, environmental benignity, and suitable optoelectronic properties for indoor light harvesting. This review provides a comprehensive overview of reported Indoor PV devices based on these absorber materials. Beyond comparing reported device performances, it critically examines the relationships between their fundamental optoelectronic properties, absorber processing, defect and interface engineering, device architecture, stability, sustainability, and demonstrated integration with IoT applications. Although research on these systems remains at an early stage, rapid progress has been achieved, highlighting their strong potential for next‐generation indoor energy harvesting. Finally, we outline key challenges and future research directions to guide the development of efficient, stable, and environmentally sustainable Indoor PVs for powering low‐power electronics and IoT devices.

title: Ring‐Retaining Polymerization of Vinylidenecyclopropanes
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Commodity feedstock‐derived vinylidenecyclopropanes (VDCPs) are a new class of allenic monomers stereoelectronically intermediate between butatrienes and allenes. While their butatriene character drives the C5 ring‐opening polymerization (C5‐ROP), the complementary allene‐type polymerization mode remains elusive. Herein we report this new pathway for VDCPs. Organonickel catalysts with coordinating counterions enable C2 ring‐retaining polymerization (C2‐RRP), yielding pendant alkylidenecyclopropane moieties. Computations ascribe this reactivity to strain‐release alkene coordination, which further enables one‐pot diblock copolymerization with conventional allenes.

title: An Expandable Library of Solid Polymer Electrolytes for Lithium‐Metal Batteries
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Solid‐polymer‐electrolytes (SPEs) offer alternatives to next‐generation solid‐state lithium‐metal batteries, promising advantages in mechanical‐compliance, processability, cost‐effectiveness, and safety. While tremendous efforts have generated diverse SPEs since 1970s, SPE‐practicality remains limited by the trade‐offs among ion‐conductivity, high‐voltage stability, and Li 0 ‐electrolyte compatibility. Here, we establish the first SPE library covering 12 SPEs across five polymer families, which allows us to collect large datasets on chemistry, interfacial, and electrochemical properties that unveil their hidden connections. Correlation analysis of these descriptors reveals binding‐strength between polymer and Li + , subtle variations in polymer molecular structure, and solid‐electrolyte‐interphase composition as dictating factors. Also discovered is that the standard deviation of coulombic‐efficiency rather than its average value governs the battery cycling stability. The SPE library can be rapidly expanded through two structural engineering pathways: grafting diverse functional segments onto backbones and constructing compositionally‐complex SPEs. As a proof‐of‐concept, we fabricate several such SPEs and find improved high‐voltage stability through gradually increasing the complexity of the polymer matrices. A terpolymer‐based acrylates SPE exhibits outstanding Li 0 plating/stripping over 1800 h, stable cycling in LiCoO 2 ||Li battery with 100% capacity retention and an average coulombic‐efficiency of 99.91% ± 0.09% over 100 cycles. This work provides a transformative framework to design the future polymer materials.

title: Ferroelectric‐Field Gating Suppresses the Outward Migration of Active Oxygen Intermediates in Li‐Rich Cathodes
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Li‐rich layered oxides deliver high capacities through cation–anion co‐redox chemistry. During high‐voltage charging, however, peroxide/superoxide‐like O─O intermediates migrate down their concentration gradient from oxygen‐redox‐active regions toward particle surfaces, accumulating at the interface. This accumulation accelerates irreversible O 2 evolution and structural degradation, leading to low initial Coulombic efficiency and rapid capacity fading. Here, we construct a spontaneously polarized ferroelectric LiNbO 3 interfacial layer that generates a built‐in electric field to regulate oxygen redox in Li‐rich cathodes. This electric field suppresses concentration‐gradient‐driven migration and interfacial enrichment of charged active oxygen intermediates, limiting O 2 evolution and preserving a uniform surface‐to‐bulk distribution of oxygen electronic states at high delithiation. Consequently, the optimized cathode delivers 310 mAh g −1 , an initial Coulombic efficiency of 99.97%, and 79% capacity retention after 500 cycles. Furthermore, this strategy enables Li‐metal pouch cells to achieve an energy density of 620 Wh kg −1 and graphite‐based pouch cells to maintain stable operation over 2000 cycles. This work establishes ferroelectric‐field regulation as an effective strategy for stabilizing oxygen redox chemistry in Li‐rich cathodes.

title: Membrane‐Fusion Navigated Cell Membrane Anchoring Enhances Pyroptosis for Photoimmunotherapy
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Pyroptosis, a membrane disruptive and highly immunogenic form of programmed cell death, remains underexploited in cancer photoimmunotherapy due to the lack of general design principles beyond photosensitizer engineering. Here, we establish a membrane confined strategy that directly programs pyroptotic execution by targeting the plasma membrane as the primary reaction interface. A membrane fusogenic liposomal system enables precise anchoring of a caged perylene bisimides (PBI) onto the cell membrane, bypassing complex molecular modification. Upon light irradiation, PBI undergoes photocyclization to generate an active photosensitizer (CBI) and a protonic acid in situ. This dual output synergistically amplifies reactive oxygen species (ROS) production within a confined lipid environment, promoting lipid peroxidation, GPX4 downregulation, and membrane destabilization. Consequently, pyroptosis is efficiently triggered alongside ferroptosis, leading to enhanced tumor cell killing and immune activation both in vitro and in vivo. By shifting the design paradigm from molecular optimization to cell membrane control, this work reframes the plasma membrane from a passive barrier into an active reaction platform, providing a general and modular strategy for programmable pyroptosis‐based photoimmunotherapy.

title: Synergistic Ethylene Glycol Synthesis via Photocatalytic CO2 Reduction Coupled With CH3OH Oxidation
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Paired photoredox catalysis enables co‐valorization of CO 2 and small molecules to high‐value chemicals via concurrent oxidation and reduction half‐reactions. However, most systems feature decoupled half‐reactions with no intrinsic substrate‐product interplay, merely utilizing electrons and holes separately, and failing to realize convergent chemical synthesis. Herein, we demonstrate a tandem photoredox‐photothermal catalytic system for efficient ethylene glycol (EG) synthesis, comprising (i) the photoredox catalysis of CO 2 reduction integrated with C─C coupling of methanol (CH 3 OH) to EG over Cu‐doped Zn 0.75 Cd 0.25 S catalysts, and (ii) the photothermal conversion of syngas to CH 3 OH over commercial CuZnAl catalysts. Of note, the CH 3 OH formed in situ via CO 2 reduction can feed into the pool of oxidation substrates, while the co‐generated syngas (ideal H 2 /CO ratio ≈ 2) is further converted to additional CH 3 OH and then recirculated as a supplemental oxidation substrate. Such a tandem catalytic design achieves high atom‐ and redox‐economy for EG synthesis, delivering an exceptional apparent quantum yield of 24.1%, outperforming those previously reported for CH 3 OH coupling to EG under an inert atmosphere. This work highlights the promise of orchestrating photoredox‐based closed‐loop catalytic architectures for value‐added C 2+ chemical synthesis with high efficiency and selectivity.

title: Desymmetrization of Acyclic meso‐1,3‐Diols by Cu─H‐Catalyzed Dehydrogenative Silylation
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT A nonenzymatic desymmetrization of acyclic meso ‐1,3‐diols by Si─O coupling with a hydrosilane is reported. The C s ‐symmetric diols undergo enantioselective monosilylation with a Cu─H/( R , R )‐Ph‐BPE catalyst system. The choice of hydrosilane was critical for suppressing undesired bissilylation, with a tertiary homobenzylic silane providing the best results. A series of simple alkyl‐substituted 1,3‐diols was converted into the corresponding silyl ethers with high enantiomeric ratios, with an unsubstituted methylene unit in the 2‐position identified as the most favorable scaffold for efficient and selective desymmetrization. Further modifications of the obtained enantioenriched products additionally emphasize the synthetic value of the reported methodology.

title: Beyond Lewis Acidity: Thiophilicity and Redox Stability as Design Principles for Sulphur‐Containing Polymerisation Catalysis
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Catalysts for the ring‐opening copolymerisation (ROCOP) of sulphur‐containing monomers are almost invariably inherited from all‐oxygen chemistry, where performance tracks the barrier of the rate‐determining propagation step. We show that this transfer fails. The activity of Cr(III), Co(III) and Zn(II) complexes of a common salicylimine scaffold cannot be explained by computationally tracking monomer insertions and metal activity is better predicted off‐cycle. A revised experimentally supported computational hypothesis implicates metal thiolates, generated by side‐reactions at the chain end, to deactivate the catalyst by either binding too tightly to or reducing the metal centre. The resulting computational descriptors, thiophilicity and redox stability, are distinct from Lewis acidity and chemical hardness, and predicted Al(III) to be competent. Al(III) catalysis delivers recyclable sulphur‐containing copolymers with a high apparent weight of M n = 238.6 kg/mol. This unlocks previously underexplored processing methods for these types of materials such as melt‐spinning and scCO 2 ‐foaming. Our results suggest new structure–activity design rules for sulphur‐containing polymerisation catalysis which are urgently required to obtain technologically useful materials.

title: Nitrogen‐Rich Covalent Organic Frameworks Enable Reversible Lithium Deposition in Anode‐Free Lithium Batteries
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Poor lithium reversibility and sluggish interfacial kinetics limit the areal capacity and rate capability of anode‐free lithium batteries. A nitrogen‐rich covalent organic framework (COF) as an interphase layer promotes uniform lithium deposition, enabling plating/stripping at 20 mAh/cm 2 in Li/Cu cells and anode‐free full‐cell operation at 4.1 mAh/cm 2 , as reported by Z. Ouyang, S. Zheng, S. Li, et al., Angewandte Chemie Novit 2 (2026): e70027.

title: Isolation of Open‐Shell Vinylidene Complexes of Iridium, Ruthenium, and Osmium
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Open‐shell vinylidene complexes are prone to undergo fast, ligand‐centered radical reactions. Herein, we describe the synthesis of paramagnetic Ir, Ru, and Os complexes with terminal N‐heterocyclic vinylidene ligands. Under inert conditions, these complexes remain stable over extended periods, allowing for isolation on a preparative scale and crystallographic analyses (for Ir and Ru). The results of computational investigations, EPR spectroscopic, and reactivity studies imply that the radical is largely localized on the vinylidene ligand.

title: Interaction Path Analysis and Privileged Learning Based Assessment of Oscillation Risk Contributions for Multiple Wind Farms with MMC-HVDC System
source: IEEE Transactions on Sustainable Energy
abstract: In wind farm (WF) transmission via modular multilevel converter-based high-voltage DC (MMC-HVDC) systems, the dominant oscillatory modes jointly established by multiple WFs and the MMC-HVDC may give rise to subsynchronous oscillations. Although the underlying mechanisms of such oscillations have been identified in prior studies, the complex interaction paths among WFs and the MMC-HVDC, as well as their impact on stability remain insufficiently elucidated. To bridge this gap, this paper develops an extended interaction path analysis method that explicitly characterizes the interaction paths between MMC-HVDC and each WF. On this basis, the mechanism through which these interactions drive unstable oscillation modes is theoretically analyzed. Furthermore, a quantitative interaction index is introduced to evaluate the interaction strength within critical frequency bands, thereby assessing the contribution of each WF to the oscillation instability risk. Moreover, a privileged-information-enhanced time-frequency network (PIETFNet) is proposed to predict the interaction index, serving as a monitoring tool for assessing vulnerable WFs during system operation. In PIETFNet, privileged frequency-domain information is distilled during training to enhance teacher network representation learning, enabling the student network to capture complex interaction dynamics using only time-domain inputs during deployment. Case studies verify the theoretical analysis of the interaction mechanism, demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed interaction index, and show that the student network achieves prediction accuracy close to that of the multimodal teacher while requiring only time-domain inputs.

title: From Tokens to Energy Flexibility: Quantization-Enabled Demand Response for Data Centers with LLM Inference Workloads
source: IEEE Transactions on Smart Grid
abstract: The rapid growth of large language model (LLM) inference is creating significant data-center loads that face increasing energy-management challenges under tightening grid conditions and demand response (DR) requirements. Conventional data-center energy management mainly relies on temporal and spatial workload shifting and campus-level energy asset scheduling, but it usually treats LLM inference demand as an aggregate load. As a result, these approaches fail to exploit the internal characteristics of LLM serving and therefore overlook the flexibility offered by LLM-specific techniques such as model quantization. To unlock this flexibility, this paper proposes a quantization-enabled energy management framework for grid-responsive LLM inference data centers. First, a quantization-to-power model is established to map each model--quantization configuration to a compact set of dispatchable parameters. Second, a two-stage quantization-enabled DR model is developed to account for model instance switching, request routing, and precision selection. Third, a multi-campus co-optimization method is introduced for DR participation by integrating grid-side electricity and carbon signals with the quantization-enabled DR model. Case studies show that the proposed framework reduces total data-center operating cost by 31.8% without curtailing served token volume, validating model quantization as an effective flexibility lever for grid-responsive LLM data-center energy management.

title: Observability and Parameter Estimation of a Generic Model for Aggregated Distributed Energy Resources
source: IEEE Transactions on Power Systems
abstract: We propose a novel framework for estimating the parameters of an aggregated distributed energy resources (DER A) model. First, we introduce a rigorous method to determine whether all model parameters are estimable. When they are not, our approach identifies the subset of parameters that can be estimated. The proposed framework offers new insights into the number and specific parameters that can be reliably estimated based on commonly available measurements. It also highlights the limitations of calibrating such models. Second, we introduce a Kalman filtering method to calibrate the DER A model. Since we account for nonlinear effects such as saturation and deadbands, we develop a specific mechanism to handle smoothing functions within the Kalman filter. Specifically, we consider the extended and the unscented Kalman filter. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework on a modified IEEE 34-node distribution feeder with inverter- based resources. Our findings align with the North American Electric Reliability Corporation's parameterization guideline and underscore the importance of model calibration in accurately capturing the collective dynamics of distributed energy resources installed on distribution systems.

title: Scalable Heterogeneous Graph Foundation-Model Workflows for Data-Driven Optimal Power Flow
source: IEEE Transactions on Smart Grid
abstract: Fast and reliable optimal power flow (OPF) approximation is important for power system operation, yet heterogeneous OPF graph models are often evaluated either with architecture-specific implementations or on limited training corpora. This paper presents a large-scale heterogeneous graph-learning workflow, built on HydraGNN, for data-driven OPF surrogate modeling and graph foundation-model (GFM) development. The workflow preserves buses, generators, loads, shunts, alternating-current (AC) lines, transformers, and device-to-bus relations and provides a common implementation for distributed preprocessing, multi-graphics-processing-unit (GPU) training, hyperparameter optimization (HPO), and downstream adaptation. Using approximately three million heterogeneous graphs from ten Power Grid Library for Benchmarking AC Optimal Power Flow Algorithms (PGLib-OPF) cases spanning 14 to 13,659 buses, we compare six heterogeneous graph neural network (GNN) families under a common HPO campaign on Frontier, resulting in two compact HeteroSAGE and HeteroHEAT models (~1.6-1.7 million parameters) that achieve the lowest observed validation MSE. Strong and weak scaling using up to 1,024 Frontier nodes show that 256 nodes (corresponding to 1,024 AMD MI250X GPUs) provides the best time-to-solution balance for the measured workload. Two downstream tasks evaluate task adaptation on the IEEE 118-bus case: a classification task to distinguish nominal operating conditions from artificially generated extreme-overload conditions and N-1 single-component-outage regression to predict bus voltage magnitude and phase angle. Partial fine-tuning provides the strongest balance between predictive performance and computational requirements.
